description: National CDL baseline checked against the AAMVA CDL manual (2025 CDL Testing System) and 49 CFR: air brakes, combination vehicles, pre-trip, cargo, and hours of service. State add-ons such as extra age rules are not in this file.

questions.q: The air compressor governor should cut out at about
options: 125 psi
45 psi
200 psi
60 psi
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor at about 125 psi, the normal cut-out pressure in the CDL manual.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The air compressor should cut back in at about
options: 20 psi
100 psi
150 psi
45 psi
questions.explanation: Cut-in pressure is about 100 psi. If it is much lower, the system needs service.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The low-air warning must come on before pressure falls below
options: 10 psi
125 psi
60 psi
20 psi
questions.explanation: The warning buzzer or light must activate before tank pressure drops below 60 psi.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Spring brakes typically come on fully when air pressure falls to
options: 100 psi exactly
They never come on from low air
125 to 135 psi
20 to 45 psi
questions.explanation: Spring brakes apply automatically in that range so a loss of air does not leave the truck without brakes.
questions.remember: Spring brakes on at 20 to 45 psi.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your straight truck or combination has working ABS on all axles. How may you make an emergency stop?
options: Fully apply the brakes, and steer
Use only the trailer hand valve
Set the parking brake while rolling
Shift to neutral and coast
questions.explanation: CDL manual 5.4.2: brake the same way with or without ABS. The one exception: "if you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop, you can fully apply the brakes."
questions.remember: ABS on all axles: brake fully, steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Stab braking, for a vehicle without ABS, means
options: A light steady pressure for the whole stop
Brake to lockup, release, then brake again
Use the parking brake only
Downshift and do not touch the brake
questions.explanation: Stab braking is for non-ABS emergency stops. If the vehicle has ABS, press and hold instead. Brake hard until the wheels lock, release to roll, then brake hard again.
questions.remember: Stab: brake hard, release, brake again.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Brake lag on an air-brake vehicle is
options: The time the governor waits to cut in
The gap in the glad hands
The delay while air flows to the brakes
A delay only on hydraulic brakes
questions.explanation: Air brakes do not apply instantly. At highway speed that extra half-second or more is a long distance. The time air takes to flow through the lines after you press the pedal, added to your stopping distance.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why should you not fan the air brakes on a long downgrade?
options: Fanning is required by ABS
Fanning cools the drums better than snubbing
Fanning builds extra pressure
It can use air faster than you replace it
questions.explanation: Use a low gear and snub braking so pressure stays up and the brakes do not fade. Fanning releases and reapplies the brakes and can use more air than you can replace.
questions.why: Fanning the pedal can let air out faster than the compressor replaces it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Snub braking on a downgrade means
options: Brake 5 mph below safe speed, then release
Use only the trailer hand valve
Shift to neutral
Riding the brakes the whole way down
questions.explanation: Snubbing lets the brakes cool between applications. Pick a safe speed, often a gear lower than you used to climb. Apply the brakes firmly enough to slow about 5 mph below your safe speed, release, and repeat.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A dual air-brake system has
options: One tank for the whole truck
Two separate air systems
No spring brakes
Hydraulic fluid in both circuits
questions.explanation: Primary and secondary circuits are protected by check valves. You can still stop if one circuit fails, but get the truck repaired. Two separate systems so a single failure does not drain every brake.
questions.remember: Dual air: two systems, one set of controls.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Glad hands connect
options: The cargo straps
The fifth wheel jaws
The trailer air lines
The steering column
questions.explanation: The service line is usually blue. The emergency or supply line is usually red. The service and emergency air lines between the tractor and the trailer.
questions.remember: Glad hands connect the trailer air lines.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The red octagonal knob in the cab is
options: The dimmer switch
The jake-brake switch only
The fifth-wheel release
The trailer air supply
questions.explanation: Pulling the trailer-air-supply knob out dumps trailer air and applies the trailer spring brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The yellow diamond knob is
options: The parking-brake control
The trailer height valve
A cargo-lamp switch
The air-dryer purge
questions.explanation: The yellow parking-brake valve applies the tractor spring brakes when you pull it out.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the brakes released, air leakage in a combination vehicle should be less than
options: 10 psi per minute
3 psi per minute
20 psi per minute
There is no limit
questions.explanation: The CDL manual's static leakage test allows no more than 2 psi per minute for a single vehicle and 3 psi per minute for a combination, brakes released.
questions.remember: Released leak, combination: under 3 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the brakes applied, leakage in a combination vehicle should be less than
options: 1 psi per hour
25 psi per minute
4 psi per minute
15 psi per minute
questions.explanation: Applied-brake leakage should not exceed 3 psi per minute for a single vehicle or 4 psi per minute for a combination.
questions.remember: Applied leak, combination: under 4 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Slack adjusters tell you
options: Fifth-wheel height
Tire pressure
Engine oil level
Brake adjustment
questions.explanation: If pushrod travel is longer than the limit for that brake chamber, the brake is out of adjustment and must be fixed before you drive.
questions.remember: Slack adjuster moves too far? Adjust it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You drain air tanks because
options: Water and oil collect and can freeze
The governor requires an empty tank
ABS needs water in the lines
Air is lighter when it is dry
questions.explanation: Drain tanks daily, or use the air dryer, so moisture does not freeze in cold weather. Compressed air leaves water and oil that can freeze or damage valves.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Brake fade on a long hill is caused by
options: Cold drums
Heat that makes the linings less effective
Too much air pressure
A high gear only when the truck is empty
questions.explanation: Riding the brakes builds heat. Use a low gear and snub so the brakes can cool.
questions.why: Overusing the service brakes overheats them and causes fade.
questions.remember: Long grade: let the engine brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before you back under a trailer you should
options: Keep the landing gear fully raised
Back under at a sharp angle
Check trailer height and line up straight
Leave the trailer air lines connected to another truck
questions.explanation: A bad angle can damage the trailer nose or miss the kingpin. The fifth wheel should just contact the trailer, then you back slowly. Check trailer height, chock the wheels if needed, and align the tractor so the fifth wheel meets the kingpin straight.
questions.remember: Trailer slightly low: the tractor lifts it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After coupling you confirm the lock by
options: Listening for a click only
Raising the landing gear first and hoping
Pulling the trailer with the landing gear still down
Seeing the jaws closed on the kingpin shank
questions.explanation: A visual check plus a tug test against the locked kingpin is required. Do not rely on the sound of the latch. Looking to see that the jaws are closed around the shank of the kingpin, the release arm is seated, and there is no gap between the fifth wheel and the trailer.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer landing gear must be
options: Fully raised, handle secured
Removed
Set on the drive tires
Left partly down so it drags
questions.explanation: Landing gear that is down, or a crank that swings, will hit the road or the tractor. Fully raised and the crank handle secured before you move.
questions.remember: Landing gear all the way up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Offtracking means
options: The trailer is longer than the law allows
Trailer tires take a shorter path in turns
The truck pulls to the left only when empty
The engine brake is on
questions.explanation: The rear of the trailer cuts the corner. Turn wide enough on the right that the trailer stays off the curb and other vehicles. The trailer tires follow a shorter path than the tractor tires in a turn.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A quick lane change in a combination vehicle can
options: Set the spring brakes
Shorten the trailer
Roll the rear trailer
Improve fuel economy
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification is strongest in doubles and triples. Steer smoothly. Amplify into a crack-the-whip and roll the rear trailer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A lightly loaded or empty trailer
options: Does not need brakes
Cannot jackknife
Always stops shorter and is more stable
Can lock its wheels more easily
questions.explanation: Light weight means the trailer brakes can lock. A locked trailer pushes the tractor into a jackknife. It has less weight on the tires.
questions.why: An empty trailer's stiff springs and strong brakes give poor traction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: If the trailer starts to skid sideways you should
options: Release the brakes to regain traction
Accelerate in a curve
Steer away from the skid and hold the brake
Apply the trailer brake harder
questions.explanation: Rolling tires can grip. Locked trailer wheels will keep sliding and can jackknife the combination. Release the brakes so the wheels can roll and regain traction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A tractor jackknife starts when
options: The trailer wheels lock and the tractor stays straight
The drive wheels lock and the tractor swings around toward the trailer
The landing gear drops
The glad hands separate
questions.explanation: Release the brake so the drive wheels roll, and steer to straighten. Do not use the trailer hand valve as a parking brake.
questions.why: A drive-wheel skid can let the trailer push the tractor into a jackknife.
questions.remember: Drive wheels locked? Release the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The rear trailer in a set of doubles is
options: Required to have no brakes
The most stable trailer in a sudden swerve
The most likely to roll over in a swerve
Unaffected by rearward amplification
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification hits the last trailer hardest. Avoid sudden steering. The trailer most likely to roll over first in a sudden swerve.
questions.why: The rear trailer is the most likely to turn over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You inspect the coupling from the rear of the tractor and you want to see
options: The kingpin sitting on top of the jaws
The release arm hanging free
Daylight between the fifth wheel and the trailer apron
No gap at the fifth wheel and locked jaws
questions.explanation: A gap means the trailer is not fully down on the fifth wheel. The jaws must close on the shank, not the head. No daylight between the upper and lower fifth wheel, and the jaws locked on the kingpin shank.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During a pre-trip you reject a tire if
options: It has a deep cut, bulge, or exposed fabric
The valve cap is present
The tire is the size listed on the vehicle
The tread looks even and the pressure matches the sidewall
questions.explanation: A damaged tire or duals that rub can fail on the road. Check pressure with a gauge, not a kick. You see a deep cut, a bulge, fabric showing, or dual tires that are touching.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Rust streaks from a wheel nut often mean
options: The nut was painted
The nut is loose
The tire is overinflated
The axle is new
questions.explanation: A loose lug nut leaves a trail of rust or shiny metal. Tighten and recheck before you drive.
questions.remember: Rust at a lug nut? Check it's tight.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Emergency equipment you should confirm before a trip includes
options: Nothing if the truck is new
A spare fifth wheel only
Extinguisher, triangles, and fuses
A case of oil only
questions.explanation: The CDL inspection test expects you to know where the extinguisher, triangles, and fuses are and that they are serviceable. Charged fire extinguisher, warning triangles, and spare electrical fuses if the truck uses them.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Steering-wheel free play that is excessive means
options: The air dryer is full
The trailer is too light
The truck is normal
Steering wear to repair
questions.explanation: Too much play delays your steering. Do not start a trip with loose steering. The steering has wear and should be repaired before the trip.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You check lights and reflectors because
options: Others must see you and your signals
They replace mirrors
ABS does not work without a clearance light
They are optional at night
questions.explanation: Walk around and confirm headlights, signals, brake lights, and required reflectors work. Other drivers and enforcement need to see your vehicle and your signals.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The heaviest part of a cargo load should sit
options: As high as possible
Low and centered, blocked in place
All the way at the rear doors
On one side so the truck leans
questions.explanation: A high or rear-heavy load increases rollover and can unload the steering axle. Low, and centered or slightly forward of the trailer's center, blocked so it cannot slide.
questions.why: Cargo piled high makes you more likely to tip over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Too little weight on the steering axle makes the truck
options: Exempt from bridge laws
Easier to steer at all speeds
Hard to steer and more likely to wander
Unable to use the service brakes
questions.explanation: The front axle needs enough weight to steer. Too much weight on the front is also unsafe. Balance the load.
questions.why: Too little weight on the front axle makes steering unsafe.
questions.remember: Too light up front: hard to steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Federal cargo-securement checks include an inspection
options: Only if a strap looks new
Only for hazmat
Only at the destination
Before and during the trip
questions.explanation: 49 CFR 392.9 requires those inspections so a shift in the load is caught early. A sealed trailer still gets the checks you can make. Before you drive, again within the first 50 miles, and then every 3 hours or 150 miles, and at a change of duty status.
questions.remember: Check the load early in the trip.

questions.q: Cargo that can blow or fall off must be
options: Covered or contained so nothing escapes
Stacked above the side rails without tiedowns
Held by gravity only
Left loose so it can shift into a better position
questions.explanation: Loose cargo is a hazard to you and to traffic behind you. Use the tiedowns and tarps the cargo requires.
questions.remember: Nothing leaks, spills, blows or falls.

questions.q: The CDL following-distance rule of thumb for a truck under 40 mph is
options: One second total
One second per 10 feet of length
Half a second per 10 feet
The same two seconds a car uses
questions.explanation: A 60-foot truck needs at least 6 seconds under 40 mph. Above 40 mph, add another second. At least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length.
questions.remember: A second per 10 feet of length.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Above 40 mph, the truck following gap should be
options: One car length
Whatever the car behind you leaves
The under-40 formula with one extra second
Shorter, because traffic is smoother
questions.explanation: Speed increases stopping distance faster than the basic formula. Add at least one second over 40 mph.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A posted bridge clearance is
options: Always two feet higher than it says
Only for the trailer
A suggestion for cars
The limit for your highest point
questions.explanation: Know your height, including anything on top. Hitting a bridge is a preventable crash. If you are not sure you fit, stop and check.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You should not use an engine brake on a slick road because
options: It can lock the drive wheels and start a skid
It drains the air tanks
It is illegal in every state at all times
It only works in high gear
questions.explanation: An engine retarder on ice or rain can break traction at the drive axles. Some cities also post bans; obey those signs.
questions.why: A retarder on a slick road can make the drive wheels skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before you cross railroad tracks in a truck you must be sure
options: The trailer will fit if you stop on the tracks and wait
You can clear the entire combination past the tracks without stopping
The gate will lift if you edge forward
First gear is not needed
questions.explanation: Never stop on the tracks. Some vehicles must stop 15 to 50 feet before the crossing. A train cannot swerve.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A truck is more likely to roll over when
options: The tanks are drained
The load is low and centered and you steer gently
It is top-heavy and takes a curve too fast
You are in a straight line at a steady speed
questions.explanation: Slow before the curve. Ramps and roundabouts are common rollover sites for trucks. The center of gravity is high and you enter a curve or ramp too fast.
questions.why: High trucks can roll over even at the posted curve speed.
questions.remember: Top-heavy? Slower than the curve sign.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: What does the CDL manual say about stopping a bobtail tractor?
options: Its spring brakes will not apply
It stops shorter than any loaded rig
It has no working brakes
It can be very hard to stop smoothly
questions.explanation: CDL manual 6.1.3: "Tests have shown that bobtails can be very hard to stop smoothly. It takes them longer to stop than a tractor-semitrailer loaded to maximum gross weight."

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A property-carrying driver may drive a maximum of
options: 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty
8 hours in any 24
As long as the 70-hour clock remains, with no daily limit
14 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty
questions.explanation: The 11-hour driving limit sits inside the 14-hour window. Both restart after 10 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.q: The 14-hour limit means
options: You may drive during all 14 hours
No driving past 14 hours after your 10-hour break
The clock pauses for all on-duty time that is not driving
It applies only to buses
questions.explanation: Off-duty breaks inside the day do not extend the 14-hour window, except for the specific split-sleeper options in the rule. You may not drive after the 14th hour from the end of your last 10-hour break, even if you took short breaks inside the window.

questions.q: After 8 cumulative hours of driving, a property-carrying driver must
options: Only log the break if hauling passengers
Keep driving if the 11-hour clock remains
Take a 30-minute break before driving again
Take 10 hours off immediately
questions.explanation: The break can be off duty, sleeper berth, or on-duty not driving. It is required before more driving time.

questions.q: The weekly on-duty limits for a property-carrying driver are
options: 80 hours in 7 days
No weekly limit if you take a 30-minute break
40 hours in 5 days
60 hours in 7 days or 70 in 8 days
questions.explanation: A 34-hour restart can reset the 60- or 70-hour clock when it is used as the rule allows. 60 hours in 7 days, or 70 hours in 8 days if the carrier runs every day.

questions.q: Ten consecutive hours off duty
options: Resets the 11-hour and 14-hour clocks
Is optional if you feel alert
Replaces the need to log
Resets only the 30-minute break
questions.explanation: You need 10 consecutive hours off, or the equivalent split sleeper period, before a new driving window.

questions.q: You test the parking brake before you move by
options: Draining the air tanks while rolling
Skipping it if the gauge reads 100 psi
Gently pulling against it in a low gear
Driving to highway speed and then pulling the yellow knob
questions.explanation: A parking brake that does not hold will not hold on a hill. Test it gently, then release it before you drive. Putting the truck in gear with the parking brake set, at a low idle, to confirm it holds.
questions.remember: Test the parking brake: low gear, gentle pull.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The air pressure gauges in the cab show
options: Engine oil pressure only
Trailer height
Only outside temperature
Air pressure in the tanks
questions.explanation: Watch the supply gauge. Do not drive if pressure will not build to cut-out or if it leaks down. How much pressure is in the tanks, and sometimes how much you are applying.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer hand valve should be used
options: Only to test the trailer brakes
Instead of the foot valve on long grades
To apply the tractor spring brakes
To park the trailer overnight
questions.explanation: The hand valve is a test tool. Parking is done with the tractor and trailer parking controls so the spring brakes hold.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: On a curve or an exit ramp you should
options: Brake hard in the middle of the curve
Slow before it, then accelerate gently out
Use the posted highway speed if the ramp sign is yellow
Shift to neutral
questions.explanation: A yellow ramp speed is an advisory. Trucks with a high load need less than that speed. Slow to a safe speed before the curve, then accelerate gently as you leave it.
questions.remember: Slow and downshift before the curve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A tanker or a partially loaded liquid tank can surprise you because
options: Baffles remove all surge
Liquid does not move
Liquid surge can push the truck
Surge only happens when the tank is completely full
questions.explanation: Smooth bore tanks surge the most. Leave extra space and brake earlier. A full tankers endorsement covers the rest of those rules. Liquid surge pushes the vehicle forward or sideways after you stop or turn.
questions.why: Liquid moving in a part-full tank pushes the truck.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An air leak you can hear, or a hose that is cut or swollen, means
options: Tape it and go
It is normal at cut-out pressure
Drive slowly and check it at the next shop in a few days
Do not start the trip until it is repaired
questions.explanation: Air leaks become brake failures. Out-of-service defects stay parked.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Total stopping distance for an air-brake truck is
options: Perception, reaction, brake lag, and braking
The same as a passenger car
Only brake lag
Only the distance the brakes take to grab
questions.explanation: Air brakes add a lag distance that hydraulic brakes do not have. Speed multiplies every part of the stop. Perception distance plus reaction distance plus brake-lag distance plus braking distance.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: If you double your speed, the braking portion of stopping distance is about
options: Twice as long
Four times as long
Ten times as long
The same
questions.explanation: Braking distance grows with the square of speed. Doubling speed makes the braking distance about four times longer, before you add lag.
questions.remember: Double the speed: braking distance times four.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The minimum tread depth on a steering-axle tire is
options: 8/32 inch
2/32 inch
4/32 inch
1/32 inch
questions.explanation: Steering-axle tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires on the vehicle need at least 2/32 inch.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Other tires on a truck, besides the steering axle, need at least
options: No measurable tread if the cords are hidden
1 inch of tread
4/32 inch of tread
2/32 inch of tread
questions.explanation: The CDL manual uses 4/32 inch on the steering axle and 2/32 inch on the other tires.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Warning triangles on a divided highway are placed
options: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind the vehicle
In the travel lane beside the driver door only
One mile ahead
Only in the cab
questions.explanation: On a one-way or divided road, all three devices go behind the vehicle toward approaching traffic.
questions.remember: Divided road: triangles behind you only.

questions.q: Warning triangles on an undivided two-way road are placed
options: All three within 50 feet in front
10 and 100 feet behind, 100 feet ahead
Only the hazard lights
One on the roof, two behind
questions.explanation: Two-way traffic needs a device ahead of the truck as well as two behind it. 10 feet and 100 feet behind the vehicle, and 100 feet in front.
questions.remember: Two-way road: triangles behind and ahead.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A federal rule for CDL drivers and alcohol is
options: 0.10 is the commercial limit
A 0.08 limit and no other restriction
No alcohol within 4 hours; never at 0.04 or more
Alcohol is unrestricted off duty the same day
questions.explanation: The commercial limit is lower than the typical passenger-car limit, and the 4-hour rule applies before duty. Do not consume alcohol within 4 hours of going on duty, and do not operate a commercial vehicle at 0.04 or more.
questions.remember: No alcohol within 4 hours of duty.

questions.q: Using a hand-held phone to text while driving a commercial vehicle is
options: Required for dispatch
Allowed on the freeway only
Allowed if traffic is light
Prohibited by federal rule
questions.explanation: Texting and hand-held phone use while driving a CMV are federal violations, not just a state preference.

questions.q: If the brakes fade on a downgrade and an escape ramp is ahead, you should
options: Use the ramp
Turn around on the ramp
Park on the ramp to check the load
Pass the ramp and look for a flatter road
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are for brake failure. Take one rather than ride failed brakes into traffic. It is there to stop a truck whose brakes have failed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The safest gear for a long downgrade is
options: Neutral, so the wheels roll freely
A lower gear, chosen before the grade
The highest gear, to save the brakes
Whatever gear you are in when the hill starts
questions.explanation: Select the gear before the downgrade. You will not be able to shift down once the truck is rolling fast. A gear lower than the one you would use to climb the hill, chosen before the grade.
questions.remember: Downgrade: a lower gear than you climbed in.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You must check that the trailer electrical cord is
options: Connected only after the first 50 miles
Optional at night
Connected, with lights and brakes working
Left unplugged so it cannot drag
questions.explanation: No lights on the trailer means you are invisible from behind and the ABS or brake circuit may be dead. Connected and the trailer lights and brakes respond before you move.
questions.remember: Cord plugged in, safety catch on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A fifth wheel that has no grease, or jaws that will not lock, means
options: Drive under 20 mph
Grease is only for the kingpin head
A normal dry coupling
Do not move until it is repaired
questions.explanation: An unlocked or dry fifth wheel can drop a trailer or wear through the plate. Do not move the combination until it is repaired and locks.
questions.why: A dry fifth wheel plate can cause steering trouble from friction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: How many tiedowns does a 10-foot cargo piece generally need, if it is not blocked against forward movement?
options: At least two
One, regardless of length
One for every 20 feet
None if it is heavy
questions.explanation: Cargo not blocked forward needs two tiedowns up to 10 feet long, plus one for each additional 10 feet or fraction. Only a piece of 5 feet or less that weighs 1,100 pounds or less can use one.

questions.q: A 34-hour restart is used to
options: Extend the 14-hour window by 34 hours
Reset the 60- or 70-hour cycle
Replace the 30-minute break
Avoid logging
questions.explanation: Thirty-four consecutive hours off duty can restart the weekly clock. It does not add driving time inside a 14-hour window. Reset the 60-hour or 70-hour on-duty cycle when the rule allows it.

questions.q: If you are cut off by a car that then slows down, a truck driver should
options: Brake-check the car
Close the gap so the car moves
Drop back and rebuild the gap
Flash high beams and pass on the shoulder
questions.explanation: You cannot stop as fast as the car. Take the space back instead of riding the bumper. Drop back and rebuild the following distance the truck needs.
questions.remember: Cut off? Drop back and make room.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: In the pre-trip check, air pressure does not build up fast enough. What does the manual tell you to do?
options: Drain the tanks while driving
Leave if the ABS light is off
Leave if the governor seems set correctly
Do not drive until it is fixed
questions.explanation: CDL manual 5.3.3: "If air pressure does not build up fast enough, your pressure may drop too low during driving, requiring an emergency stop. Don't drive until you get the problem fixed."
questions.why: Air that builds too slowly can drop too low while driving.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Converter dollies and the second trailer of a set of doubles must be checked for
options: Locked couplings, chains, and lines
A single glad hand
Landing gear that stays down
Paint color only
questions.explanation: Every coupling in the combination can separate. Check each one the same way you check the first. Locked pintle or fifth-wheel connections, safety chains or cables, and air and electric lines.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You measure pushrod travel on a parking-brake application or with a brake tool because
options: ABS replaces the need to measure
A short stroke always means the brake is failed
Too long a stroke means poor adjustment
The color of the chamber is the limit
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes are an out-of-service item. Do not guess from the cab. A stroke longer than the limit for that chamber means the brake is out of adjustment.
questions.remember: Pushrod past the limit? Something's wrong.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: On a typical dual-air tractor at operating rpm, pressure has not climbed from about 85 to 100 psi after 45 seconds. What should you do?
options: Idle in high gear until the safety valve seals the leak
Do not start the trip until the system can build pressure in that time
Leave if the warning buzzer is still quiet
Open a tank drain so the gauge needle jumps
questions.explanation: A dual system that cannot rise from about 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds at operating rpm is not building air fast enough for repeated stops. Park it and have the compressor, belts, and leaks repaired.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Both needles on your dual-air gauges are still short of 100 psi after a cold start. When may you move the truck?
options: When the parking valve will stay in even if one tank is empty
After the alcohol evaporator has been filled with water
Only after both the primary and secondary systems are at least about 100 psi
As soon as the primary gauge alone passes 60 psi
questions.explanation: A dual-air vehicle needs usable air in both circuits. The manual expects both systems to be at least about 100 psi before you drive. One healthy gauge does not cover a circuit that is still empty.
questions.remember: Wait for 100 psi in both systems.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The compressor unloads and the gauges hold steady near 125 psi. How do you treat that pressure?
options: Bleed the tanks down to 60 psi before you release the parking brake
Cap the line
Assume the low-air warning has stuck open
Treat it as normal governor cut-out, near 125 psi
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor at about 125 psi. That unload is cut-out, not a failed safety valve and not a signal to drain the tanks before every move.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After the gauges settle near cut-out, pumping the pedal brings the compressor back as pressure nears 100 psi. What does that restart mean?
options: The governor cut back in at about the normal 100 psi point
The safety valve is dumping and the compressor is chasing the leak
Cut-in is supposed to wait until the springs have already applied
The wet tank is full of oil and the governor is confused
questions.explanation: Cut-in near 100 psi is how the governor keeps a reserve. A restart far below that, or a compressor that never restarts, means the governor needs service.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your governor does not cut back in until tank pressure is far below 100 psi. What is the right call before a loaded run?
options: Pour water into the supply tank to raise cut-in
Have the governor serviced
Prefer the late cut-in
Set the warning buzzer to the same low number and go
questions.explanation: Normal cut-in is about 100 psi. If the compressor waits until pressure is much lower, you can run out of air between applications. That is a maintenance defect, not a fuel-saving setting.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the key on and the engine off, you fan the pedal and the low-air warning is still silent at 55 psi. Is the truck legal to leave?
options: Yes, because the warning is only required under 20 psi
Yes, once you tape the buzzer so it cannot sound in town
No. The warning must come on before pressure falls below 60 psi
Yes, if the springs have not popped out yet
questions.explanation: The low-air device is your last clear notice before the springs start to apply. If it is still quiet below 60 psi, the warning is defective and the truck stays parked.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: While you are on a freeway the low-air light and buzzer come on with the gauges still above 60 psi. What do you do next?
options: Speed up so you reach the consignee before the springs apply
Fan the pedal lightly to reset the warning
Pull only the trailer hand valve and ignore the gauges
Get off the road safely and do not keep driving on a failing air system
questions.explanation: A warning that comes on in motion means air is being lost or a circuit has failed. Stopping distance is no longer trustworthy. Park it. Do not try to finish the run on the remaining air.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You fan the brakes with the engine shut down and the yellow and red valves pop out on their own near 35 psi. What just happened?
options: The spring brakes applied, which is normal
The governor cut out early and dumped the trailer
The safety valve opened
The service relay stuck and only the blue glad hand closed
questions.explanation: Spring brakes are held off by air. Somewhere between 20 and 45 psi they apply by themselves so a pressure loss does not leave you with no parking brake. A pop-out near 35 psi is that design working. The spring brakes applied automatically inside the normal 20-to-45 psi range.
questions.remember: Valves pop out at 20 to 45 psi.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A helper says to fan the pedal all the way down a long grade until the spring brakes grab and then ride them. Why refuse?
options: The springs only work above cut-out and cannot apply on a hill
Spring brakes are for parking and air-loss emergencies
Spring brakes release themselves as soon as air pressure falls
Fanning is required so the drums stay cool on a descent
questions.explanation: Air holds spring brakes off. They come on hard when pressure is gone, and they are not a modulated service brake. Using them to descend overheats and can lock wheels. Choose a low gear and snub with the foot valve instead. For snubbing a grade.
questions.remember: Lose air, spring brakes come on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The safety valve on the supply tank suddenly discharges air. What should you conclude?
options: Plug the valve so the compressor can build a higher reserve
The discharge is the low-air warning and is normal above 60 psi
Pressure reached about 150 psi and the charging system needs service
The valve should vent every time the governor cuts in near 100 psi
questions.explanation: The safety valve is a last resort near 150 psi when the governor fails to cut out. If it opens, do not cap it and do not keep driving. The compressor or governor has to be repaired.
questions.remember: Safety valve hissing? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Cut-out never comes. Pressure keeps climbing and the safety valve has already hissed once. What is the safe choice?
options: Keep the engine at idle so the extra pressure shortens stops
Drain only the secondary tank and leave the governor alone
Tie the safety valve closed for the rest of the week
Shut down and get the governor repaired before another trip
questions.explanation: If the governor will not unload, pressure will keep rising until the safety valve dumps air near 150 psi. That is a failed control, not extra braking power. The truck needs service.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are about to time a static leak test. The tanks are full and the engine is off. What else has to be true?
options: Chock, release the parking brakes, let gauges settle
Leave the yellow valve out so the springs hide any leak
Hold the foot valve to the floor for the whole static test
Keep the engine at operating rpm so the compressor covers small leaks
questions.explanation: The released-brake test measures leakage while the springs are held off, so the truck can roll. Chock first, engine off, parking brakes released. Time the drop only after the needles stop moving from the release itself. Chock the wheels, release the parking brakes, and let the gauges settle before you time one minute.
questions.remember: Leak test: engine off, chocks, brake released.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: On a single-unit air-brake truck, brakes released and engine off, the gauge falls 5 psi in one minute. What does that mean?
options: Add shop air through the glad hands and the reading no longer counts
That leak is over the 2 psi per minute limit, so do not start the trip
Five psi is acceptable
Any drop under 10 psi is normal compressor cooling
questions.explanation: With the brakes released, a single vehicle may lose no more than 2 psi in one minute. A combination may lose no more than 3. Five psi is too much on either. Find the leak.
questions.remember: Released leak, single: under 2 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your tractor-trailer, brakes released, loses 3 psi in a timed minute. How do you score that static test?
options: Released-brake leakage has no limit if the applied test will pass
Three psi means the safety valve is set 3 psi low
It does not pass; the loss must be less than 3 psi
It passes, because combinations may lose up to 5 psi
questions.explanation: CDL manual 5.3.3: with the brakes released, the loss rate "should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles and less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles." A 3 psi loss is not less than 3.
questions.remember: Leak test: less than the limit, not equal.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the foot brake held fully applied, a straight truck loses 6 psi in one minute. What is wrong with leaving?
options: The applied limit is 4 psi for every vehicle, so 6 psi is close enough
Holding the pedal always dumps 6 psi as the chambers fill
An applied test is only for trailers
Applied leakage on a single vehicle may not exceed 3 psi per minute
questions.explanation: Full service application pressurizes the lines and chambers. A single vehicle may then lose no more than 3 psi in one minute. Six psi means a leak under load. Park the truck.
questions.remember: Applied leak, single: under 3 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You hold a full service application on a combination for one minute and lose 4 psi. Is that over the limit?
options: No. A combination may lose up to 4 psi per minute with the service brakes applied
Yes. Every combination is limited to 2 psi once the pedal is down
Yes. Applied leakage must be zero or the glad hands are crossed
No. Applied leakage is unlimited if the static test was under 3 psi
questions.explanation: With the brakes fully applied, the manual allows no more than 3 psi per minute on a single vehicle and no more than 4 psi per minute on a combination. Four psi on a combination meets that limit.
questions.remember: Applied leak, combination: under 4 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A combination loses 7 psi in one minute while you hold the foot brake down. What should happen to the trip?
options: Reset the test by shifting into neutral and ignoring the drop
Cancel it. Applied leakage above 4 psi per minute on a combination is too much
Go if the loss stops once you release the pedal
Go if most of the loss is on the trailer gauge only
questions.explanation: The applied test is where diaphragm, hose, and valve leaks show up. More than 4 psi in one minute on a combination, or more than 3 on a single vehicle, means you do not have a dependable reserve.
questions.remember: Applied leak, combination: under 4 psi a minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During the released-brake minute, pressure drops 2 psi on your straight truck. What is the correct reading of that result?
options: Two psi passes with room to spare
Any loss with the brakes released means the governor is stuck
It does not pass; a single vehicle must lose less than 2 psi
It passes, because the released limit is 4 psi for all trucks
questions.explanation: CDL manual 5.3.3: with the brakes released, the loss rate "should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles". A 2 psi loss is not less than 2.
questions.remember: Leak test: less than the limit, not equal.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Blue and red glad hands are sitting in your hands at the trailer nose. Which pairing is correct?
options: Blue to the emergency supply and red to the service signal
Either color on either trailer fitting if the seals look clean
Both hoses on the trailer service fitting so the emergency line stays capped
Blue to the service line and red to the emergency line, colors matched
questions.explanation: Blue is the service signal that applies the trailer brakes with the foot valve. Red is the emergency supply that charges the trailer and holds its spring brakes off. Crossed colors will not give you a normal trailer brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The glad hands are locked, but the trailer air gauge never rises and the trailer brakes will not release. What do you do?
options: Do not move until the trailer actually has air and the brakes release normally
Drag the trailer a short distance so the shoes knock free
Push the yellow parking valve only and leave the red valve out
Open the trailer tank drains while you roll so the lines dry out
questions.explanation: Matching colors is not enough if air is not reaching the trailer. A closed shutoff, a bad seal, a kink, or a leak can leave the springs applied. Moving against dragging trailer brakes overheats them and means you have no trailer reserve.
questions.remember: Air won't build? Check for crossed lines.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You notice the red hose is on the trailer service fitting and the blue hose is on the emergency fitting. What is the risk if you leave them that way?
options: The compressor will cut out 25 psi higher to compensate
The trailer will not charge and brake as designed
The only effect is a wrong-colored lamp on the dash
Crossed hoses make the trailer brakes stronger in a panic stop
questions.explanation: The emergency line supplies and releases the trailer spring brakes. The service line carries the application signal. Swapping them mixes those jobs. Rematch the colors before anyone moves the combination. The trailer will not charge and apply the way the foot valve and spring brakes are designed.
questions.why: Crossed lines send supply air to the service line, so the trailer tanks don't fill.
questions.remember: Red to red, blue to blue.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You push the red octagonal knob in and hear air rush back to the trailer. What did that control just do?
options: It turned on the trailer-only hand valve for the rest of the trip
It opened the safety valve to test cut-out
Opened trailer air so its tanks can charge
It applied the tractor parking brakes and dumped the tractor tanks
questions.explanation: The red octagon is the trailer air supply. In supplies the trailer. Out dumps trailer air so the trailer spring brakes apply. Confirm that pressure recovers and the trailer brakes actually release before you roll.
questions.remember: Red knob in: trailer gets air.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You pull the red octagonal knob out to park a coupled trailer. What should the trailer do?
options: Keep its tanks full and release the springs for a faster pull-away
Apply only the tractor drive-axle service brakes
Charge the blue service line and leave the springs held off
Lose its air supply so the trailer spring brakes come on
questions.explanation: Pulling the red valve out cuts the trailer supply and the trailer spring brakes apply. That is how you set the trailer brakes, not by leaving the hand valve on or by hoping the glad hands stay sealed.
questions.remember: Red knob out: trailer brakes on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The yellow diamond knob is pulled out and the tractor will not roll. What is holding it?
options: The tractor parking brake, which applied the tractor spring brakes
The trailer service signal
The governor, which cut out and locked the driveline
The secondary tank drain
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond is the parking-brake valve. Out applies the tractor spring brakes. In lets air hold those springs off, but only after you have enough pressure. It is not the trailer supply and not the trolley valve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Pressure is still low and the yellow parking valve will not stay in. Why should you stop forcing it?
options: Low air is fixed by pushing the valve in harder than the spring
There is not enough air to hold the spring brakes off, and they should stay applied
The valve only stays in after the safety valve has opened
A wooden wedge in the button is the approved way to release the springs
questions.explanation: Spring brakes stay on until air pressure is high enough to hold them off. If the yellow valve will not stay in, you do not have that pressure. Forcing or tying it in defeats the fail-safe.
questions.remember: Lose air, spring brakes come on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The red trailer-supply valve pops back out by itself while you are trying to charge a newly coupled trailer. What is the likely meaning?
options: The blue glad hand has sealed
Pop-out means the trailer ABS finished its bulb check
Pressure is too low or air is escaping faster than the compressor can replace it
The trailer tanks are full and the valve pops out at normal cut-out
questions.explanation: The red valve should stay in once the system has normal pressure and the lines are tight. If it pops back out, you are losing air or you never built enough to hold the springs off. Do not tie it in and leave.
questions.remember: Valve pops out? Air is too low.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A city street is tight and you want a very smooth stop from highway speed. Why is there still a delay after your foot moves?
options: The governor waits to cut in before any chamber gets air
Hydraulic fluid in a truck has the same air-flow lag as a car
Lag is only the time the low-air buzzer needs to warm up
Air has to flow through the lines and valves before the shoes work
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance is perception plus reaction plus brake lag plus braking distance. Cars with hydraulic brakes do not wait for air to travel the lines. That lag is real distance at highway speed, so you need more room than the car ahead seems to have.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You compare your air-brake tractor to the hydraulic car you drove to work. Which difference matters in a panic stop?
options: The truck has brake lag; the car does not
The car has more brake lag
Air brakes apply the shoes before the pedal moves
Lag disappears once tank pressure is above 60 psi
questions.explanation: Air-brake lag is the time between pedal movement and air reaching the chambers. Hydraulic brakes do not have that air-travel delay. Add lag to perception, reaction, and the actual braking distance when you judge a gap. The truck adds brake lag while air moves through the system, and the car does not have that same lag.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An emergency stop is straight ahead in a truck that does not have ABS. How do you stab-brake?
options: Pump in short taps so the wheels stay locked the whole time
Apply fully until the wheels lock, release so they roll, then apply fully again
Squeeze lightly and never let the shoes reach the drum
Hold the parking valve out and steer with the foot off the pedal
questions.explanation: Stab braking is for a non-ABS emergency stop. Locked wheels give up steering and, on a combination, can start a skid. Releasing lets the tires roll and grip, then you apply hard again. If the truck has ABS, do not stab.
questions.remember: Stab: brake hard, release, brake again.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The same non-ABS truck is in an emergency but you must also steer around debris. Which technique fits?
options: Trailer hand valve only, with the foot pedal up
Parking brake on and the foot valve untouched
Controlled braking, firm but not locking up
Stab braking with the wheels held locked while you turn
questions.explanation: Controlled braking is firm pressure that stops short of lockup so the tires can steer. Stab braking is for a straight emergency stop without ABS. Locking the wheels and then turning is how you lose the path you wanted.
questions.remember: Controlled: hard, no lockup, small steering.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your tractor and trailer both have ABS and a car stops hard ahead of you. What do you do with the pedal?
options: Pump the pedal so the ABS valves can wake up
Stab until you feel the wheels lock, then release every second
Use only the trolley valve so ABS on the tractor stays out of the stop
Press firmly and hold it, and steer
questions.explanation: ABS pulses the brakes for you. Pumping or stabbing turns that control off and on and lengthens the stop. Press firmly, hold, and steer. The system needs a steady application. Do not pump and do not stab.
questions.remember: ABS on all axles: brake fully, steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Only the tractor has ABS. The trailer is an older non-ABS unit. How should you handle a hard stop?
options: Brake normally, and ease off if the trailer swings out
Pump everything, because mixed equipment cancels ABS
Stab the tractor brakes and hold the trailer hand valve down
Disconnect the tractor ABS so both units feel the same
questions.explanation: CDL manual 2.18.5: with ABS on only the tractor, "Brake normally... keep your eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes (if you can safely do so) if it begins to swing out."
questions.remember: Trailer swinging out? Ease off the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The yellow ABS lamp on the dash comes on during the bulb check and then goes out. What does that sequence mean?
options: Cut-out pressure is too high and the lamp is the safety valve
The bulb works and no fault was found
ABS has been cancelled for the rest of the trip
The service brakes will not work until the lamp is on steady
questions.explanation: The ABS lamp should light for a bulb check and go out if the system passes. A lamp that never lights can hide a failure. A lamp that stays on means ABS may not work and needs service. The bulb works, and the light going out means the self-check did not find a fault.
questions.remember: ABS lamp: on, then off at start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After the bulb check, the tractor ABS lamp stays on while you drive. What is still true about stopping?
options: Pull the ABS fuse so the light goes out and the brakes become stronger
ABS lamps only matter on trailers
Normal brakes should work; get ABS serviced
The foot brake is now disabled until a shop clears the lamp
questions.explanation: ABS is an addition to the foundation brakes, not a replacement. A lamp that stays on means the antilock function may be offline. You can still brake, but you must not count on ABS, and you must not unplug it to hide the defect. Ordinary service brakes should still work, but ABS may not, so get it serviced and do not disconnect it.
questions.remember: ABS out? Normal brakes still work.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: In the mirror, the trailer ABS lamp stays lit after the start-up check. What should you do about that trailer?
options: Ignore it if the tractor ABS lamp went out
Cover the lamp
Stab-brake that trailer on every stop so the lamp resets
Treat its ABS as failed and get it repaired
questions.explanation: A trailer ABS fault does not care that the tractor lamp is out. That trailer can lock even while the tractor modulates. Leave the system connected and have the fault repaired before you depend on trailer ABS.
questions.remember: ABS lamp stays on? ABS may be lost.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are at the top of a long grade in a gear you used to climb the other side. Why is that gear often the wrong one for the descent?
options: You usually need a lower gear, chosen first
The climb gear is always one gear too low for a safe descent
Neutral is safer
Any gear is fine if you fan the brakes lightly the whole way down
questions.explanation: Gravity will push a loaded combination faster than the engine holds it. Pick a low enough gear before the downgrade, often lower than the gear that climbed the hill. Once you are already too fast, you may not get that gear back in. You usually need a lower gear than the climb gear, and you must select it before speed builds.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You chose a gear and a target speed for the downgrade. How do you snub when speed reaches that target?
options: Set the parking brake each time you are 5 mph over the target
Brake to 5 mph under target, release, repeat
Ride a light pedal all the way so the speed never changes by even 1 mph
Fan quick light taps without ever letting the shoes leave the drums
questions.explanation: Snubbing puts a firm application on, drops about 5 mph under your safe speed, then lets the brakes cool until speed creeps back. Light continuous fanning keeps the drums hot and can use more air than the compressor restores. Apply hard enough to fall about 5 mph below the target, release so the brakes can cool, then repeat.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A driver feathers the foot brake in light taps from the top of the mountain to the bottom. What is the likely result?
options: Light fanning builds extra pressure above cut-out
Fanning is the required method whenever the truck has ABS
The drums overheat and braking fades
The drums stay cool
questions.explanation: Heat causes fade. A light drag never gives the linings a chance to cool, and the compressor may not keep up with constant use. A low gear plus occasional firm snubs is the controlled method. The drums stay hot, braking power fades, and air pressure can fall faster than it is rebuilt.
questions.why: Overusing the service brakes overheats them and causes fade.
questions.remember: Long grade: let the engine brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Speed is climbing on a downgrade even though the pedal is near the floor and the smell of hot brakes is strong. An escape ramp is signed ahead. What do you do?
options: Pass the ramp and look for a flatter spot farther down
Jump the gravel bed at an angle so the trailer stays on the pavement
Shift to neutral and hope the springs apply by themselves
Use the ramp and stay on it
questions.explanation: Fade means the linings are too hot to do their job. The ramp is built to stop you, with gravel or an uphill grade. Leaving the ramp, or trying to jump it, throws away the only designed stop. Do not try to jump it or steer around it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After that long grade the drums are smoking hot and you can park on level ground. How should you secure the truck?
options: Stop, chock the wheels, and let the drums cool before you set the parking brake
Set the parking brake immediately so the hot drums cool in a clamped position
Keep rolling in a low gear so the wind cools the linings
Pour water on the drums and then clamp the parking brake
questions.explanation: A parking brake clamped on an extremely hot drum can crack the drum as it cools and shrinks. If you can chock and wait, do that. Do not use the parking brake as a routine way to stop a truck that is still moving.
questions.remember: Hot brakes? Chock, don't set the parking brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: At the end of the day the supply tank and the other reservoirs still have their drain cocks. What belongs in the shutdown routine?
options: Add water to the wet tank so the drains have something to seal against
Skip the drains whenever an alcohol evaporator is installed
Drain the tanks, including the supply tank where water collects, and close the cocks again
Leave every drain cock open overnight so the governor stays unloaded
questions.explanation: Compressed air leaves water and oil behind. Water freezes and rusts valves. Drain the tanks at the end of the day, then close the valves so the next start can build pressure. An alcohol evaporator does not remove that water.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your tractor has an alcohol evaporator, and the tanks were not drained after a wet week. Is the evaporator enough?
options: Yes. Alcohol replaces draining in every season
Yes, if you fill the evaporator with water instead of alcohol
No need to drain
No. The evaporator is not a substitute for draining water out of the tanks
questions.explanation: Alcohol vapor can reduce freezing of moisture that gets downstream. It does not empty the water already sitting in the tanks, and it does not fix a compressor pumping oil. Open the drains.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The supply-tank drain spits a stream of water. What does that tell you about tomorrow's trip if you do not drain it?
options: Water left in the tanks can freeze or damage valves, so drain it as maintenance
Water in the tank is required to lubricate the foot valve
A wet tank should be topped up with water until the safety valve weeps
Water only matters if the low-air lamp is on
questions.explanation: The compressor condenses moisture into the supply tank first. Draining removes it. Adding water, or leaving the puddle in cold weather, is how lines and valves freeze closed or stick.
questions.why: Water in the air tanks can freeze and cause brake failure.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Pressure builds very slowly, well outside the normal rise from about 85 to 100 psi, and a drain has already shown water and oil. What do you do?
options: Start and rely on the safety valve to finish the buildup on the road
Disconnect the low-air warning so a slow climb will not distract you
Do not start the trip
Add water to the wet tank to help the compressor seal
questions.explanation: Slow buildup, water, or oil are all reasons to stay parked. The fix is the compressor, governor, belts, leaks, or dryer. It is not water poured into a tank and not a longer hope that pressure will appear on the highway. Slow buildup means the charging system needs maintenance.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You pull a slack adjuster by hand with the brakes released and it moves more than about one inch where the pushrod attaches. What does the manual say that means?
options: One inch of free play is required so the drum can cool
Movement at the slack adjuster only measures tire pressure
Automatic adjusters should be forced past that point on every pre-trip
The brake probably needs adjustment before you depend on it
questions.explanation: With the wheels chocked and the springs released, excess movement at the pushrod clevis means the shoes are too far from the drum. The manual uses about one inch at that point as the sign it probably needs adjustment.
questions.remember: Slack adjuster moves too far? Adjust it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Applied pushrod travel on one chamber is longer than the adjustment limit listed for that chamber size. What is the status of that brake?
options: It is out of adjustment, even if a different chamber size allows a longer stroke
It is fine if every chamber on the truck is held to the same two-inch guess
Stroke limits apply only to steering-axle brakes
A long stroke means the brake will grab harder and stop shorter
questions.explanation: Each chamber size has its own maximum pushrod travel. Past that limit the S-cam can go over center and braking force collapses. Do not invent one stroke number for every chamber. If travel exceeds the limit for that chamber, the brake is out of adjustment.
questions.remember: Pushrod past the limit? Something's wrong.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An automatic slack adjuster is beyond its limit again a week after someone shortened the stroke by hand. What should happen next?
options: Lengthen the stroke on purpose so the adjuster stops clicking
The brake needs repair
Keep backing the adjuster off every morning and skip the repair
Disconnect that chamber so the other brakes work harder
questions.explanation: Automatic adjusters that cannot hold a setting usually mean worn parts or a failed adjuster. A roadside twist of the screw may get you a legal stroke for a moment and then leave you long again. Have the foundation brake repaired. Repeating a manual tweak is not a lasting fix.
questions.remember: Auto adjuster out again? Fix the brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Grease is smeared on a brake lining and the drum on that wheel. How will that brake behave if you leave anyway?
options: Contamination matters only when ABS is turned off
The lining will not hold reliably
Grease makes the shoe grab harder and shortens the stop
Oil on the lining burns off cleanly on the first downgrade
questions.explanation: Oil or grease on the friction surface drops the brake's torque and can pull the truck to the dry side. Do not try to boil it off on the highway. The linings and the leaking seal have to be repaired. The truck needs service before the trip.
questions.why: Dirt or grease on the brakes cuts braking friction.
questions.remember: Grease on the brakes? Fix it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before you roll, you set the parking brake, select a low gear, and pull against it gently. The truck moves. What did you learn?
options: Movement is normal if the service brake test felt smooth
The yellow valve is a hill-holder and should creep on level ground
The parking brake will not hold, so do not start the trip
A parking brake is only required to slow the truck
questions.explanation: The parking-brake test is a gentle pull in low gear against the spring brakes. If the truck moves, the springs, the adjustment, or the linkage will not hold you on a grade. Repair it before you need it.
questions.remember: Test the parking brake: low gear, gentle pull.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The parking brake held. You release it, roll slowly, and press the foot brake. The truck dives to the left and does not stop straight. What next?
options: A pull to one side is normal on a dual-air system
Drive it until both gauges read 125 psi and the pull will center
Use the trailer hand valve on every stop to hide the pull
Do not start the trip
questions.explanation: The moving service-brake test is where you feel a dead chamber, a greased lining, or a long stroke. A stop that pulls is not a successful test. Park and repair before the combination is in traffic.
questions.remember: Truck pulls when braking? Brake trouble.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You want the trailer brakes alone for a test in a yard. How does the hand valve fit, and how does it not fit?
options: Use it only as a test tool
Leave it partially on while you drive so the trailer shares every stop
It is the best parking brake
Hold it down on a long grade instead of snubbing with the foot valve
questions.explanation: The trolley valve applies trailer service brakes only. It does not charge or dump the emergency line, so it is not a parking brake. Driving with it on drags the trailer brakes, and using it to slow a light trailer can lock the trailer and start a skid. Do not park with it and do not drive with it applied.
questions.why: Using the hand valve while driving can make the trailer skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer is empty and you keep the hand valve partly applied to 'keep the rig straight' in traffic. What can that cause?
options: The hand valve charges the tractor spring brakes and prevents a skid
The light trailer wheels can lock and the trailer can swing or jackknife
An empty trailer cannot lock
A partial hand-valve application cools the drums
questions.explanation: Light weight on the trailer tires means the same application locks them sooner. Locked trailer wheels lose sideways grip and the trailer swings. Control the combination with the foot brake and a smooth steer, not with the trolley valve.
questions.why: Using the hand valve while driving can make the trailer skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are testing the low-air warning and the spring-brake pop-out. Why is the key on and the engine off?
options: A running engine is required so the safety valve can be part of the test
The warnings need power; a compressor hides drops
The engine must be off
The key must be off or the springs cannot apply
questions.explanation: Fan the pressure down with the compressor stopped or the gauges will climb while you are trying to lower them. The warning is electric, so the key has to be on or a dead buzzer looks like a pass. The lamps and buzzer need electrical power, and a running compressor would hide the pressure drop.
questions.remember: Key on, engine off for the warning test.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The wheels are not chocked, the engine is off, and you are about to push the parking valves in for a leak test on a grade. What can happen?
options: A grade makes the leak test invalid
The yellow valve cannot release the springs unless the truck is moving
The spring brakes will release and the truck can roll, so chock before you release them
Spring brakes stay applied whenever the engine is off, even with the valves pushed in
questions.explanation: Released spring brakes are just air holding mechanical springs back. On a grade, with no driver in the seat, the truck will roll. Chock first, then do the test.
questions.remember: Leak test: engine off, chocks, brake released.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A belt that drives the air compressor is frayed and slipping. Buildup from 85 toward 100 psi is already too slow. What is the connection?
options: The belt only drives the fan, so buildup is unrelated
A loose belt raises cut-out and shortens stopping distance
Spray the belt with oil so it slips less and the leak test will pass
A slipping belt cannot turn the compressor fast enough
questions.explanation: Compressor output depends on engine speed and a belt that actually grips. A slipping or broken belt is a failed buildup test even if the governor is set correctly. Replace the belt. Do not oil it and hope. You do not leave.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Two supply gauges are fitted on a dual-air tractor. Why watch both, not just the one that usually reads higher?
options: The secondary gauge is only a spare bulb for the primary
Each gauge is a separate circuit that can fail
The lower gauge is a trailer-hand-valve thermometer
Both needles must match within 1 psi or the safety valve opens
questions.explanation: Primary and secondary are protected from each other. Looking at a single needle hides an empty circuit. Both should be at least about 100 psi before you move, and both should be included in the leak and warning tests. Each gauge is a separate circuit, and one can fail while the other still looks normal.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An older truck has a manual front-brake limiting valve, and the control is left in the slippery position on dry pavement. What did you give up?
options: The rear brakes
ABS, because the limiting valve replaces the foot pedal
Full air to the steer-axle brakes
Nothing, because the slippery setting is required on dry roads
questions.explanation: The limiting valve, on trucks that still have one, reduces front-brake pressure for a slick surface. On dry pavement that reduction only lengthens the stop. Put it in the normal position when the road is dry. Many newer trucks use ABS instead of this valve. The stop is longer than the system was built for.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Someone ties the low-air wigwag up so it will not drop in front of the windshield. What protection did they remove?
options: Only a decoration on the visor
The governor cut-out
The trailer spring brakes
The low-air warning device
questions.explanation: A wigwag is one form of the low-air warning. Tied up, it cannot tell you the tanks are emptying. The warning has to work before pressure goes below 60 psi. Do not disable it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You disconnect a trailer on a windy yard and the glad hands are left open on the tractor deck. Why couple them to the dummy fittings or to each other?
options: Open glad hands pick up dirt that will be blown into the valves at the next hookup
Open glad hands let the governor cut out at a lower pressure on purpose
Dummy couplers are only for the electrical cord
Leaving them open drains water out of the foot valve while you drive bobtail
questions.explanation: The emergency and service lines should be sealed when they are not on a trailer. Dirt in a glad hand becomes dirt in a valve. Seals also have to be present and not cracked when you do connect, or the next trailer will leak.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A glad-hand seal is cracked and flat. Air leaks at the connection as soon as you supply the trailer. What is the fix before you move?
options: Pull the red valve out and drive with the trailer springs dragging
Replace the seal and do not leave with air escaping at the glad hand
Wrap the seal with tape and charge the trailer anyway
Cross the hoses so the leak moves to the other color
questions.explanation: The rubber seal is what makes the glad hand airtight. A leak at that joint fails the leak test and can pop the red valve back out. Put in a good seal, rematch the colors, and confirm the trailer holds air.
