provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The service line separates from the trailer while you are moving, but the red emergency line stays coupled. What did you lose?
options: The tractor spring brakes, which immediately lock the drive axles
Governor cut-out, which now depends on the blue line
The signal that applies the trailer service brakes with the foot pedal, so stop and reconnect
Nothing, because the emergency line applies the trailer brakes every time you press the pedal
questions.explanation: The blue service line carries the application. If it comes apart, the foot valve no longer commands the trailer brakes. The emergency line may still hold the trailer springs off. You are stopping with less brake than you think. Pull over and recouple. Do not keep going.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The red emergency line tears off while you are moving. What should the trailer and the tractor protection valve do?
options: The trailer should roll free with no brakes so you can reach a shop
Both tractor tanks should dump instantly through the open glad hand
The blue line should become the supply and release the trailer springs
Trailer springs apply; tractor air is saved
questions.explanation: Loss of the emergency line is a trailer emergency. The trailer springs come on, and the tractor protection valve closes so a trailer breakaway does not empty the tractor. Stop safely. Do not try to finish the trip with the trailer brakes locked or the line hanging.
questions.remember: Tractor protection valve keeps tractor air.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: S-cam brakes on the drive axles are the foundation brakes your air chambers operate. What is the chamber actually doing when you press the pedal?
options: Releasing the spring brake directly on the steer axle only
Opening the governor so compressor air blows the shoes outward
Pushing a rod that rotates the S-cam and forces the shoes out against the drum
Sending hydraulic oil through the cam to the rotor
questions.explanation: Air in the service chamber moves the pushrod, the slack adjuster turns the S-cam, and the cam lifts the shoes. If the stroke is too long, that cam can rotate past the point of useful force. The air system is only as good as that foundation brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You coast a long grade in neutral to save the brakes, planning to snub only if speed gets high. Why does the manual reject that plan?
options: You lose engine braking and the brakes overheat
Neutral lets the compressor build air faster than any gear
Coast-in-neutral is the preferred snub method on air brakes
A neutral descent keeps the drums near outside temperature
questions.explanation: Engine compression in a low gear is part of the hold. Neutral turns the whole grade over to the foundation brakes, which then fade. Select the gear before the hill and stay in it. Do not coast. You give up engine hold, you may not get a low gear back in, and the brakes then have to do all the work hot.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The engine dies while you are moving and you still have a full air tank. What is true about the next several brake applications?
options: Spring brakes immediately release and stay off without air
Stored air gives a limited number of stops
A dead engine releases all air at once through the governor
Hydraulic backup takes over as soon as rpm hits zero
questions.explanation: The tanks, not the spinning compressor, hold the air you have. Each application and each leak spends it, and a stalled engine does not pump more. Brake to a safe stop while you still have pressure. Do not keep driving a long distance on the air that is left. Stored air will apply the brakes a limited number of times, but the dead engine will not replenish it.
questions.remember: Tanks hold air for a few stops.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During a pre-trip the low-air warning comes on at 75 psi as you fan down. Does that fail the warning test?
options: Yes. Any warning above cut-in means the governor is failed
No. The warning is allowed to wait until 20 psi if it is loud
No. It must come on before 60 psi
Yes. The warning must wait until pressure is under 60 psi
questions.explanation: Early is acceptable. Late is not. If the buzzer and light are on by the time pressure reaches 60 psi, the warning test is met. If they are still off at 55 psi, it is not. No. The warning must come on before pressure falls below 60 psi, so 75 psi is early enough.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Spring brakes on your tractor apply by themselves at about 25 psi during the fan-down test. Is that inside the designed window?
options: No. They must wait until pressure is under 20 psi
No. They should apply as soon as pressure leaves 100 psi
Yes, but only if the safety valve opened first
Yes. Between 20 and 45 psi is normal
questions.explanation: The springs are a backup, not the service brake. They should come on by themselves between 20 and 45 psi. Application only after the gauge is under 20, or application up near normal driving pressure, means the system needs service.
questions.remember: Valves pop out at 20 to 45 psi.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You finish fueling and the trailer supply valve is in, but a tractor protection leak keeps dropping both gauges whenever the engine is off. What is the disciplined choice?
options: Cross the glad hands to move the leak off the emergency line
Do not start until the leak is repaired
Leave, because a compressor at cruise rpm is an approved leak repair
Open the tank drains so the leak has a second path
questions.explanation: If the system only holds while the compressor is pumping, it will not hold in a stall, a long snub, or a traffic jam. An audible leak or a hose that is cut or swollen is the same decision: do not go. Do not start the trip until the leak is repaired, even if a running compressor can almost keep up.
questions.remember: Air leak? Fix it before driving.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Rain has pooled and the next morning is below freezing. You did not drain the tanks. What failure are you setting up?
options: Frozen water only affects the alcohol evaporator
A frozen drain cock shortens brake lag in a useful way
Water can freeze and block the brakes
Ice in the tank raises cut-out and makes the brakes grab harder
questions.explanation: Draining is a cold-weather brake check, not a housekeeping extra. Ice can close a valve or hold a brake on. The alcohol evaporator, if you even have one, does not remove the water you left in the tank. Water in the lines and valves can freeze and block a brake application or a release.
questions.why: Water in the air tanks can freeze and cause brake failure.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your combination is legal on the leak test, the warning works, and both gauges are above 100 psi, but the service-brake stop pulls hard to the right. Which result controls?
options: Pressure tests override a pull
A pull means the load is balanced and the brakes are equal
Pull is corrected by lowering cut-out 10 psi
The pulling stop fails the truck even though the pressure tests passed
questions.explanation: Air pressure, leakage, warning, and spring-brake tests do not prove the foundation brakes are even. The slow roll and a firm pedal should stop the truck smoothly and in a straight line. A pull means one side is not doing its share.
questions.remember: Truck pulls when braking? Brake trouble.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are snubbing correctly, but you started down the grade one gear too high and speed will not stay near your target. What is the dangerous temptation?
options: To ride the brakes harder instead of using an escape ramp if they begin to fade
To drop about 5 mph under target and then release
To stay in the low gear you should have chosen at the top
To keep the parking brake released while the drums are still cool
questions.explanation: A gear that cannot hold the grade forces the brakes to do continuous work. If firm snubs no longer bring speed down, the linings are fading. The escape ramp is the next tool. Do not trade it for a hotter pedal.
questions.why: Brakes used hard keep fading until you can't stop.
questions.remember: Long grade: let the engine brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During the applied leak test you ease the pedal up halfway through the minute. Why is that test now useless?
options: The minute only counts with the parking brake also applied
A half pedal is the required combination test
The chambers are no longer fully applied
Easing off makes the test stricter and any drop fails
questions.explanation: The applied limits, 3 psi single and 4 psi combination, are for a full, steady service application held for one minute. Letting the pedal up changes the pressure in the lines. Start the minute over with the pedal held. The reading is not the full-application leak rate.
questions.remember: Applied leak test: hold the pedal a full minute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The static test is underway and you realize the compressor is still running. Why restart the test with the engine off?
options: The compressor must run or the gauges will fall about 5 mph
Engine-off tests only measure the safety valve
The governor will not allow a leak test below cut-out
A running compressor can hide a leak
questions.explanation: Leak-rate numbers are measured on stored air, not on air the compressor is adding. Engine off, wheels chocked, brakes in the condition the test calls for. Otherwise a bad system can look tight. A running compressor replaces leaked air and can hide a failure you would see with the engine off.
questions.remember: Leak test: engine off, chocks, brake released.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The manual lists perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. Which of those is the air-system piece a hydraulic car does not share?
options: Braking distance, which does not exist on vehicles with S-cam brakes
Brake lag distance, caused by the time air needs to flow after you move the pedal
Perception distance, which is longer because air gauges are harder to see
Reaction distance, which starts only after the governor cuts in
questions.explanation: You see the hazard, you move your foot, then air still has to travel before the shoes work, and only then do you get braking distance. Forgetting lag is how truck drivers leave the same gap they used in a car.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A loaded combination and an empty one use the same air pressure at the pedal. Why can the empty combination still be harder to control in a hard stop?
options: Light weight doubles reservoir pressure and causes a runaway
Empty trailers are required to use the parking brake for every stop
Light axles lock sooner
An empty combination has no brake lag
questions.explanation: The brakes are sized for a load. With little weight on the tires, the same application locks them. Locked trailer or drive wheels start a skid or a jackknife. Smooth, moderate applications, and ABS where you have it, matter more when the trailer is light, not less.
questions.why: An empty trailer's stiff springs and strong brakes give poor traction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your pre-trip finds the compressor will not cut out near 125 psi and will not cut in near 100 psi. Which statement is fair?
options: Only cut-out matters, and any cut-in below 60 psi is legal
Cut-in at 50 psi is normal if cut-out is above 150 psi
The safety valve replaces the governor
Both ends of the governor's job are wrong
questions.explanation: Cut-out about 125 psi stops the compressor. Cut-in about 100 psi starts it again. The safety valve near 150 psi is not a substitute governor. If those control points are far off, have the governor serviced. The charging system is not in normal condition.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A tractor protection valve closes during a yard test when you open the trailer emergency line. What useful thing just happened?
options: Protection valves are only for hydraulic trailers
It saved tractor air and set trailer brakes
The valve failed
The blue service line is now the parking brake
questions.explanation: A breakaway or a bad trailer leak must not take the tractor's air with it. The protection valve closes and the trailer springs apply. If it does not, a trailer failure can leave you with no air in the tractor either. The tractor's air was protected and the trailer emergency brakes applied instead of emptying the tractor.
questions.remember: Tractor protection valve keeps tractor air.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are in a curve when you make a hard non-ABS stop and you lock the wheels. Why did steering quit working?
options: Lockup shortens brake lag to zero and steering becomes hydraulic
Locked wheels steer better
Steering loss means the secondary air circuit has cut in
Locked wheels slide instead of rolling
questions.explanation: A tire that is sliding goes where momentum takes it. Controlled braking keeps the wheels rolling so they can generate a turn. With ABS you press and hold so the ABS can prevent that lock. Without ABS you ease off a lockup if you still need to steer.
questions.why: Locked wheels have less traction than rolling wheels.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During a roadside check an officer measures pushrod travel with the brakes applied and a marked tool. One brake is past the limit for its chamber and the others are inside their own limits. Which brakes are out of adjustment?
options: None, if the slack adjusters moved less than about one inch with the brakes applied
Only steer-axle brakes can be out of adjustment
Only the brake whose travel exceeds the limit for its own chamber
Every brake, because one long stroke sets a new limit for all of them
questions.explanation: Adjustment is per chamber. A type of chamber with a longer legal stroke does not lend that number to a smaller chamber, and a long chamber does not condemn a short one that is still inside its own limit.
questions.remember: Pushrod past the limit? Something's wrong.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Non-ABS stab braking is described to a new driver as 'lock the wheels and hold them locked until you stop.' What did that description leave out?
options: You must release the brakes so the wheels can roll, then reapply
You should apply only the trailer hand valve during a stab
Stab braking means a gentle 5 mph snub on level ground
Locked wheels are held that way only when ABS is installed
questions.explanation: The release is the part that lets the tires get traction back. Holding a lock is a skid, not stab braking. And if the vehicle has ABS, you do not stab at all. You press and hold.
questions.remember: Stab: brake hard, release, brake again.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your dual-air gauges both read about 90 psi and the low-air warning is off. A dispatcher wants the truck moving now. Why do you still wait?
options: Dual-air trucks may leave at whatever pressure the springs release
Both systems should be at least about 100 psi before you drive a dual-air vehicle
Ninety psi is above 60 psi
The warning being off means cut-out has already happened
questions.explanation: The warning threshold and the driving threshold are different. The buzzer must be on before you fall below 60 psi, but you do not start out just above that floor. Wait until both circuits are at least about 100 psi.
questions.remember: Wait for 100 psi in both systems.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A long downhill ends at a traffic light. Your snubs worked and speed is controlled, but the drums are very hot. The light is red and the shoulder is wide enough to chock. What parking choice protects the drums?
options: Keep the foot brake and the parking brake both clamped for the whole cool-down
Drive another mile with the hand valve on to cool the tractor drums
Stop, chock, and let the heat leave the drums before you apply the parking brake
Set the parking brake at once so the shoes can press the heat out of the drum
questions.explanation: Extremely hot drums can crack if the parking brake clamps them while they cool and contract. Chocks exist for this. Use them when you can, and do not add a hard parking-brake application to a drum that is already in trouble.
questions.remember: Hot brakes? Chock, don't set the parking brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A newly rebuilt foot valve applies the brakes, but the stop-lamp switch never lights the brake lamps. Why does that switch matter to other drivers?
options: It is only a bulb check for the ABS lamp and does not feed the brake lamps
Brake lamps are powered by the governor
The switch is optional if the trailer hand valve is never used
It turns the brake lamps on when you apply the service brakes
questions.explanation: Air pressure from a service application closes the stop-light switch. If the lamps stay dark, the people behind you get no warning. That circuit is part of the air-brake system, and you fix it before you mix with traffic.
questions.remember: Stop-light switch lights the brake lights.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You just coupled and the trailer brakes will not release even though the red valve stays in and the gauges are above 100 psi. What should you refuse to do?
options: Refuse to check the glad-hand colors
Add water at the trailer tank so the shoes swell free
Drive a few miles so heat can free the shoes
Refuse to drag the trailer with its brakes on
questions.explanation: Moving a trailer whose springs or service brakes are stuck on destroys linings and drums and means you may not have a real trailer application later. Air at the tractor gauges does not prove the trailer is charged and released. Match the lines, open the shutoffs, and confirm the brakes come off. Find the closed valve, crossed line, or leak first.
questions.remember: Brakes won't release? Check the air lines.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The fifth-wheel plate is dry and rusty on a pre-trip, and the jaws look undamaged. Why does that dry plate still keep the combination parked?
options: A dry plate is preferred
Plate grease is only for sliding tandems
A dry plate binds as the trailer turns and can make the tractor hard to steer
Grease belongs only on the kingpin head so the jaws slip off
questions.explanation: The plate has to be greased so the trailer can pivot without fighting the tractor. A dry plate wears the coupling and makes steering heavy. Grease does not replace jaws that lock on the kingpin shank.
questions.why: A dry fifth wheel plate can cause steering trouble from friction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before you back under, the fifth-wheel jaws are still closed from the last trailer. What has to happen first?
options: Leave the jaws closed so they grab the kingpin head on contact
Grease the closed jaws shut and skip the lock check
Couple with the jaws closed if the trailer is empty
Open the jaws and set the release so the kingpin can enter and lock
questions.explanation: Closed jaws cannot take the kingpin. You will hit the pin or sit on top of it without a lock. Open the lock, confirm the plate is tilted down toward the trailer, and only then back under.
questions.remember: Back under with the jaws open.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You line the tractor up at an angle to save time in a tight yard. What can that angle do to the trailer?
options: Shove the trailer sideways and bend or collapse the landing gear
Help the jaws find the kingpin head
Reduce offtracking on the way out of the yard
It is required whenever the fifth wheel is greased
questions.explanation: The tractor and trailer should meet straight. An angled approach pushes the trailer off its landing gear. Straighten out, even if that means a longer setup, before the fifth wheel touches the nose.
questions.why: Backing under at an angle can push the trailer sideways and break the landing gear.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The fifth wheel has just touched the trailer nose and a helper waves you to keep backing until it clicks. Why get out now instead?
options: The electrical cord has to be tested before the fifth wheel is allowed to touch
You still have to check height, kingpin condition, and that the jaws are open before you slide under
A click at first contact is proof the shank is locked
Height only matters after the landing gear is fully stowed
questions.explanation: The model sequence stops when the fifth wheel meets the trailer. Trailer too high can put the jaws on the kingpin head or let the pin ride over the plate. Trailer too low lets the tractor strike the nose. Look before you commit.
questions.remember: Line up the kingpin and fifth wheel.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer nose is high enough that the kingpin could pass over the fifth-wheel plate. What kind of couple are you risking?
options: No risk if you supply air before you look
A high nose only matters on a converter dolly
A false latch on the kingpin head
A couple that is stronger
questions.explanation: The jaws must close on the shank. If they close on the head, or the pin never enters, the trailer can separate. Lower the trailer with the landing gear until the tractor will lift it slightly as you slide under. A missed couple or a false latch on the kingpin head instead of a lock on the shank.
questions.remember: Trailer too high? It may not couple.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer sits so low that the fifth-wheel ramps will meet the nose below the kingpin. What damage are you trying to avoid?
options: A low trailer only scuffs paint and always locks correctly
The danger is extra grease being wiped off the plate
A low setting puts more weight on the steering axle automatically
Striking and bending the trailer nose or the landing gear as you force the couple
questions.explanation: The trailer should be just low enough that backing under raises it slightly. Too low and you are using the tractor as a ram. Adjust the landing gear. Do not power under a nose that is in the way.
questions.remember: Trailer too low? You'll hit the nose.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You connect the air lines, charge the trailer, and then pull the red supply valve back out. Why is that the step before the final backup?
options: It sets the trailer spring brakes so the trailer cannot roll while you finish the couple
It releases the trailer brakes so you can shove a free-rolling trailer onto the jaws
It is the tug test, and no visual check comes after it
It opens the jaws from the cab
questions.explanation: With the trailer brakes set, the kingpin stays put and you can later pull against it. Charging first proves air is there and lets you hear leaks. Leaving the trailer brakes released while you bang into the pin is how a trailer gets shoved off its gear.
questions.remember: Pull the air supply knob: trailer brakes set.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The yard air is up and you are ready to slide under for the lock. Which gear and speed fit that backup?
options: Any gear if a helper says they heard a click
Lowest reverse, slow enough that you stop as soon as the kingpin locks
High reverse so the pin clicks harder and the lock is deeper
Neutral, and let the trailer roll onto the tractor
questions.explanation: A fast hit can bend the kingpin, the jaws, or the landing gear. Use the lowest reverse and walk it under until the lock closes. A sound is not the end of the job. The tug and the look under the trailer still have to happen.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Landing gear is still down hard when you tug. The tractor does not move, but the gear is carrying the trailer. Why raise the gear slightly and tug again?
options: A second tug with the legs up is only for doubles
Raising the legs releases the jaws on purpose
The first pull can pass even if the jaws missed
Landing gear must stay fully down for the whole road test
questions.explanation: The security check is a gentle pull against the locked pin with the trailer brakes set and the legs just off the ground, so the fifth wheel is actually holding the nose. Then you still get under and look.
questions.remember: Lift the landing gear off the ground.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The tug against set trailer brakes held. Under the trailer you can see daylight between the fifth wheel and the apron. What does that gap mean?
options: A small gap is required so the trailer can pivot
Daylight means the plate has the right amount of grease
The gap shows the jaws are on the shank
The trailer is not fully seated
questions.explanation: No daylight should show between the upper and lower fifth wheel. A gap means the nose is not down on the plate. The jaws may be on the head of the kingpin. That high couple can drop the trailer. Redo it. The couple is not safe to take on the road.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Looking in from the side, the jaws are closed on the head of the kingpin rather than around the shank. What should you expect if you drive away?
options: The trailer can separate
A lock on the head is the design and is stronger than a shank lock
The head lock is acceptable when the plate is greased
The safety latch makes a head lock legal for a short move
questions.explanation: The shank is the groove the jaws are shaped to hold. The head is wider and can pull out of a false latch. If you see jaws on the head, or you are not sure, uncouple and do it again. Do not trust the road to finish the lock. The lock is not on the part of the pin that holds.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The jaws look closed on the shank and there is no gap, but the locking lever is not seated and its safety latch is hanging. Is the visual check done?
options: No need, because the red air valve is the safety latch
No. Seat the lever and set the latch
Yes. The latch is optional if the tug already held
Yes. The lever only matters on a sliding fifth wheel
questions.explanation: The lever and latch keep the jaws from opening. A couple that looks closed but is not latched can unlock over a bump. Seat the lever and put the latch on. Then stow the landing gear. No. The lever has to be seated and the safety latch has to be on before you trust the couple.
questions.remember: Safety latch over the locking lever.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The couple passed the tug and the visual check. The legs are still partly down and the crank is swinging free. What has to happen before you roll?
options: Tie the crank to a glad hand so you can find it later
Partly raised legs are required at railroad crossings
Raise the landing gear all the way and secure the crank handle
Leave a few inches of leg down so the nose cannot drop
questions.explanation: Landing gear that is only partway up will catch crossings, curbs, and railroad tracks. A loose crank swings into traffic or into the tractor. Raise the legs fully, put the handle in its keeper, and check that the legs will not hit the frame in a turn.
questions.why: Landing gear left part way down can catch on tracks or other things.
questions.remember: Landing gear all the way up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Air lines are coupled and the electric cord is plugged in, but both droop onto the catwalk and the frame. Why is that not a finished hookup?
options: Lines should drag so a turn cannot stretch them
The cord may drag if the air lines are supported
Slack is unsafe
They can be pinched or torn off
questions.explanation: Too tight, and a turn pulls the glad hands or the plug apart. Too loose, and they drag, chafe, or get crushed between the plate and the apron. Support them, match the air colors, and look at them again after a tight turn. They can be pinched, torn off, or pulled apart, so support them with enough slack for a full turn and no drag.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A bent kingpin is visible when you inspect the nose, and the apron is cracked. Why refuse the trailer even though the jaws on your tractor work?
options: A bent pin or a cracked apron may not lock or may break the couple after you leave
A bent pin locks more tightly and is preferred on a heavy load
Cracks in the apron only matter for the landing gear crank
You can straighten a kingpin with the fifth-wheel release handle
questions.explanation: The upper coupler has to present a straight pin and a flat apron. If either is damaged, the jaws can miss or the pin can fail. Do not couple it. Get another trailer or a shop.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fifth-wheel mounting bolts are loose and a crack runs in the bracket that holds the fifth wheel to the frame. What is the right status for that tractor?
options: Fixed by sliding the fifth wheel all the way forward
Out of service for coupling until the mounting is repaired
Safe if you grease the plate heavily to cushion the crack
Safe for an empty trailer only
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel is only as strong as its mount. Loose bolts or a cracked bracket can let the whole coupling shift or break. Grease and a careful tug do not repair metal. Do not put a trailer on it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You heard one solid click as the pin entered and the helper is already cranking the legs up. Why is the click not the security check?
options: One click means the jaws took the head
The click is the electrical cord seating
A click can happen on a partial or false lock
The click replaces both the latch and the no-daylight check
questions.explanation: Locks can sound closed and still be on the wrong part of the pin, or the lever can be short of its seat. The manual's proof is a gentle pull with the trailer brakes set, plus eyes on the jaws, the gap, and the latch.
questions.remember: Tug test: pull gently, trailer brakes on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer has no spring brakes, and you need to leave it dropped in a yard. How do you keep it from rolling?
options: Chock the wheels
Leave the hand valve connected to a dead glad hand
Set the tractor parking brake and then uncouple
Turn the landing-gear crank to high and that brakes the axles
questions.explanation: Spring brakes are what hold a normal parked trailer after the air line is pulled. Without them, the trailer is free to roll as soon as the tractor leaves. The manual tells you to chock a trailer that has no spring brakes.
questions.remember: No spring brakes? Chock the wheels.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are choosing a spot to uncouple. The pavement is soft gravel and the tractor is still at an angle to the trailer. Why look for another place?
options: The kingpin releases only when the ground is soft
The legs can sink or bend
An angle is required so the jaws unload evenly
Gravel is preferred
questions.explanation: The legs have to hold the whole nose. Soft ground, a slope, or an angled pull-out is how landing gear folds or punches in. Pick firm, level ground and line the tractor up with the trailer before you touch the release.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer brakes are set and you want the fifth-wheel release to move without jumping. What do you do to the jaws before you pull the handle?
options: Raise the landing gear fully before you lower it, with the jaws still loaded
Dump the tractor air so the springs open the lock
Back gently against the pin, then set brakes
Pull forward hard so the pin snaps the jaws open
questions.explanation: Loaded jaws bind on the pin. A gentle backup with the trailer brakes holding transfers that pressure off the lock so the handle can move. Set the tractor brakes in that eased position. Stay clear of the release; equipment can shift when it lets go.
questions.remember: Back gently to ease the jaws.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer is loaded. The landing gear has just made firm contact with the pavement. Why give the crank more turns in low gear?
options: Extra turns are only for an empty trailer
Extra turns are how you lock the pintle hook
Stop at first contact even when the trailer is loaded, or the nose will be too high to uncouple
To take weight off the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: An empty trailer needs firm contact. A loaded trailer needs firm contact plus a few more low-gear turns so the legs actually carry weight. High gear under a heavy nose is how the crank kicks back and injures you. Do not drive away at an angle after this. Those extra turns lift some trailer weight off the fifth wheel so the jaws can release and the next driver is not stuck with a high bind.
questions.remember: Landing gear down, then a few extra turns.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Air lines and the electric cord are still connected and you pull the fifth-wheel release. What should you have done with those lines first?
options: Open the tank drains instead of disconnecting anything
Disconnect them and stow them
Leave them coupled so they pull apart cleanly and save a step
Disconnect only the blue line and leave the cord to tear free
questions.explanation: Glad hands that separate under tension can snap back into the cab. An electric cord that is pulled apart is ruined, and a dragging line gets caught under the fifth wheel. Disconnect and stow them before you unlock and drive out. Do not use a breakaway as your uncoupling method. Disconnect them and stow them on the tractor fittings so they cannot yank apart or drag.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The fifth wheel is unlocked and you start to pull clear. How far do you go on the first move?
options: Not at all; you lower the legs after the tractor is fully gone
Far enough to swing the tractor sideways and park it beside the trailer
Just until the fifth wheel clears the kingpin
All the way clear in one motion so the landing gear gets a sharp test
questions.explanation: If the legs fold or the ground gives up, a tractor that is still under the nose can catch the trailer. Stop there, set the brake, and look at the legs and the ground. Only then pull the rest of the way clear. Only far enough that the fifth wheel clears the kingpin while the tractor frame is still under the nose.
questions.remember: Pull out until the fifth wheel clears.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You stopped with the frame still under the trailer and the landing gear is bending. What did that pause give you?
options: Proof that an angled uncoupling is safer
A reason to pull the red valve in and drive away quickly
Evidence that chocks are illegal on a dropped trailer
A chance to see the failure before the nose dropped clear of the tractor
questions.explanation: The partial pull-out is a deliberate test of the legs. If they sink or bend, you are still in a position to hold the nose. Pulling clear in one move turns a bending leg into a dropped trailer.
questions.why: Stopping with the frame under the trailer keeps it from falling if the landing gear gives way.
questions.remember: Stop with the frame still under the trailer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After a fifth-wheel slide the locking pins are not fully in, and you can see the slider can still move. What is the hazard if you enter traffic that way?
options: An unlocked fifth wheel steers better
The only risk is a dash lamp for the trailer ABS
The kingpin cannot come out if the plate is greased
The fifth wheel can shift under braking
questions.explanation: A sliding fifth wheel that is not locked can walk forward or back. That unloads an axle you just set, and in the worst case the slider hits the stops hard. Look at the locks. Do not drive with them out. The fifth wheel can shift under braking or in a turn and suddenly change axle weights and handling.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A right turn is coming up and there is oncoming traffic in the lane you would swing into. How should you set up the turn?
options: Do not swing left into that oncoming lane
Swing left first
Hug the curb with the tractor so the trailer has room to track outside the turn
Stop in the intersection and back the trailer around the corner
questions.explanation: The trailer cuts inside the tractor's path. Swinging wide to the left puts you in front of oncoming traffic and opens a hole on your right that cars will try to fill. If you can avoid that swing, do. Watch the right mirror. If someone is inside the turn, stop instead of dragging the trailer into them. Turn wide enough that the trailer clears the inside, and keep vehicles out of the space on your right.
questions.remember: Right turn: don't swing left first.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The tractor is clearing a right corner, but the trailer tires are headed for the curb and a sign on the inside. What is that path called, and what do you change next time?
options: High-speed swing, which pulls the trailer outside the curb
Offtracking: the trailer takes a shorter path
Rearward amplification, which only happens on a straight highway
A jackknife, which you fix by adding trailer-hand-valve pressure
questions.explanation: At low speed the rear wheels track inside the front wheels. Longer trailers and a longer distance from kingpin to tandems offtrack more. Know that distance before you commit. Once the trailer is into the curb, stop. Do not try to scrub it around. You needed a wider turn.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An exit ramp is signed for a lower speed and your load is stacked high in a van. When do you slow down?
options: You do not slow a combination on a ramp
Before the ramp, while you are still on the straight road
After the tractor is already in the curve, using a hard brake
Only if the trailer ABS lamp comes on
questions.explanation: Rollover risk is a high center of gravity plus too much speed in a curve or on a ramp. Braking hard in the curve, or waiting until you feel the tractor lean, is late. The trailer can start over while the cab still feels acceptable. Set the speed before the turn.
questions.remember: Slow and downshift before the curve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: In a set of doubles, you make a sudden steer and the tractor still feels flat. Why is that feeling a poor guide to what the rear trailer is doing?
options: The rear trailer is the most stable unit in a sudden swerve
Amplification only affects the tractor drive axles
The rear trailer can roll while you feel fine
Doubles cancel crack-the-whip
questions.explanation: A quick move grows as it passes through the pintle and the second fifth wheel. The last trailer sees the biggest sideways force. That is worse on doubles and worse again on triples. Steer gently, and do it at a speed you set before the curve, not in it. Rearward amplification can roll the last trailer while the tractor still feels stable.
questions.why: A sudden steering move can tip your trailer over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Triples are on the hook and traffic is opening a gap that would take a sharp lane change. Why is that gap a bad invitation?
options: Triples offtrack less than a single trailer, so sharp moves are safer
A sharp change is required so the dolly does not bind
The converter dolly removes rearward amplification
The last trailer could roll over
questions.explanation: Every extra articulation point adds crack-the-whip. The rear trailer is the one that goes first, and the cab is a poor instrument for that roll. Leave the sharp move to the cars. Take the gap slowly or not at all. The last trailer can amplify the steer into a rollover that you will not feel in time from the cab.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer is empty, the road is wet, and you make a hard foot-brake application. Why can this stop be less stable than the same stop with a loaded trailer?
options: Light trailer tires lock more easily and a locked trailer can swing
An empty trailer cannot jackknife
Empty brakes always out-stop a load and cannot skid
Wet pavement increases trailer weight on the tandems
questions.explanation: Brake force that was sized for a load overcomes a light tire quickly. Once those wheels slide, the trailer loses sideways grip and can swing out or jackknife the combination. Brake earlier and more gently when you are light or empty, and do not add the hand valve.
questions.why: An empty trailer's stiff springs and strong brakes give poor traction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are bobtail, with no trailer, and a car stops hard ahead. What have tests shown about bobtail tractors?
options: They stop shorter than a fully loaded tractor-semitrailer
They take longer to stop than a fully loaded tractor-semitrailer
A bobtail has no brake lag and should stop like a car
Their brake linings double in size without a trailer
questions.explanation: CDL manual 6.1.3: bobtails "can be very hard to stop smoothly. It takes them longer to stop than a tractor-semitrailer loaded to maximum gross weight."

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The trailer is sliding out to the side and the trailer wheels are locked. What is the correction?
options: Set the tractor parking brake and hold the foot valve down
Accelerate while holding the trailer brakes locked
Release the brakes so the trailer tires can roll and regain traction
Apply the trailer hand valve harder to drag the trailer straight
questions.explanation: A trailer skid is a traction problem at the trailer tires. More brake keeps them sliding and the trailer keeps swinging. Release, let them roll, and then brake smoothly if you still need to slow. The hand valve is the wrong tool in this skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The drive wheels locked and the tractor is swinging around toward the trailer. What is this called, and what do you do?
options: A trailer swing: add hand-valve pressure until the drive tires grab
A rollover: hold the parking brake so the springs finish the stop
Offtracking: steer the opposite way and keep the wheels locked
A jackknife: release the brake and steer
questions.explanation: When the drive tires slide, the tractor hinges at the fifth wheel and tries to catch the trailer. Release the brake so those tires can roll and steer. Point the tractor where you want the combination to go. Adding trailer brake on top of a drive-wheel skid does not straighten the hinge.
questions.remember: Drive wheels locked? Release the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A trainer says that if the combination starts to fold, the hand valve will straighten it. Why is that the wrong rescue?
options: More trailer-only braking can lock the trailer or keep a skid going
The hand valve releases the fifth wheel and lets the pin self-align
The hand valve shifts weight onto the steer axle and ends a jackknife
Hand-valve braking is the required ABS method in a skid
questions.explanation: The trolley valve is a test tool, not a skid corrector. Trailer swing wants the trailer wheels rolling. A tractor jackknife wants the drive wheels rolling and the tractor steered where you want to go. Extra trailer brake is how folds get worse. It is not the fix.
questions.remember: Never fix a skid with the hand valve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are coupling a second trailer with a converter dolly. The dolly fifth wheel is on the second kingpin, but you have not checked the pintle. What still has to be true?
options: Air lines are optional on the dolly
Lock the pintle, secure chains, connect lines
The pintle may stay open if the dolly fifth wheel clicked
Safety chains replace a locked pintle on a short run
questions.explanation: Doubles have a coupling at every joint. The dolly's fifth wheel must be a real kingpin lock, jaws on the shank, and the tongue must be locked in the pintle with the latch or chains secured. Then air and the electric cord have to be on, shutoffs open, and the dolly legs up. Inspect every one of those points.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The rear shutoff valves on the lead trailer are still closed after you hook the dolly lines. What will the second trailer do?
options: Closed valves shorten rearward amplification
The second trailer uses tractor hydraulic brakes when the valves are closed
It will not get air, so its brakes will not release and work normally
It will charge through the pintle hook without the valves
questions.explanation: Those valves exist so an unused rear glad hand does not dump the lead trailer's air. Once a dolly is coupled, the valves have to be open or the rear unit never charges. Confirm the rear brakes release and apply before you move. When you uncouple, close the valves before you open the glad hands.
questions.remember: Shut-offs open, except at the very back.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Nothing is coupled behind the lead trailer, and the rear shutoff valves are open with glad hands uncovered. What is the air system doing?
options: Nothing, because open rear valves only matter on triples
Building extra pressure for the tractor through the open hands
Automatically setting the converter-dolly legs
Bleeding air out of the open lines
questions.explanation: Open valves at an unused rear connection are a leak. Close them and cap or couple the glad hands when no dolly is there. Open them only after the next unit's lines are actually connected. Bleeding at the open rear lines, which can empty the trailer brakes you still need.
questions.remember: Shut-offs open, except at the very back.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The dolly landing leg is still down as you prepare to enter the street with a set of doubles. What has to change first?
options: Raise and secure the dolly support
Leave the dolly leg down a few inches to limit crack-the-whip
The dolly leg is a spare tire carrier and does not touch the road
Only the lead trailer's legs matter
questions.explanation: A dolly leg on the pavement will catch the first bump or crossing. It is part of the combination inspection, along with the pintle latch, the dolly fifth-wheel lock, and the lines. Do not roll until it is up and the handle is stowed. Raise and secure the dolly support, the same way trailer landing gear must be fully up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You need to put a set of doubles into a dock and a teammate says to back them in quickly while they watch from the passenger seat. What does good practice say?
options: The passenger's verbal guide replaces getting out to look
Avoid backing doubles
Doubles back more accurately at a higher speed
Backing doubles is safer if you hold the trailer hand valve on
questions.explanation: Two articulations make a backup unpredictable, and the rear trailer can head somewhere the cab never pointed. The manual's bias is to avoid the move. If there is no other way, creep, use a spotter who is visible, and stop to look. Do not keep feeding a wrong angle. If you must, go very slowly, watch every trailer, and get out to look.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You have to back a single trailer into a dock and both sides are available. Which side do you choose, and why?
options: Either side, because offtracking is the same in reverse
The side with less room
The driver's side
The blind side
questions.explanation: Backing toward the driver's side puts the trailer where you can see it out the window and in the left mirror. A blind-side back hides the trailer's path. Use the sight side when the lot lets you choose. You still get out and look.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The dock is crowded, you have no spotter, and you cannot see the space behind the trailer from the cab. What belongs in the plan before the wheels turn?
options: A faster back so you spend less time in the hole
The trailer hand valve held on to stiffen the trailer
A swing into opposing traffic to get a better angle
A goal, a straight path, and a walk-around
questions.explanation: Backing without a target is how trailers meet doors, people, and other trucks. Straighten the combination when you can, because a bent combination in reverse keeps bending worse. Get out and look. A horn and a hope are not a look. A goal for where the trailer must end, a straight path if you can make one, and a walk to look behind you.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A bridge ahead is posted with a clearance, and your trailer has a reefer unit on the nose. What does that posted number limit?
options: A number you may exceed by a few inches if you straddle the center line
Cars only; combinations use the height on the registration card instead
The highest point on the combination, including the reefer
Only the trailer floor height
questions.explanation: Posted clearance is the limit for whatever is tallest on the vehicle. A reefer, a tarp bow, or an exhaust stack counts. If you are not sure you fit, stop and check. Do not guess and do not assume the sign is conservative.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your measured height is an inch under the posted clearance, but the pavement into the bridge is rutted and you are not sure the sign matches this approach. What now?
options: Proceed because an inch on paper always survives a rut
Proceed in the center at a higher speed so you bounce under
The inch is a cushion the sign already subtracted for trucks
Stop and check
questions.explanation: Signs can be wrong after a repave, and a rut or a crown changes the gap. The rule is the posted limit for your highest point, and if you are not sure you clear it, you stop and find out. Scraping a bridge is not a low-speed option. Being unsure means you do not guess your way under.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A railroad crossing is clear of trains, but your combination would still be across the rails if you had to stop on the far side. What do you do?
options: Do not start across until the whole combination can clear the tracks in one move
Start across and stop on the rails if the far side fills up
Edge onto the rails and wait
Stop on the tracks to shift into a lower gear for the pull away
questions.explanation: A combination is long. If the far side cannot hold all of it, you will sit on the crossing. Wait until there is room beyond the tracks for the entire vehicle. A train cannot swerve, and it will not stop for the part of you that did not fit.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You start over a crossing in the proper gear and then reach for a shift while the drive tires are still on the rails. Why is that shift a bad idea?
options: Neutral on the rails shortens the combination
A missed shift can stall you on the tracks
Shifting on the rails is required so the trailer does not offtrack
A shift charges the trailer air system for the crossing
questions.explanation: Cross in a gear that will pull the whole combination clear without a shift. A missed gear or a stall leaves the trailer sitting where the train will be. Do not start the crossing until that path is long enough, and do not change gears in the middle of it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: In a full lock turn in the yard, a line that was fine on the straight road pulls tight and tugs a glad hand. What does that tell you to change before the highway?
options: Disconnect the tight line and let it hang
Cross the colors so the longer hose is on the emergency fitting
Tie the tight line to the crank handle
Give them supported slack for a full turn
questions.explanation: Straight-line routing hides a short hose. The turn is the test. Support the lines so they are not crushed on the catwalk and not tight at full articulation. Then check them again. A glad hand that separates in a corner applies the trailer springs in traffic. Give the lines enough supported slack for a full turn so they cannot pull apart, without letting them drag.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The kingpin lock looks good, the legs are up, and the crank handle is still hanging beside the trailer tires. Why is that handle part of the go or no-go decision?
options: A loose crank can swing into the tires, the ground, or another vehicle
A hanging crank is the safety latch for the fifth wheel
The crank must hang free so you can hear it if the legs drop
Handles are stowed only on converter dollies
questions.explanation: The manual's finish to raising the gear is the handle in its keeper. A spinning crank is a projectile and a snag. Secure it before you move, every time, including after a yard adjustment of the legs.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You coupled, tugged, and looked: no gap, jaws on the shank, latch on. On the road the steering feels notchy when the trailer pivots. What maintenance item is the likely cause?
options: Trailer tandems that are locked in the holes
A fifth-wheel plate that was left dry
Jaws that are on the shank, which always make the steer heavy
Too much slack in air lines that are not dragging
questions.explanation: A locked couple should still pivot on grease. A dry plate fights the turn and wears the metal. If the feel is a bind at the fifth wheel, park and deal with the plate. Do not keep driving a coupling that will not rotate freely. The trailer binds instead of turning smoothly.
questions.why: A dry fifth wheel plate can cause steering trouble from friction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A converter dolly's pintle latch is down, but the drawbar eye is sitting on top of the hook instead of in it. What will a pull do?
options: Separate the dolly from the lead trailer
Seat the eye automatically once you reach highway speed
Bend the eye into the hook
Transfer the second trailer onto the tractor fifth wheel
questions.explanation: The eye has to be in the hook, the latch closed, and the safety device in place. An eye resting on the horn of the pintle will drop off at the first bump. Look at it. Do not take a dolly onto the road because the handle moved. The eye was never locked in the hook.
questions.remember: Drawbar eye onto the pintle hook.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You finish hooking doubles and the second trailer's ABS lamp stays on after the check. The tractor lamp went out. Why does the rear lamp still matter?
options: Rear ABS lamps are required to stay on while the combination is moving
That trailer's ABS may not work, and it is the least stable
Only the tractor lamp counts on a combination
A trailer lamp that stays on means the pintle is locked
questions.explanation: ABS on the last trailer is part of how a doubles or triples set stays straight in a hard stop. A lamp that stays on means you should not count on that unit to modulate, and it needs service. Do not unplug it to darken the lamp. Ordinary brakes should still work, but the whip at the back is worse without ABS. That trailer's ABS may not work, and the rear trailer is already the one most likely to lose control in a swerve.
questions.remember: ABS lamp stays on? ABS may be lost.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The lead trailer is loaded and the rear trailer of a set of doubles is empty. You have to brake hard on a wet road. Which unit is the more likely to lock and start a problem?
options: Neither, because doubles share one set of wheels
The tractor steer axle
The empty rear trailer
The loaded lead trailer
questions.explanation: Light weight plus rearward amplification is a bad pair. The empty rear trailer can lock and swing while the loaded lead trailer still has grip. Brake early, keep applications smooth, and do not use the hand valve to 'settle' the empty trailer. Light wheels lock first and the whip is greatest at the back.
questions.why: An empty trailer's stiff springs and strong brakes give poor traction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A low bridge is on the planned route and a tight right turn is on the same block. You know the trailer height clears the bridge. What else can still make this block the wrong route?
options: Offtracking on the turn can still hit things
Height clearance includes the turning path
Offtracking only happens on left turns
A trailer that clears a bridge cannot be long enough to offtrack
questions.explanation: Height and path are different limits. Posted clearance does not tell you the trailer will track inside the turn. Know the length and the tandem setting before you commit. If either the bridge or the corner is a guess, stop and check or take another route. Offtracking on the tight turn can put the trailer into a pole, a parked car, or the corner even when the roof clears.
questions.why: Wide turns and off-tracking can hit vehicles and objects.
questions.remember: Big rig turns: watch the rear wheels.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are lining up to couple and the upper coupler is bent so the apron will not sit flat on the fifth wheel. Why will a 'good enough' tug still be a bad idea?
options: Daylight under a bent apron is the normal running clearance
The electrical cord flattens the apron once it is plugged in
A bent apron will not seat with no daylight
A bent apron greases itself and locks more deeply
questions.explanation: The no-daylight rule assumes a flat apron on a flat plate. If the nose is bent, you can have a click and a gap at the same time. That is not a couple. Reject the trailer. The jaws cannot be trusted even if something clicks.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A railroad crossing has a hump, and the combination is long and low between the tractor and the trailer tandems. The posted height on a nearby bridge is not your problem here. What is?
options: You should shift gears on the hump to lift the middle
The middle can hang up on the hump
Humps only affect bobtails
If the tractor clears, the trailer has already cleared
questions.explanation: Know the length and the ground clearance of this equipment before you commit. A crossing that a car floats over can belly a long trailer. If you are not sure, stop and look, or take another crossing. Do not find out by straddling the rails. The middle of the combination can hang up on the hump even though both ends clear the rails.
questions.remember: Humped crossing? Don't risk hanging up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You have room for the tractor beyond a crossing and no room for the trailer. Traffic behind is honking. Why do you still wait?
options: The trailer may stop on the tracks if the tractor is clear
You should shift on the tracks to gain the extra length
The whole combination has to clear
Honking means you may stop on the rails as long as you are in gear
questions.explanation: Length is not negotiable in the moment. If the far side cannot hold the tractor and the trailer, you are choosing to occupy the crossing. Wait until it can. Do not change gears on the rails while you try to creep clear. The whole combination has to clear, and pressure from traffic does not shorten the trailer.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The combination is in a curve on a ramp and you feel the need to brake firmly. You did not slow before the ramp. What risk are you now managing late?
options: Low-speed offtracking only, which a firm brake cancels
A fifth-wheel unlatch, which braking prevents
Nothing, if the trailer is on sliding tandems
A rollover, which starts more easily in a curve
questions.explanation: Speed belongs in the approach, not in the middle of the ramp. Braking in the curve transfers weight and can start the roll you were trying to avoid, especially with a high load or with doubles at the rear. Next time, scrub the speed on the straight road. A high-center-of-gravity rollover, which begins more easily once you are already in the curve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During coupling the glad-hand seals look cracked, and you can hear a leak as soon as the trailer is supplied. The kingpin lock itself is fine. What still holds you in the yard?
options: A kingpin lock cancels an air leak
Cracked seals are normal and quiet down after a few miles
Leave with the red valve pulled out so the leak stops and the trailer brakes drag
Do not move a combination that is leaking at the air connection
questions.explanation: Colors matched on bad seals still leak. The trailer may not hold the springs off, and the leak test will fail. Put in good seals, support the lines, and confirm the trailer charges and releases. Dragging sprung trailer brakes is not a workaround. Replace the seals and recharge.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You backed under far enough to hear a click, then you connected the electric cord and called the couple done. You never looked at the jaws and never pulled against the pin. What is missing?
options: A tug test and a look at the jaws and latch
Nothing, because the cord powers the lock
Only the landing gear crank, which can stay loose
A high-speed road test instead of a yard tug
questions.explanation: Electricity does not hold the trailer on the tractor. The manual's proof is mechanical: brakes set, a gentle pull, no daylight, jaws on the shank, lever and latch seated. Do those before the legs come all the way up and you leave.
questions.remember: Tug test: pull gently, trailer brakes on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The combination is legal on the scale and the couple is latched. A tight toll booth ahead has a curb on the right and a concrete island on the left. How do you approach?
options: Use the hand valve to shorten the trailer for the booth
Slow down and leave room for offtracking
Aim the tractor through and let the trailer choose a path
Swing left into the next booth's lane as the default
questions.explanation: Booths and gates are low-speed offtracking traps. The trailer will cut inside whatever path the tractor used. Set up straight, go slowly, and watch the trailer tires in the mirrors. If you are not sure the width works, stop and get a ground guide instead of clipping the island. Slow before the booth and leave room for offtracking so the trailer does not climb either curb.
questions.why: Wide turns and off-tracking can hit vehicles and objects.
questions.remember: Big rig turns: watch the rear wheels.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The dolly fifth wheel on a set of doubles shows a gap under the second trailer, and the pintle latch on the lead trailer is secure. Is the set ready?
options: No. A gap at the dolly means a bad couple
Yes. The pintle is the only load-bearing coupling on doubles
Yes. A gap at the dolly is normal because dollies are shorter
No need to check the dolly jaws if the second trailer ABS lamp is out
questions.explanation: The dolly repeats the fifth-wheel rules: no daylight, jaws on the shank, latch on, legs up. A good pintle does not repair a bad kingpin lock behind it. Inspect every coupling, then the air, the electric, and the shutoff valves.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A new driver asks which coupling to inspect on a triples set. How many places deserve the same kingpin or pintle check?
options: Only the rearmost pintle
None, if the shutoff valves are open and the gauges are up
Every coupling on the set
Only the tractor fifth wheel
questions.explanation: Triples fail at whichever joint you did not look at. Each fifth wheel needs jaws on a shank, no gap, and a latch. Each pintle needs the eye in the hook and the safety device on. Air, electric, and legs get the same full treatment. Rearward amplification makes a missed latch on the back unit the one you feel last.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Proper couple, legs fully up, crank stowed, lines supported, lamps working, pins in. You are about to enter a highway curve posted well below your current speed with a tall, heavy load. What is the last combination skill that still decides whether you roll?
options: Slow before the curve
Hold this speed
Apply the trailer hand valve through the curve to stiffen the fifth wheel
Slide the tandems in the curve to lower the load
questions.explanation: Coupling keeps the trailer attached. It does not change physics in a ramp. High freight and speed are the rollover pair. Scrub speed on the straight approach. Do not brake late and do not steer sharply just because the jaws are latched. A legal couple does not keep a high center of gravity upright if you are too fast.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The combination's path through a curve is smooth and legal, and then a small steer correction becomes a quick flick because you were late seeing a pothole. On a triple, what can that flick do?
options: Nothing, because a pothole correction is too small to amplify
Shorten brake lag on the steer axle only
Lock the pintle
Crack the whip and roll the rear trailer
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification does not require a large steer at the wheel. A sharp input grows at each trailer. Triples are the worst. The cab can feel routine while the last trailer is already on its side. Smooth is a coupling and handling rule, not a style choice. Crack the whip and overturn the rear trailer even though the tractor only moved a little.
questions.why: A sudden steering move can tip your trailer over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Loaded trailer, firm level ground, tractor in line, trailer brakes set, and you have backed slightly to ease the jaws. The next crank turns are in low gear until the legs carry weight. Why low gear specifically?
options: The gear range does not matter if the pintle is latched
Low gear gives the leverage to lift a loaded nose
High gear is for the loaded turns and low gear is only for empty trailers
Low gear slides the tandems while you crank
questions.explanation: Landing-gear gearboxes exist so you do not lift a loaded trailer in the fast range. Start in low under the load, then use high only after the weight is off the mechanism, such as when you are finishing a raise with the legs already unloaded. Extra turns after firm contact, on a loaded drop, are what actually transfer the nose onto the legs.
questions.remember: Landing gear down, then a few extra turns.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: All mechanical locks check out on a single trailer, and you are about to take a downhill ramp you have never driven. The freight is tall. Which two combination facts decide the entry speed?
options: The ramp cancels offtracking, so speed is unlimited if the couple is latched
Tall freight is more stable
Slow before the ramp; tall loads roll easily
Enter at highway speed and snub with the hand valve in the curve
questions.explanation: A good couple keeps the trailer attached to you while you roll it over. It does not add stability. High freight and a curve want their speed set on the approach. Doubles and triples add crack-the-whip on top of that. Do not wait for the cab to feel loose. Slow before the ramp, and remember a high center of gravity can roll even when the fifth wheel is perfect.
questions.why: High trucks can roll over even at the posted curve speed.
questions.remember: Top-heavy? Slower than the curve sign.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A driver plans to park a combination overnight by leaving the trailer hand valve applied and the tractor engine off. Why will that not hold the trailer?
options: The hand valve uses service air and is not a parking brake
The hand valve cages the springs in the applied position
An engine-off hand valve becomes the red supply control
Service air in the hand valve lasts as a parking brake for several days
questions.explanation: Parking is the spring brakes: yellow valve for the tractor, red supply dumped for the trailer, on firm ground, wheels chocked if there are no springs. The trolley valve only applies trailer service brakes while air and the valve say so. It is a test control. Do not go to sleep on it.
questions.why: All the air could leak out and release the brakes.
questions.remember: Never park with the hand valve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Someone tells you to hook the second trailer by setting the dolly fifth wheel on the kingpin head if the shank is hard to reach. How do you answer?
options: Agree; dolly kingpins are designed to be caught by the head
Agree if the pintle latch is on
The head is acceptable on an empty second trailer only
Refuse; the jaws must lock the shank
questions.explanation: A false latch on the head drops trailers, including the second trailer in a set. There is not a looser standard for a dolly. No daylight, jaws on the shank, latch seated, then the pintle, the air, the electric, the shutoffs, and the dolly leg. Refuse; dolly jaws have to lock the shank, with no gap, the same rule as the tractor fifth wheel.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The combination is straight, brakes are tested, and a railroad gate ahead is up. You cannot see far enough down your side of the train's approach, and the trailer is long. What is the combination-specific rule you still obey?
options: Shift to a higher gear on the rails so the long trailer clears faster
Wait until the whole rig can clear
A raised gate means the trailer may stop on the rails
Long trailers are exempt if the tractor cab has crossed the first rail
questions.explanation: Gates and lights do not shrink the trailer. If you cannot clear the far side, or you cannot cross without a gear change, you wait. A raised gate is not a promise that a second train or a stalled pull will spare the part of the combination still on the rails. Do not start across unless the whole combination can clear, and do not shift on the tracks even if the gate is up.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Pre-trip on the combination finds the fifth wheel greased, jaws locked on the shank, no daylight, latch on, legs up, crank stowed, lines matched and supported, cord in, lamps good, and tandem pins seated. Which road habit still prevents the most common combination wreck after all of that?
options: Use the hand valve as a second service brake in every turn
Swing left on every right turn now that the kingpin is locked
Slow for curves and leave room for the trailer
Hold highway speed on ramps
questions.explanation: Most of the hookup can be perfect and the combination can still roll over, whip, or offtrack into someone. Speed goes down before the curve. Lane changes stay smooth, especially with doubles or triples. Turns stay wide enough for the trailer, without giving a car the inside and without taking the oncoming lane when you can avoid it. Slow before curves and ramps, steer smoothly, and leave room for the trailer's different path.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A forty-foot straight truck is rolling at 35 mph on dry pavement. What following time does the CDL rule of thumb call for?
options: Three seconds, because every vehicle uses the passenger-car rule
One second total
Two seconds, counted only for the cargo body and not the cab
At least four seconds, one second for each ten feet of vehicle length
questions.explanation: Under 40 mph the manual uses one second for each ten feet of length. A forty-foot truck therefore needs at least four seconds, which is not the car's three-second rule.
questions.remember: A second per 10 feet of length, plus a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: That forty-foot truck later cruises at 55 mph on dry pavement. How should the following gap change?
options: Add one second, for at least five seconds total
Keep four seconds
Drop to three seconds, the usual highway gap for a car
Double the gap to eight seconds for every ten feet of length
questions.explanation: Above 40 mph, add one second to the length-based count. Four seconds for a forty-foot truck becomes at least five seconds on a dry road. Speed is over 40 mph.
questions.remember: Longer truck, longer gap; add a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Rain begins while a sixty-foot combination is already traveling over 40 mph. What gap fits the rule of thumb?
options: A shorter gap so cars cannot cut into the space
At least seven seconds for length and speed, then still more
The dry-road minimum
A three-second car gap, which covers any truck in the rain
questions.explanation: A sixty-foot vehicle needs six seconds under 40 mph and one more second above 40. Rain is a reason to add still more space. The pavement is wet.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Night has fallen and a fifty-foot truck over 40 mph is carrying a heavy load. What following time should you build?
options: The daytime dry minimum, with nothing added for night or weight
Whatever gap the car in the next lane happens to be using
Start from six seconds, then add more for darkness and the heavy load
Three seconds, because headlights show the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Fifty feet is five seconds, plus one second over 40 mph, which is six. Night and a heavy load each call for still more following time.
questions.remember: Longer truck, longer gap; add a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A twenty-foot truck is under 40 mph in dry daylight. Why might a three-second gap be the wrong lesson to take from that count?
options: Twenty feet requires ten seconds under 40 mph
Under 40 mph every truck must use exactly three seconds
Length does not matter under 40 mph, only the car rule does
Two seconds is the length rule here
questions.explanation: The CDL count is one second per ten feet under 40 mph. A twenty-foot truck needs at least two seconds. Do not replace that formula with a car's three-second rule.
questions.remember: A second per 10 feet of length, plus a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)
