questions.q: Your seventy-foot combination is under 40 mph on a dry, clear afternoon. Which following gap matches the length rule?
options: At least seven seconds, one second for each ten feet of the vehicle
At least three seconds, the most any commercial vehicle needs
At least one second total whenever speed is under 40 mph
At least fourteen seconds, two seconds for each ten feet
questions.explanation: Under 40 mph, leave one second of following distance for each ten feet of vehicle length. Seventy feet means at least seven seconds in these dry conditions.
questions.remember: A second per 10 feet of length, plus a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: That seventy-foot combination then runs faster than 40 mph in dry daylight. What is the new minimum from the rule of thumb?
options: Seven seconds, because the over-40 second applies only at night
At least eight seconds: seven for length plus one more for speed over 40
Six seconds, because higher speed lets you subtract one
Three seconds, because the extra second replaces the length count
questions.explanation: Above 40 mph, add one second to the under-40 count. Seven seconds for seventy feet becomes at least eight seconds when the road is otherwise dry and clear.
questions.remember: Longer truck, longer gap; add a second over 40.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A car is tailgating your trailer on a dry highway. How should that change the space you keep in front?
options: Close up on the vehicle ahead so the tailgater has to back off
Match the tailgater by leaving only one second in front
Move your gap down to the passenger-car three-second rule
Leave even more room ahead
questions.explanation: You cannot control the driver behind you. A larger gap in front lets you slow smoothly and reduces the chance the tailgater rear-ends the truck. Leave even more room ahead so you can brake gradually instead of slamming to a stop.
questions.remember: Cut off? Drop back and make room.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your disabled tractor-trailer sits on the shoulder of a divided highway. Where do the three warning triangles go?
options: About 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind the vehicle
About 10, 100, and 200 feet ahead of the tractor
All three triangles stacked against the rear bumper
One on the cab roof and two stored in the trailer
questions.explanation: On a divided highway, place the triangles behind the vehicle at about 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet so approaching traffic has a staged warning.
questions.remember: Divided road: triangles behind you only.

questions.q: The breakdown is instead on an undivided two-way road. How should those triangles be arranged?
options: All three triangles in the oncoming lane within arm's reach of the bumper
About 10 feet and 100 feet behind the vehicle, and about 100 feet ahead
About 10, 100, and 200 feet behind, the same pattern as a divided highway
Only one triangle, placed beside the driver door
questions.explanation: On an undivided two-way road, warn traffic from both directions: 10 feet and 100 feet behind you, and 100 feet ahead toward oncoming drivers.
questions.remember: Two-way road: triangles behind and ahead.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are setting the triangles at dusk on a divided interstate after the engine quits. Which device belongs farthest back?
options: A triangle kept in the cab until morning
A triangle placed beside the fuel tank only
The triangle about 200 feet behind the vehicle
The triangle about 200 feet in front of the tractor
questions.explanation: Divided-highway placement is behind the vehicle: about 10 feet, then 100 feet, then 200 feet. The farthest warning is the 200-foot triangle.
questions.remember: Divided road: triangles behind you only.

questions.q: Traffic still comes toward your disabled truck on a two-lane road. Why put one triangle ahead of the rig?
options: The ahead triangle is used only on divided highways
Oncoming traffic is never given a triangle
Place every device behind you even when traffic approaches from the front
Oncoming drivers need a warning about 100 feet in front
questions.explanation: An undivided two-way road uses triangles about 10 feet and 100 feet behind and about 100 feet ahead so both directions are warned. Only devices behind you.
questions.remember: Two-way road: triangles behind and ahead.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A cargo tank placarded for Class 3 flammable liquid is stopped beside the road. Why leave the fusees in the box?
options: Triangles are legal only in daylight, so flares must be lit at dusk
Fusees are safer than triangles beside a flammable tank
Burning signals must never be used around that tank
Flares are required any time a placard is on the trailer
questions.explanation: CDL manual 9.6.4 and 49 CFR 392.25: use reflective triangles or red electric lights. "Never use burning signals, such as flares or fusees, around a tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Flammable Gas) whether loaded or empty."
questions.remember: Flammable tank stopped? No flares near it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Ice covers the highway and the engine-brake switch is still on. What should you do before you need to slow?
options: Leave it on, because a Jake brake cannot break traction on ice
Select the strongest engine-brake setting for a shorter stop
Shift to neutral and let the engine brake work by itself
Turn the engine brake off so it cannot lock the drive wheels
questions.explanation: Do not use an engine brake on a slick road. It can lock the drive wheels and start a skid when you still need those tires to roll.
questions.why: A retarder on a slick road can make the drive wheels skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A light rain has left the pavement slick and the Jake brake is on its highest setting. What is the hazard?
options: The engine brake can lock the drive wheels on that slick surface
The Jake brake works only in first gear
Engine brakes add air-tank pressure whenever the road is wet
A Jake brake is required by law whenever it is raining
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slick enough for an engine retarder to break traction at the drive axles. Turn it off instead of using a high setting.
questions.why: A retarder on a slick road can make the drive wheels skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A city sign bans engine brakes, and the street is also wet. Why leave the Jake brake off?
options: Wet pavement makes an engine brake safer than the service brakes
It can lock the drive wheels on a slick road, and you must obey the posted ban
Engine brakes are required in cities and on every wet hill
A posted noise ban applies only to motorcycles
questions.explanation: Turn an engine brake off on a slick road so the drive wheels do not lock. A posted engine-brake ban is a second, independent reason to leave it off.
questions.why: A retarder on a slick road can make the drive wheels skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The grade is long and dry, and no sign bans engine brakes. How is that different from ice?
options: A Jake brake should be used only when the road is icy
An engine brake removes the need to choose a low gear
On a slick road leave the engine brake off
A Jake brake is illegal on every dry downgrade
questions.explanation: The slick-road warning is about lost traction. On a dry grade with no posted ban, an engine brake can help, but you still select a low gear before the hill.
questions.why: A retarder on a slick road can make the drive wheels skid.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A high, heavy van approaches a curving freeway ramp. How do you keep the combination upright?
options: Hold straight-road speed if the ramp pavement looks wide
Slow to a safe speed before the curve instead of braking after the trailer leans
Enter at highway speed and brake hard once you are in the ramp
Accelerate through the curve so the stacked freight stays planted
questions.explanation: A truck rolls more easily when the center of gravity is high and a curve or ramp is taken too fast. Slow before the curve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Freight is stacked high in the trailer, so the center of gravity is well above the axles. What does a fast curve do?
options: Rollover depends only on tire brand
Braking in the middle of the curve is safer than slowing early
It raises the chance of a rollover
It makes a high load more stable than a floor-loaded trailer
questions.explanation: High center of gravity plus too much speed in a curve or on a ramp is a classic rollover setup. Get the speed down before the turn starts.
questions.why: Weight loaded high makes a rollover more likely.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are entering a tight exit with a tall load. Where should the lower speed already be?
options: Held at highway speed until the apex, then cut with hard braking
Higher than your straight-road speed so the trailer tracks better
Left to the ramp itself while you coast in neutral
Established before the curve
questions.explanation: Slow before the curve. Waiting until the rig is leaned over in the ramp is how a high load rolls. Scrubbed off after you are already in it.
questions.remember: Slow and downshift before the curve.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A bridge ahead is posted with a clearance, and you are not sure your highest point will fit. What do you do?
options: Stop and check your height first
Continue if the trailer looks an inch or two under the sign
Treat the posted clearance as advice written only for cars
Assume every posted bridge is higher than the number on the sign
questions.explanation: Posted bridge clearance is the limit for your highest point. If you are not sure you fit, stop and check rather than trying to squeeze under.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You know the posted clearance but not today's height with the reefer unit and the antenna. What is the safe move?
options: Ignore antennas and reefer units when you figure vehicle height
Find your highest point and do not go under if you are not sure it clears
Guess and proceed
Count only the trailer floor
questions.explanation: Know your height, including equipment on top. The posted clearance is the limit. Uncertainty means stop and check, not a guess.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your measured height is above the clearance posted on the bridge. What is the limit you must respect?
options: You may proceed if you hug the center of the lane
Height signs are suggestions when traffic is stacked behind you
The posted clearance is the limit for the highest point, so do not try to fit
The posted number applies to the cargo floor only
questions.explanation: If your highest point is over the posted clearance, the sign controls. Do not try to squeeze under a bridge you already know is too low.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You think you might clear a low structure by a very small margin. What does the manual want instead of squeezing?
options: Accelerate so the suspension rises and the roof clears
Let air out of the tires and drive through without stopping
Follow a shorter truck and assume your height matches it
If you are not sure, stop and check rather than trying to squeeze under
questions.explanation: A posted clearance is a hard limit for your highest point. A tiny hoped-for margin is not a check. Stop and confirm before you commit.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Traffic is stopped on the far side of a railroad crossing. When may your long combination start across?
options: Only when the entire vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping on them
As soon as the tractor nose passes the first rail
Whenever the lights are dark, even if the trailer would stop on the rails
If you can pause the trailer on the crossing and wait for a gap
questions.explanation: Do not start over the tracks unless the whole vehicle can clear. Do not stop on the tracks, even when the warning lights are dark.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The crossing lights are dark, but cars are backed up beyond the rails. Should the combination start over?
options: Yes, if the trailer stops on the rails without blocking a gate
No, not if any part of the vehicle would still be on the tracks when you stop
Yes, if the tractor can reach the first stopped car
Yes, because dark lights mean trains are not using the crossing
questions.explanation: A clear signal is not permission to block the tracks. Start across only when the entire combination can get all the way off the crossing.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your vehicle is one the rules require to stop at railroad crossings. How should you handle this crossing?
options: Stop with the drive wheels already on the rails, then look
Shift gears while crossing so the engine does not lug
Stop, look and listen, then cross without shifting
Roll across without stopping
questions.explanation: If your vehicle must stop, stop where the rule requires, look and listen, and do not shift gears on the tracks. A missed shift can leave you stalled there.

questions.q: A placarded cargo tank that must stop is nearing the crossing. What is the right way to make that stop?
options: Stop only after the tank is already sitting on the rails
Skip the stop whenever no train is in sight
Shift through several gears while the tank is still on the crossing
Stop, look and listen, then cross without shifting
questions.explanation: Special railroad stops apply to the vehicles the rule names, including certain placarded tanks. Stop where required, look and listen, and do not shift on the tracks.

questions.q: You drive an ordinary straight truck that is not a bus, not placarded, and not a tank required to stop. What is still true at the tracks?
options: Cross only if the whole truck can clear
Ignore the crossing and hold highway speed
Stop on the rails if the road beyond looks busy
Crossing rules apply only after you can already see the train
questions.explanation: Not every straight truck has the special stop. You still must not start over unless you can clear, and you must not stop on the tracks.
questions.remember: Can't clear the tracks? Don't start.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A sign says hazardous materials must stop at the crossing. You are hauling unplacarded lumber in a straight truck. What applies?
options: The sign means unplacarded trucks should speed up and shift on the crossing
That special stop names the vehicles in the rule
Every commercial vehicle must stop on the tracks for a timed minute
An empty or lumber truck must stop with its wheels on the rails
questions.explanation: Hazardous-materials railroad stops and similar special rules apply to the vehicles named, not automatically to every CMV. You still must be able to clear the tracks. It does not by itself order every CMV to stop.
questions.remember: Buses and placarded hazmat stop at crossings.

questions.q: The bus ahead must stop for the crossing. Your truck is not in a must-stop class. What do you still avoid?
options: Any slowdown at a crossing that has no gate
Using a gear that lets you cross without a shift
Stopping or shifting on the tracks
Looking both ways
questions.explanation: Even when your truck is not one that must make the special stop, do not start across unless you can clear, and do not stop or shift on the tracks.

questions.q: While a must-stop vehicle is on the rails, the driver wants a lower gear. Why is that shift a bad idea?
options: Shifting on the tracks is the required way to build speed
Neutral is the safest gear to select while you are on the rails
The crossing rule requires two gear changes before you clear
Do not shift gears on the tracks
questions.explanation: If your vehicle is one that must stop, look and listen, then cross in a gear that does not require a shift. Do not shift gears on the tracks. A missed shift can leave the vehicle stalled in front of a train.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You drank alcohol and would go on duty in three hours. What does the on-duty alcohol rule require?
options: Do not go on duty yet
Three hours is enough
The four-hour rule applies only to passenger-bus drivers
Coffee and a full meal cancel the four-hour waiting period
questions.explanation: Do not drink within four hours of going on duty. Three hours is still inside that window, so you are not ready to go on duty.
questions.remember: No alcohol within 4 hours of duty.

questions.q: Dispatch wants you to log on ninety minutes after you finished a drink. How do you answer?
options: The wait applies only if you still feel impaired
You cannot go on duty until four hours have passed
Ninety minutes meets the commercial waiting period
There is no waiting period when the drink came with a meal
questions.explanation: The rule is four hours from the drink until you go on duty. Ninety minutes does not satisfy it, whether or not you feel the alcohol.
questions.remember: No alcohol within 4 hours of duty.

questions.q: A later test might read zero, but you had a drink only two hours ago and would go on duty now. Is the time rule still a problem?
options: No. The four-hour rule starts only after the truck is already moving
No. Two hours is the full federal waiting period
Yes. No drinking within four hours of duty
No. A zero reading erases the four-hour rule
questions.explanation: The four-hour ban is about when you drank, not only about a later number on a breath test. Two hours is not enough time before duty. Yes. Do not drink within four hours of going on duty, even if you expect a later test to read zero.
questions.remember: No alcohol within 4 hours of duty.

questions.q: A breath test reads 0.04 BAC as you are about to drive the CMV. May you take the trip?
options: Yes, because the CMV limit is the same 0.08 figure used for many cars
Yes, if the truck is empty and the trip is short
Yes, if another person holds the shipping papers
No. Do not operate a commercial vehicle at 0.04 BAC or higher
questions.explanation: The per-se CMV limit is 0.04. At 0.04 or higher you must not operate a commercial vehicle. Do not treat 0.08 as the CMV limit.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You feel steady, but the test shows 0.04 BAC. Why is feeling fine not a defense?
options: The per-se CMV limit is 0.04
Feeling fine raises the legal CMV limit to 0.08
The per-se number applies only when the driver feels drunk
0.04 is legal in a CMV whenever the shift is under a few hours
questions.explanation: Operating a CMV at 0.04 BAC or higher is prohibited on its own. How sober you feel does not raise that per-se limit, and 0.08 is not the CMV number. You may not operate at that level even if you feel normal.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A CMV test comes back at 0.06 BAC. Which description of the limit is accurate?
options: 0.06 is legal if the test was taken while you were in the sleeper
0.04 or higher prohibits operating a CMV, and 0.06 is over that per-se limit
The commercial per-se limit is 0.08, so 0.06 is still legal
Any result under 0.10 is legal in a commercial vehicle
questions.explanation: Do not operate a CMV at 0.04 BAC or higher. A 0.06 result is above that per-se limit. The CMV figure is not 0.08.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your BAC is 0.03, at least 0.02 and still under 0.04. What federal result follows for this CMV driver?
options: You may drive, because 0.08 is the commercial alcohol limit
Nothing happens until the reading reaches 0.10
You are placed out of service
You may drive, because out of service starts only at 0.04
questions.explanation: A BAC from 0.02 up to but not including 0.04 puts you out of service. The separate per-se ban on operating a CMV starts at 0.04.
questions.remember: Any alcohol on duty puts you out of service.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During a roadside check your BAC is 0.02 exactly. What alcohol rule applies?
options: Out of service for alcohol begins only at 0.08
0.02 is below every federal alcohol threshold for CMV drivers
You are out of service only if the medical card is also missing
A BAC from 0.02 up to but not including 0.04 puts you out of service
questions.explanation: The federal out-of-service floor you may use is 0.02. At 0.02, and up to but not including 0.04, the driver is out of service.
questions.remember: Any alcohol on duty puts you out of service.

questions.q: An officer says your BAC is under 0.04 but at least 0.02. Which label fits the federal rule?
options: Out of service for alcohol, while the per-se ban on operating a CMV starts at 0.04
Free to drive a CMV
A warning that applies only to drivers of passenger cars
A problem that starts only when the reading reaches 0.04 and not before
questions.explanation: From 0.02 up to but not including 0.04, the federal result is out of service. At 0.04 or higher you must not operate a CMV. 0.08 is not the CMV limit.
questions.remember: Any alcohol on duty puts you out of service.

questions.q: You are driving a CMV in moving traffic and want to read and answer a text. What does 49 CFR 392.80 require?
options: Texting is allowed if the phone stays below the window line
The texting ban covers buses
A one-word reply is allowed at highway speed
Do not text. Texting while driving a CMV is prohibited
questions.explanation: 49 CFR 392.80 prohibits texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle. Reading and answering a text in moving traffic is not allowed.

questions.q: Traffic is crawling, and you want to type a message while the CMV is momentarily stopped in that traffic. Does the texting ban still apply?
options: Yes. Texting is banned even in traffic stops
No. The ban lifts whenever speed falls below highway pace
No. Texting is allowed if the transmission is in neutral
The ban applies only when the CMV is a school bus
questions.explanation: Driving, for the texting ban in 49 CFR 392.80, includes being temporarily stopped by traffic. Do not type a message in that crawl. Yes. Texting while driving a CMV is prohibited, including during momentary traffic delays.
questions.remember: Stopped in traffic still counts as driving.

questions.q: You are tempted to type a dock address into a device while the CMV is rolling. Which rule covers that manual entry?
options: The ban applies only when the device is mounted
49 CFR 392.80 prohibits texting, including manually entering text into a device while driving
No federal rule addresses typing into a device in a CMV
Manual entry is banned only for drivers who hold a passenger endorsement
questions.explanation: Manually entering text while driving a CMV is texting under 49 CFR 392.80. Enter the address before you move, not while the truck is rolling.

questions.q: You reach for a handheld phone to place a call while the CMV is moving. What does 49 CFR 392.82 say?
options: Only texting is banned
The handheld ban applies only while you are hauling passengers
Handheld mobile phone use while driving a CMV is prohibited
A handheld call is legal if it stays under one minute
questions.explanation: 49 CFR 392.82 prohibits using a handheld mobile phone while driving a CMV. Pick up the handset and the call is not legal while driving.

questions.q: The truck has a hands-free setup, but you still lift the handset to your ear in traffic. What did you do?
options: Nothing illegal, because any phone use is legal once hands-free gear is installed
You broke only a courtesy habit
You broke a rule that applies solely when the truck is parked
You used a handheld phone, which 49 CFR 392.82 prohibits while driving a CMV
questions.explanation: Hands-free equipment does not make holding the phone legal. Handheld mobile phone use while driving a CMV is prohibited by 49 CFR 392.82.

questions.q: You want to hold the phone to your ear during a red light while still in highway traffic. Is that handheld call allowed?
options: No. Handheld calls are banned even then
Yes. A red light makes any handheld call legal
Yes, if you turn on the speaker while you keep holding the phone
Yes, because the rule bans texting and never bans handheld calls
questions.explanation: A temporary stop for a traffic light is still driving for 49 CFR 392.82. Do not hold the phone to make a call there. No. Handheld mobile phone use while driving a CMV is still prohibited in that momentary stop.
questions.remember: Stopped in traffic still counts as driving.

questions.q: A car cuts sharply in front of the truck and then slows. What is the professional response?
options: Tap the car with the bumper to make it move over
Drop back and rebuild the following gap
Close up and tailgate until the car changes lanes
Brake-check the car so the driver learns a lesson
questions.explanation: If you are cut off, drop back and rebuild the following gap. Brake-checking or tailgating to teach the car is how a close call becomes a crash.
questions.remember: Cut off? Drop back and make room.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After that cutoff your gap is only about one second. What should you rebuild toward?
options: No extra space
One car length, regardless of truck length or speed
The full CDL gap for your length and speed
A three-second car gap and nothing more, even in a long truck
questions.explanation: Rebuild the manual's gap: one second per ten feet under 40 mph, one more second over 40, and more for night, rain, or a heavy load.
questions.remember: A second per 10 feet of length.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Another driver brake-checks you and you want to return the favor. Why is that the wrong lesson?
options: A brake-check is the approved way to restore a following gap
Tailgating is safe when the truck has new brake linings
Teaching the car matters more than the space you keep ahead
Drop back and rebuild your gap
questions.explanation: Do not brake-check and do not tailgate to make a point. The safe response to a too-small gap is to drop back until the CDL following distance is restored. Teaching the other driver with a brake-check can cause a crash.
questions.remember: Cut off? Drop back and make room.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Service brakes are fading on a downgrade and an escape ramp is signed just ahead. What should you do?
options: Use the escape ramp rather than hoping the brakes will come back
Pass the ramp and look for a steeper hill to slow the truck
Shift to neutral and coast past the ramp entrance
Pull the parking brake at highway speed and stay in the travel lane
questions.explanation: If the brakes fade on a downgrade and an escape ramp is ahead, use the ramp. It is there for a truck that can no longer hold the grade.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The brakes smell hot, the grade is still falling, and the escape-ramp sign is in sight. Why take the ramp?
options: Using the ramp is a last resort you should skip if neutral is available
Fading brakes may not stop the truck
Escape ramps are only for passenger cars with failed brakes
A hot smell means the brakes are working better than they were at the top
questions.explanation: Heat fade means the service brakes are losing the grade. When an escape ramp is ahead, use it instead of coasting past in hope. The ramp is the designed way to get it stopped.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: There is no ramp yet, you are still near the top, and the dry grade ahead is long. What gear plan fits?
options: Pick the gear only after the truck is already too fast
Use a higher gear than the climb so the engine does not slow you
Select a low gear before the descent
Descend in neutral and ride the brakes the whole way down
questions.explanation: The safest gear on a long downgrade is chosen before the hill and is usually lower than the gear you would use to climb that hill. Select a low gear before descending, usually lower than the climb, so brakes are not your only control.
questions.remember: Downgrade: a lower gear than you climbed in.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The hill you climbed in a high gear is the hill you are about to go down. Which gear is usually safer for the descent?
options: A higher gear than the climb
Neutral, selected at the crest so the wheels roll freely
Whatever gear you happen to be in when the brakes begin to fade
A lower gear than the one you used to climb, chosen before you start down
questions.explanation: Choose the descent gear before the hill. It is usually lower than the climbing gear so engine braking helps and the service brakes are not ridden the whole way.
questions.remember: Downgrade: a lower gear than you climbed in.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Brake fade continues and an escape ramp now appears beside the grade. What changes in the plan?
options: Use the ramp
Skip the ramp until you have coasted in neutral
Use the ramp only when the truck is also on fire
Stop at the ramp entrance and walk away while the truck is still rolling
questions.explanation: A low gear chosen at the top is the first defense. If the brakes still fade and a ramp is ahead, use the ramp. It exists for a truck whose brakes can no longer hold the grade.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: At night an oncoming driver approaches while your high beams are on. When should you dim?
options: Leave the high beams on
Dim before your high beams hit the other driver's eyes
Wait until the two vehicles are side by side
Dim only after the other driver dims first
questions.explanation: Dim high beams for oncoming drivers before the beams hit their eyes. Do not wait until you are beside them, and do not make it a contest.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are close behind a car and your high beams fill that driver's mirrors. What should you do?
options: Flash the high beams until the car changes lanes
Switch every lamp off until the lane ahead is empty
Dim to low beams so you are not glaring in those mirrors
Keep the high beams on until the car speeds up
questions.explanation: Dim when you are following closely enough that high beams glare in the other driver's mirrors. Low beams are the correction, not a blackout.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: An oncoming driver flashes you because your high beams are already in their eyes. What should have happened sooner?
options: You should have switched to parking lights only
You should have turned the headlights completely off
You should have answered with a longer high-beam flash
You should have dimmed sooner
questions.explanation: Dim before your high beams hit the oncoming driver's eyes. A flash from that driver means you are already late. You should have dimmed before those beams reached the other driver's eyes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A driver ahead is squinting from lamp glare in the mirrors. What distance rule should you use for dimming?
options: Dim when the high beams would hit those mirrors
Dim only inside a made-up national distance of fifty feet
High beams may stay on until you are nearly touching the vehicle ahead
Mirror glare is only the other driver's problem to solve
questions.explanation: The manual point is to dim before high beams glare in another driver's eyes or mirrors. There is not a single national foot distance you must memorize for that moment.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You dimmed for an oncoming truck. Another vehicle is now close ahead of you in your lane. What second case calls for low beams?
options: Turn the headlights off when following
Dim when following another vehicle closely
High beams are required whenever you follow another truck
Dim only for oncoming traffic and never for traffic ahead
questions.explanation: There are two dimming cases: oncoming drivers, and vehicles you follow closely enough to glare in their mirrors. Use low beams in both.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You have just doubled your speed. What should you expect from the braking portion of the stop?
options: Braking distance stays the same if the drums are already warm
Braking distance gets shorter
Braking distance becomes about four times longer
Braking distance merely doubles with speed
questions.explanation: Doubling speed makes braking distance about four times longer. A modest increase in speed is a large increase in the distance the brakes need.
questions.remember: Double the speed: braking distance times four.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: At 30 mph the braking portion of a stop is a certain length. At 60 mph, what do you expect of that portion?
options: About the same braking distance
About twice the braking distance and no more
About half the braking distance
About four times the braking distance
questions.explanation: Speed doubled from 30 to 60 mph, so the braking portion is about four times longer. Plan the gap and the start of the stop for that growth.
questions.remember: Double the speed: braking distance times four.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why can a truck's total stopping distance be much longer than the braking distance alone?
options: Total stopping distance also includes perception, reaction, and brake lag
Total stopping distance is only the distance after the wheels lock
Brake lag is part of car stops and is not counted on trucks
Air brakes have no lag
questions.explanation: Doubling speed makes the braking portion about four times longer, and a truck's total stop also includes brake lag plus the distance used to see and react.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You press the air-brake pedal at highway speed. Why does the truck not start slowing at that instant?
options: Lag disappears once tank pressure is above cut-out
Brake lag while air flows to the brakes
The delay is only in your head and is not part of stopping distance
Air brakes apply the shoes before the pedal moves
questions.explanation: Air brakes do not apply instantly. Brake lag adds distance to perception and reaction distance and to the braking distance itself. Brake lag is the time air needs to flow to the brakes, and that distance is part of the total stop.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The air is just below freezing and a bridge deck looks wet while the approaches look drier. What should you assume?
options: A wet-looking deck is always liquid water
Black ice forms only where plowed snow is piled on the lane
Bridges freeze first, and the shine may be black ice rather than plain water
Bridges freeze last
questions.explanation: Black ice and bridges freeze first. Treat a wet-looking bridge in freezing weather as ice, and slow before you are on it.
questions.remember: Freezing and looks wet? Expect ice.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Shaded pavement and a bridge both look dark on a freezing morning. Where is ice likely to show up first?
options: Only in the sunny lane, never on a bridge deck
Black ice is limited to gravel mountain roads
Bridge decks stay warmer than the road and freeze last
On the bridge, which freezes first
questions.explanation: Expect ice first on bridges and in other early-freeze spots, and expect black ice when the pavement looks merely wet. On the bridge, which freezes before ordinary roadway, often as black ice you barely see.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fog has dropped visibility to a short distance and your high beams turn it into a white wall. Which lamps should you use?
options: Low beams, so the fog does not bounce bright light back into your eyes
High beams, because fog requires the brightest lamp you have
Parking lights only, while you hold highway speed
Hazard flashers as the only lights aimed down the road
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beams. High beams reflect off the droplets and reduce what you can see. Slow down and add following space as well.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You switch on every forward lamp, including the high beams, and the fog glows solid white. What change actually helps?
options: Use the trailer dome lights as your main forward lamps
Go back to low beams so less light is reflected into your eyes
Add spotlights aimed up into the fog
Drive with the headlights off and only the marker lamps lit
questions.explanation: Fog plus high beams creates glare you cannot see through. Low beams are the fog setting, along with a slower speed and a bigger gap.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The right steer tire blows out at highway speed. What is the first response?
options: Accelerate so the tire can reseat on the rim
Pull the parking-brake valve while the truck is still fast
Grip the wheel, ease off the power, and do not brake hard
Stamp the brake and steer for the shoulder immediately
questions.explanation: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel, ease off the power, and do not brake hard. A hard brake or a sudden swerve can take the rig out of line.
questions.why: Braking right after a blowout can make you lose control.
questions.remember: Blowout: hold the wheel, stay off the brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After the blowout the rig is slowing and still tracking straight. What do you do next?
options: Jerk the wheel toward the nearest exit ramp
Stop in the travel lane and leave the truck there with no further plan
Cross several lanes at once toward the median
Keep steering straight until speed drops, then pull off the road
questions.explanation: Stay straight while the rig slows, then pull off. The blowout procedure is grip, ease off, no hard brake, steer straight, and leave the road only after speed is down.
questions.remember: Then brake gently and pull off.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A trailer tire has blown, you have eased off the throttle, and the combination is still straight. What do you avoid until speed comes down?
options: Hard braking and a sudden lane change
A firm two-handed grip on the wheel
Staying in your lane while the truck slows
Pulling off only after the rig has slowed
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard and do not swerve while the tire is coming apart. Hold the wheel, ease off the power, track straight, then pull off once you have slowed.
questions.why: Braking right after a blowout can make you lose control.
questions.remember: Blowout: hold the wheel, stay off the brake.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The alley behind the customer is tight, and you cannot see the end of the backing path from the cab. What should happen before the truck rolls backward?
options: Skip the look
Get out and look at the path, and use a helper when you have one
Back faster than a walk so you spend less time in reverse
Choose a blind passenger-side back even when a driver-side setup is available
questions.explanation: Backing starts with getting out and looking. Use a helper when you can, and prefer a setup that lets you back toward the driver's side.
questions.why: There are blind spots you can't see.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A coworker will guide you to the dock. How should that helper be used?
options: Once the truck is moving, ignore the helper and finish from memory
Let the helper walk beside the drive tires where you cannot see a signal
Agree on signals, keep the helper in sight, and stop if you lose sight of them
Have the helper stand directly behind the trailer, out of every mirror
questions.explanation: A helper only helps if you agreed on signals and can see them. If the helper disappears, stop. Do not guess at the next command.
questions.remember: Agree on a stop signal first.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your helper steps out of the mirrors while you are backing toward the dock. What do you do?
options: Continue, using the last hand signal you remember
Keep backing as long as nobody sounds a horn
Finish quickly because a missing helper means the path is clear
Stop at once and do not move again until the helper is back in the agreed place
questions.explanation: Losing sight of the helper means stop. Backing on memory, or assuming silence means go, is how you hit a person or the dock.
questions.remember: Lose sight of the helper? Stop.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You can reach the same dock with either a driver-side or a passenger-side back. Which setup should you prefer?
options: Back toward the driver's side
Back toward the passenger side
Choose the side farther from both mirrors
Back only with the landing gear still on the pavement
questions.explanation: When you have a choice, prefer backing toward the driver's side. You can see the path better than on the passenger side.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You need to change lanes in heavy traffic. How should the turn signal be used?
options: Wait for one national foot-distance mark before you are allowed to signal
Signal early enough that others can react, then cancel it after the move
Signal only after half the truck is already in the next lane
Leave the signal on for the rest of the trip so the lane stays yours
questions.explanation: Signal early enough for other drivers to react, complete the lane change, then cancel. Do not rely on a single national foot distance for the signal.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The lane change is finished and the truck is straight in the new lane. What should the signal be doing?
options: It should be flipped to the other side as a courtesy flash
It should stay on until someone honks
It should be canceled
It should stay on to claim the lane against faster traffic
questions.explanation: An early signal lets others react. Once the move is done, cancel it. A signal left on is a false message about your next move.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A broker offers a placarded shipment and you do not have the hazmat endorsement. The trip is described as short. What do you do?
options: Remove the placards until you are past the scale house
Refuse it. Do not haul a placard load without the proper endorsement
Accept it and cover the placards with tape until delivery
Haul it, because placards are optional on a short trip
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle requires the proper endorsement and the hazmat rules. A short trip does not waive that. Do not cover or remove placards to hide the load.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The freight is already placarded and your license has no hazmat endorsement. What is still true if the shipper says the papers are simple?
options: The endorsement is the shipper's duty
You may haul it if the bill of lading says the placards are a mistake you can ignore
You still may not haul that placard load without the endorsement
Simple papers replace the need for the endorsement
questions.explanation: Do not haul a placard load without the proper endorsement. Paperwork that looks simple does not change the placards or the endorsement requirement.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You smell a leak from a hazmat trailer and a bystander tells you to open the doors for a look. What should you do?
options: Open both doors on the shoulder so the fumes can air out
Climb inside and tighten caps or tape the packages yourself
Drive into a tunnel so the leak is less visible to traffic
Do not open a leaking hazmat trailer
questions.explanation: Do not open a leaking hazmat trailer. Opening it can spread the release. Use the emergency response steps for the load and keep people away.
questions.why: Many people get hurt by touching hazardous materials.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Vapor is coming from a placarded trailer at the dock. Why refuse a request to crack the rear doors?
options: Opening a leaking hazmat trailer can make the release worse and expose people around you
Opening the doors is the standard first step for identifying every leak
Door seals are meant to be opened beside an active spill
A short look is safe if you hold your breath while you stand in the doorway
questions.explanation: Leave a leaking hazmat trailer closed. Do not open the doors to satisfy curiosity. Get the right emergency guidance for the commodity.
questions.why: Many people get hurt by touching hazardous materials.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Smoke is coming from the engine compartment and you can still steer. What is the first useful move?
options: Open the trailer doors to see if the freight is involved before you stop
Get the rig off the road if you can, then aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire
Keep driving to the terminal with the hood latched
Spray the extinguisher into the smoke above the flames only
questions.explanation: If you can, get the rig off the road before you fight an engine fire. Aim the extinguisher at the base of the fire, not at the flames floating above it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A small fire is burning under the hood after you have parked off the roadway. How should the extinguisher be aimed?
options: Into the cab, even though the cab is not on fire
At the tires first, even though they are not burning
At the base of the fire, where the fuel is burning
At the top of the smoke so powder can fall down later
questions.explanation: Aim at the base of the fire. Spraying only the flames or an uninvolved part of the truck wastes the extinguisher and leaves the source burning.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fire is burning in the cargo of a closed trailer, and the cab extinguisher cannot handle it. What should you do?
options: Open the rear doors so you can fight the fire from the doorway
Drive to a fuel stop and ask to borrow water
Stay in the trailer and smother the flames with the freight
Do not open the trailer doors
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors on a cargo fire. Opening them feeds the fire with air. Evacuate when the fire is more than you can safely fight.
questions.why: Opening the doors lets air in and can make a cargo fire flare up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A cargo fire is beyond a portable extinguisher. Someone tells you to cut the seals and open up. Why refuse?
options: Opening the doors feeds oxygen to a cargo fire and puts you in the path of the fire
Cargo fires should always be fought from inside the trailer
Seals are opened so the fire burns cleaner and goes out
A cargo fire is safe to fight once the truck is still on the travel lane
questions.explanation: Know when to evacuate instead of fighting a cargo fire. Do not open the trailer doors. Get people away and get help.
questions.why: Opening the doors lets air in and can make a cargo fire flare up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are ill, fighting sleep, and not fit to control the CMV. What does 49 CFR 392.3 require?
options: Fatigue is allowed whenever the log still shows hours remaining
Do not drive while illness or fatigue impairs your ability to operate safely
Drive anyway if the delivery window cannot be moved
The rule applies only after a crash has already happened
questions.explanation: 49 CFR 392.3 says not to drive a CMV when illness, fatigue, or any other cause makes it unsafe for you to operate. Hours left on a log do not cure that.
questions.remember: Too tired or sick? Don't drive.

questions.q: You are on duty, feverish, and nodding off before you even roll. What is the right choice?
options: Drive with the windows down as a legal substitute for rest
The rule allows an ill driver if a passenger agrees to stay awake
Stay parked. Do not drive ill or fatigued under 49 CFR 392.3
Start the trip and see whether the fever breaks
questions.explanation: If you are too ill or too tired to drive safely, do not go. 49 CFR 392.3 forbids operating a CMV in that condition.
questions.remember: Too tired or sick? Don't drive.

questions.q: Cars are piling up behind your slower truck on a multi-lane highway. Where should you put the rig?
options: Stay in the left lane at a steady slow speed
Ride alongside the truck next to you for several miles
Weave from lane to lane without a signal to break up the line
Move right and let faster traffic pass, and do not camp beside another vehicle
questions.explanation: When you are slower, move right for faster traffic. Do not camp beside another vehicle, where you block a lane and sit in a blind area.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You are the slower vehicle on a freeway with open lanes to your right. How should you share those lanes?
options: Keep right except when passing
Use the left lane so cars can pass you on the right
Pick one vehicle and stay next to it so you have a wind break
Change lanes often without signaling to keep traffic from packing up
questions.explanation: Slower traffic should move right and let others pass. Lingering beside another vehicle takes away an escape and hides you in that driver's blind spot. Keep right except when you are passing, and do not travel for a long time beside another vehicle.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Coasting in neutral down a long grade feels easier on the engine. Why is that a poor plan?
options: Neutral is required whenever you do not see an escape ramp
You give up engine braking and can overspeed
Neutral is the safest gear on any long downgrade
Coasting is the manual's preferred way to save the service brakes
questions.explanation: Do not coast down a grade in neutral. Pick the low gear before the hill, usually lower than the climb, so the engine helps hold the truck.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The drive wheels start to slide on a slick curve while you are still on the power. What is the first correction?
options: Set the parking brake to stop the skid immediately
Ease off the power without braking
Turn the Jake brake to its strongest setting to yank the truck straight
Accelerate so the spinning wheels scrub through the slide
questions.explanation: On a slick road, locked or braking drive wheels lose traction. Ease off the power, leave the engine brake off, and let the tires roll.
questions.remember: Drive wheels spin? Ease off the gas.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: This combination has working antilock brakes on all axles and you need an emergency stop on a straight, open road. How may you use the pedal?
options: Make the stop with the parking brake only
Shift to neutral and stay off the service brake
Fully apply the brakes and let the antilock system work
Use only the trailer hand valve for the stop
questions.explanation: CDL manual 5.4.2: with working ABS on all axles, "in an emergency stop, you can fully apply the brakes." Without ABS on every axle, brake as you always have.
questions.remember: ABS on all axles: brake fully, steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A merging car does not appear to see the trailer. How should you use the horn?
options: Give a light tap soon enough to be noticed
Lean on the horn and steer toward the car
Do not use the horn for any traffic warning
Flash high beams into the car's mirrors in place of any horn use
questions.explanation: A brief horn tap can make you noticed. An angry blast, or moving toward the car, turns a warning into a conflict. Signal early and leave room.
questions.remember: A light tap of the horn.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Kneeling beside the left steer wheel, you rock a 20-inch steering wheel and the rim moves well over two inches before the tires respond. What does that mean?
options: Extra play makes yard turns safer, so more movement is better
Over about 10 degrees is too much; repair it
Two inches of rim movement is the normal minimum and should be left alone
Steering play is checked only at the annual inspection
questions.explanation: More than about 10 degrees of steering-wheel play is excessive. On a 20-inch wheel that is about two inches at the rim. Repair it before you roll.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Free play at the steering wheel is more than about 10 degrees, with almost no movement at the steer tires. May you start the trip?
options: Yes, if you grip the wheel harder than usual
Yes, because 10 degrees is the smallest play a truck should have
No. Excessive free play has to be repaired before you leave
Yes, if you notice the play only while the truck is parked
questions.explanation: Steering play more than about 10 degrees must be repaired before the trip. Holding the wheel tighter does not remove the wear.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: On this 20-inch wheel the rim travels about two inches, then a little more, before the steer tires move. How do you treat that picture?
options: Treat two inches as a trailer-wheel limit that does not apply to the steering wheel
Apply the two-inch picture to any wheel size without using the 10-degree check
Accept any play that is less than a half turn of the wheel
Treat it as the manual's picture of excessive play, about 10 degrees, and repair it before the trip
questions.explanation: About two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel is about 10 degrees. Play more than about that is excessive and parks the truck until it is fixed.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A slight steering movement is clearly less than about 10 degrees and the tires answer right away. What does that amount of play mean?
options: It is not the excessive free play the manual tells you to repair before the trip
Any free play at all means the steering gear must be replaced before you move
Play under 10 degrees is more dangerous than a half turn of the wheel
Steering play is not something a pre-trip looks at
questions.explanation: The defect is play more than about 10 degrees, about two inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. A clearly smaller movement is not that excessive-play defect.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The steer tires stay still while the 20-inch wheel rim moves several inches. Lights and tires otherwise look fine. What holds you in the yard?
options: Add power-steering fluid and the play will disappear on its own
Excessive steering play must be repaired before the trip even when other items look fine
Fine tires and lights cancel any amount of steering play
Several inches of rim movement is the play you want for highway tracking
questions.explanation: Several inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel is well past about two inches, the picture of about 10 degrees. Repair that play before you start the trip.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Major-groove tread on a steer tire measures under 4/32 inch. What do you do with that tire?
options: Go if the other steer tire is deeper than 4/32 inch
The 4/32-inch rule applies only to trailer tires
Do not go. Steering-axle tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread
Go, because 2/32 inch is the tread rule on every axle including the steer axle
questions.explanation: Steering-axle tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Under that depth, the tire is not ready for the trip.
questions.remember: Front tires need the deepest tread.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: This steer tire shows 2/32 inch, a depth that would meet the rule on a trailer tire. Is the front tire legal to leave on?
options: Yes. Every tire on the truck uses the same 2/32-inch minimum
Yes. Steer tires are allowed to be smoother than drive tires
Yes, if the whole trip stays off the highway
No. Steer tires need at least 4/32 inch
questions.explanation: Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. The steering axle is stricter: at least 4/32 inch. A 2/32-inch steer tire is not enough.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Both front tires measure 4/32 inch in the major grooves, with no cuts, bulges, or fabric showing. What does tread depth alone say?
options: 4/32 inch meets the minimum tread depth for steering-axle tires
Steer tires must show at least twice 4/32 inch or they fail
4/32 inch is acceptable only on drive axles
Tread depth is not part of the steer-axle inspection
questions.explanation: The steering-axle minimum is at least 4/32 inch. At that depth, with no cuts, bulges, or fabric showing, tread depth itself is not the defect.
questions.remember: Front tires need the deepest tread.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A drive-axle tire is below 2/32 inch in a major groove. May that tire start the trip?
options: Yes, because drive tires may be bald when the trailer tires are not
No. Tires other than the steering axle still need at least 2/32 inch of tread
Yes. Only the steer tires have a tread-depth minimum
Yes, if the dual beside it is a new tire
questions.explanation: Other tires, including drive tires, need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Below that, replace the tire before you go.
questions.remember: Front tires need the deepest tread.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: That trailer tire measures 2/32 inch and shows no cuts, bulges, or fabric. What does the depth mean?
options: Any tire under a much deeper tread must come off before every trip
2/32 inch is illegal on every axle of a commercial vehicle
It meets the 2/32 minimum for non-steer tires
Trailer tires must meet the 4/32-inch steer-tire minimum
questions.explanation: Tires other than the steering axle need at least 2/32 inch. A trailer tire at that depth, with no damage, meets the tread minimum.
questions.remember: Front tires need the deepest tread.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Another trailer tire is under 2/32 inch in a major groove. What is the pre-trip decision?
options: Leave it, because only the steer axle has a tread rule
Leave it if the tire still holds air
Move it to the steer axle, where less tread is allowed
Replace it before the trip
questions.explanation: Under 2/32 inch fails a non-steering tire. Do not start the trip on that trailer tire, and do not solve it by moving a thin tire to the front. Tires off the steering axle need at least 2/32 inch.
questions.remember: Front tires need the deepest tread.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Sidewall damage shows a bulge on a drive tire that still has deep tread. What controls the decision?
options: A bulge means the tire is done
A bulge is normal on a radial and can be ignored
Bulges matter only when they are on the steer axle
Deep tread cancels sidewall damage
questions.explanation: Cuts, bulges, and fabric showing mean the tire is done. Tread depth does not save a tire with a bulge.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fabric is visible in a cut on a trailer tire. The rest of the tread still looks deep. What should you do?
options: Cuts count only in the tread grooves, never where fabric shows
Do not go on that tire
Tape the cut and leave if the tread is over 2/32 inch
Fabric showing is acceptable when the tire is part of a dual
questions.explanation: When fabric shows through a cut, the tire is finished regardless of how much tread is left. Replace it before the trip. Fabric showing means the tire is done.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Those dual tires on the same wheel end are touching each other. What is wrong with that setup?
options: Touching is a defect only when the tires are on the steer axle
A light contact between duals is required for stability
Duals must not touch each other
Duals are supposed to touch so they share the load evenly
questions.explanation: Dual tires that touch can rub, overheat, and fail. They must not touch each other. Fix the match or the spacing before you go. Correct the contact before you roll.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Radial and bias tires are mixed on the left drive axle. What does the manual say about that pair?
options: Mixing radial and bias construction on one axle improves wet traction
The ban on mixing applies only to the trailer, never the tractor
Bias and radial tires should be mixed on every axle
Do not mismatch radial and bias tires on the same axle
questions.explanation: Do not mismatch radial and bias tires on the same axle. Replace one so the axle is matched before you leave.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A recapped tire is mounted on the right front wheel of a bus. What does the manual say?
options: Recapped, regrooved or retreaded front tires are prohibited on a bus
Recaps are the preferred tire for the front of a bus
Recaps are banned on every axle of every commercial vehicle
A front recap is fine on a bus when the other front tire is new
questions.explanation: CDL manual 2.1.3: "Re-grooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on the front wheels of a bus are prohibited." (49 CFR 393.75(d) says the same for buses. For trucks, 393.75(e) restricts only regrooved front tires.)

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The tire shop offers a regrooved tire for a steer position and says the grooves look deep. Should you mount it there?
options: Regrooved tires are banned only on the trailer
No. Do not use regrooved tires on the front wheels
Yes. Regrooved tires are the preferred steering-axle tire
Yes, whenever the new grooves look deeper than 4/32 inch
questions.explanation: Deep-looking grooves do not make a regrooved tire acceptable on the front. The model manual says not to use regrooved or recapped tires on the front wheels.

questions.q: Rust streaks run outward from several lug nuts on a drive wheel. What might that mean, and what do you do?
options: Rust on the nuts means the tire is overinflated
Streaks mean the axle was aligned recently
The nuts may be loose
Rust streaks mean the nuts were painted at the factory and can be ignored
questions.explanation: Rust streaks from lug nuts can mean the nuts are loose. Check them, and do not leave with loose wheel nuts.
questions.remember: Rust at a lug nut? Check it's tight.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Shiny metal trails show in the rust around the lug nuts during the walk-around. What is the right next step?
options: Wash the wheel and leave
Remove two nuts so the wheel can center itself on the road
Ignore the wheel until the next scheduled service interval
Check those lug nuts
questions.explanation: Shiny or rusty trails from lug nuts are a clue the nuts may have moved. Check them before the trip rather than washing the clue away. The trails can mean they are loose.
questions.remember: Rust at a lug nut? Check it's tight.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After seeing rust streaks, you find a lug nut that turns by hand. May you start the trip?
options: No. A loose lug nut has to be corrected before you leave
Yes, if at least half the nuts on that wheel feel tight
Yes. Hand-tight is the normal state for dual wheels
Yes, if you plan to keep the truck off highway speeds
questions.explanation: Rust streaks told you to check, and a nut that turns by hand is loose. Do not start the trip until the wheel is properly secured.
questions.why: Loose or missing lug nuts can make you lose a wheel.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Engine oil sits well below the safe mark on the dipstick. What is the decision before you start out?
options: A low mark on the dipstick means the crankcase is overfilled
Do not start until it is at a safe level
Go, and plan to add oil at the next state line
Oil level is something you check only when the oil is changed
questions.explanation: Oil is a pre-trip item. A level well below the safe mark means you do not roll until it is corrected and you know why it was low.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Coolant is pooled under the radiator and the reservoir is low. What should you do?
options: Coolant puddles are normal after every shutdown
Low coolant matters only when the weather is below freezing
Do not go until the coolant leak is repaired and the level is safe
Top the reservoir off with water and leave while the leak is still running
questions.explanation: A coolant leak you can see, with a low reservoir, is a do-not-go defect. Fill-and-hope is not a repair.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Power-steering fluid is low and the hose at the steering box is wet. May you roll?
options: Yes. Power steering is optional once you are at highway speed
Yes, if the wheel can still be forced from lock to lock while parked
Add fluid in the morning and ignore a hose that stays wet
No. Fix the power-steering leak and restore a safe fluid level before the trip
questions.explanation: Power steering fluid and hoses are part of the pre-trip. A wet hose and a low level mean you do not start the trip.
questions.remember: Power steering: fluid full, hoses sound.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The air-compressor belt is cracked and fraying. Why does that belt decide whether you leave?
options: Do not go; you could lose brake air
The compressor belt can be missing if the fan belt looks new
A cracked belt is acceptable until it snaps on the highway
Compressor belts are looked at only during a brake overhaul
questions.explanation: The compressor belt drives the air supply. Cracked or fraying, it is a repair-before-trip item, not something you watch fail on the road. Do not go. A failing compressor belt can leave you without the air the brakes need.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Chunks are missing from a glazed belt that drives the charging system. What do you do with that belt?
options: A glazed belt charges the batteries better than a new belt
Replace it before the trip so charging works
Spray belt dressing on the chunks and leave
Belts are a roadside repair
questions.explanation: Belts are inspected before the trip. A belt with chunks missing cannot be trusted to run the charging system. Replace it before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A cut splits a coolant hose, but the hose is not dripping while the engine is off. Is that good enough to leave?
options: Tape the cut and start the trip
Cut hoses are normal on the heater circuit and can be ignored
No. A cut hose means do not go, even if it is not dripping at this moment
Yes. Only a hose that is spraying has to be repaired
questions.explanation: A hose that is cut is a do-not-go defect. Waiting to see it spray, or covering it with tape, is not the repair the pre-trip requires.
questions.why: A broken hose can cause engine failure, even fire.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: This heater hose is swollen and soft when you squeeze it. What is the pre-trip call?
options: A swollen hose is stronger than a new hose and should be left
Swollen hoses matter only when they carry air to the brakes
Soft hoses are acceptable whenever the day is hot
Do not go. A swollen hose is repaired before the trip
questions.explanation: A hose that is cut or swollen means do not go. Soft, swollen rubber can fail once the system is hot and under pressure.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Air is hissing at a hose fitting with the brakes released. What is the rule for a leak you can hear?
options: Do not start the trip until that audible leak is repaired
An audible air leak is normal at any tank pressure
Drive slowly and listen again at the end of the day
Leave it; audible leaks seal themselves once the truck is rolling
questions.explanation: A leak you can hear means do not go. Air that is escaping now can become a brake failure later in the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: One low-beam headlight stays dark while the other lamps look fine. May you leave because it is still daylight?
options: Tape a flashlight to the mirror and count it as the headlight
No. Repair the required headlight before the trip
Yes. Headlights are required only after sunset
Yes. One working headlight is enough if the marker lamps are on
questions.explanation: Required lights are a pre-trip item in daylight too. A dead headlight is fixed before you roll, not patched with a flashlight.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your helper presses the service-brake pedal and the left stop lamp stays dark. What do you do?
options: Brake lights are optional when the turn signals work
A dark stop lamp is legal on a trailer if the tractor lamps work
Fix the brake light before you enter traffic
Use hand signals for the entire trip instead of the lamp
questions.explanation: Brake lights are required lamps. If one stays dark, repair it before you take the truck into traffic.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A required rear reflector is broken and hanging by one fastener. What is the finding?
options: Reflectors are decorations and are not part of the inspection
A broken reflector is acceptable when the trailer is placarded
Reflectors are checked only during night stops
Repair or replace the reflector before you go so the vehicle can be seen
questions.explanation: Lights and reflectors are pre-trip items. A broken required reflector is repaired before the trip so others can see the vehicle.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The right-side mirror is cracked across the main view and loose on its bracket. What should happen before you roll?
options: Repair or replace the mirror so it is secure and you can see
Fold that mirror in and rely on the left mirror only
A cracked mirror is legal if you can see over the crack
Mirrors are adjusted only after you are on the highway
questions.explanation: Mirrors must be secure and usable. A cracked, loose mirror that ruins the view is fixed before you start the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Windshield damage crosses the driver's view of the road. The wipers still move. What is the call?
options: Tilt your head until the crack sits above your line of sight and go
Do not start the trip with windshield damage that blocks your view
A crack through the view is legal whenever the wipers still move
Windshield cracks matter only after dark
questions.explanation: The windshield is part of the pre-trip. Damage that blocks the driver's view is repaired before you leave, even if the wipers still sweep.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Driver-side wiper rubber is torn and smears the glass. Rain is in the forecast. What do you do?
options: A torn blade is fine if you wipe the glass with a sleeve at stops
Wiper condition is not part of a pre-trip inspection
Replace the blade before the trip so the windshield can be cleared
Wipers are optional when the washer tank is full
questions.explanation: Wipers have to clear the windshield. A torn blade that smears the glass is replaced before a trip, especially with rain coming.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Pressing the horn button produces no sound at all. May you go anyway?
options: Yes. A horn is only a courtesy in city traffic
Yes. Horns are tested only during roadside inspections
A dead horn is legal when the four-way flashers work
No. The horn has to work before you start the trip
questions.explanation: The horn is checked in the cab before you move. If it does not sound, repair it. Flashers do not replace a horn you may need.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Seat-belt webbing is frayed and the latch will not hold. What is required before the truck moves?
options: Repair or replace the belt so it will latch before the trip
Tuck the belt behind the seat and go without it
A seat belt is required equipment only on buses
Knot the ends together and treat the knot as a latch
questions.explanation: The seat belt is a pre-trip item. Frayed webbing or a latch that will not hold must be repaired before you start the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The extinguisher needle sits in the recharge zone instead of showing a full charge. What do you do?
options: Charge level matters only when the vehicle is a bus
Do not leave until you have a charged extinguisher appropriate to the vehicle
A discharged extinguisher still counts if the pin and seal are in place
Extinguishers are optional on property-carrying trucks
questions.explanation: Emergency equipment includes a charged fire extinguisher appropriate to the vehicle. A gauge in the recharge zone means it is not ready.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Nothing is clipped into the extinguisher bracket in the cab. What equipment is missing?
options: A spare tire, which replaces the extinguisher
Only a flare, which the manual accepts in place of an extinguisher
A charged fire extinguisher appropriate to this vehicle
Nothing important, as long as three triangles are on board
questions.explanation: You need a charged extinguisher appropriate to the vehicle, not an empty bracket. Triangles do not replace it, and flares are not the substitute.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Only two reflective triangles are in the rack and you cannot find a third. Is the emergency set complete?
options: Yes. Two triangles meet the requirement on any road
Yes. One triangle is enough when the highway is divided
Triangles are carried only when the load is placarded
No. You need three reflective triangles before the trip
questions.explanation: Emergency equipment includes three reflective triangles. Two is not a complete set. Find or replace the third before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fuse protection is what this truck uses, and the spare-fuse kit is empty. What is the defect?
options: Carry spare fuses before you go
