Spare fuses are required only on vehicles that use circuit breakers
Any piece of wire can stand in for a spare fuse
Fuses are checked only after one blows on the road
questions.explanation: If the vehicle uses fuses, spare fuses are part of the emergency equipment you confirm before the trip. An empty kit is not ready.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Circuit breakers protect this tractor, and it does not use fuses. What is true about spare fuses on this truck?
options: Breakers mean you may skip the lights, the horn, and the extinguisher
Spare fuses are required when the vehicle uses fuses
Every commercial vehicle must carry spare fuses even when it has no fuses
Circuit breakers have to be replaced with fuses before any trip
questions.explanation: Spare fuses are confirmed if the vehicle uses fuses. A truck that uses circuit breakers is not failed merely because there is no spare-fuse kit. As an extra rule for this breaker-equipped truck.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Daylight shows between the fifth wheel and the trailer apron. What does that gap mean?
options: Daylight there means the jaws are locked
Gaps are normal until the trailer is loaded
The trailer is not fully coupled
A visible gap is required so the trailer can pivot
questions.explanation: A fifth-wheel coupling should show no gap. Daylight between the fifth wheel and the apron means the trailer is not fully down. Do not leave.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fifth-wheel jaws stand open around the kingpin. May you pull away from the dock?
options: Yes. Open jaws let the kingpin find its seat while you drive
Yes, if the landing gear is already fully up
Jaws lock themselves once highway speed shakes the fifth wheel
No. The jaws must be locked before you move
questions.explanation: Jaws locked around the kingpin shank are part of a safe coupling. Open jaws mean you are not coupled. Do not pull out.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Neither the locking lever nor the safety latch is seated. The lever sits high and the latch hangs free. What is the coupling status?
options: Not safe to move
The latch is optional if the lever looks almost seated
A free-hanging latch is the sign that the jaws are locked
The lever and latch are checked only after the first leg of the trip
questions.explanation: The locking lever must be seated and the safety latch must be on. If either is free, the coupling is not ready and you do not move.
questions.remember: Safety latch over the locking lever.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Looking under the trailer nose, you see the kingpin sitting on top of the jaws. What do you do?
options: Raise the landing gear and the kingpin will seat while you turn
Do not go. The kingpin must not ride on top of the jaws
Drive forward hard so the kingpin drops into the jaws by itself
That position is the normal locked position of a fifth wheel
questions.explanation: If the kingpin rides on top of the jaws, the trailer is not locked into the fifth wheel. Stop and couple it correctly before any move.
questions.remember: Jaws on the shank, not the head.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The fifth-wheel plate is dry, with no grease on it. What should you correct before the trip?
options: Grease belongs only on the threads of the kingpin
Grease is used only when the trailer is a tanker
Put enough grease on the fifth wheel
Leave the plate dry so it grips the trailer better
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel needs enough grease. A dry plate is not a proper coupling inspection result. Grease it as the manual describes before you leave.
questions.why: A dry fifth wheel plate can cause steering trouble from friction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Trailer air lines drag on the catwalk and along the frame. What should you do before you move?
options: Let them drag so you can watch them in the mirror
Air lines are supposed to rest across the driveshaft
Dragging lines are better
Secure the air lines so they are not dragging or rubbing
questions.explanation: Air lines must be secured, not left to drag or chafe. Pick them up, check the connections, and stow them before you roll.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The electrical pigtail is unplugged and hanging beside the catwalk. What fails if you leave it that way?
options: Trailer lamps and signals will not work
The cord only charges a trailer refrigerator and can wait until the delivery
An unplugged cord is the normal way to set the trailer brakes for the trip
Electric cords are connected only after dark
questions.explanation: The electric cord has to be connected and secured. An unplugged pigtail means the trailer lights you depend on are not in the circuit.
questions.remember: Cord plugged in, safety catch on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Landing-gear feet remain on the pavement as you reach for a gear to pull away. What do you do?
options: Landing gear is raised only when you arrive at the destination
Raise the landing gear fully before you move
Leave the feet down a few inches so they can catch a dropout
Drag the legs
questions.explanation: Landing gear must be up before you move. Feet still on the pavement will dig in, damage the gear, or hang up as soon as you pull.
questions.remember: Landing gear all the way up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the legs fully up, the landing-gear crank is free to swing under the trailer. Why secure that handle?
options: The handle should drag so other drivers can see the trailer
Crank handles are removed at the shipper and not used again
A swinging crank can catch on things
A free crank is how you show the gear is still down
questions.explanation: Landing gear up includes keeping the crank from swinging into the road or the tractor. Secure the handle before you move.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A drive-axle leaf spring is cracked through. What is the suspension decision?
options: Cracked springs settle into place and are safe once the truck is warm
Only leaking shocks count as suspension defects
A cracked leaf is legal if the spring on the other side matches it
Do not go. A cracked spring is a defect that must be repaired first
questions.explanation: Cracked springs are suspension defects. Do not start the trip until that spring is repaired.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: From the side of the trailer you can see one axle shifted out of line with the other. What do you do?
options: Do not start the trip with a shifted axle
A shifted axle affects only fuel economy and can wait
Drive it; road speed will center the axle
Schedule the axle for next month and leave with it shifted
questions.explanation: A shifted axle is a suspension defect. It is not something you drive out or postpone. Repair it before the trip.
questions.remember: Axle out of line? Don't drive.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Spring U-bolts turn by hand where they should be tight. What can you do about that before leaving?
options: If the spring leaf is not cracked, loose U-bolts can wait
Do not leave
Loose U-bolts let the axle float
U-bolts are tightened only at an alignment shop once a year
questions.explanation: Loose U-bolts can let the axle shift. They are a pre-trip defect. Secure the suspension before you start the trip.
questions.remember: Loose U-bolts or torque rods? Don't drive.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Shock-absorber fluid coats the body of a shock from its own seal. What is the finding?
options: Leaking shocks are required equipment on a loaded trailer
Shocks are decorative
A leaking shock is a defect and should be repaired before the trip
Fluid on the shock body means the shock was just greased
questions.explanation: Leaking shocks are suspension defects. A shock wet with its own fluid is repaired before you go, not written off as grease.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Pushrod stroke on one chamber is longer than the adjustment limit published for that chamber size. What does the extra travel mean?
options: Extra travel means the brake is newer and will grip harder
One inch of travel is the legal stroke for every chamber, so ignore the chamber size
Pushrod travel is a suspension measurement
That brake is out of adjustment and must be repaired before the trip
questions.explanation: If pushrod travel is longer than the limit for that chamber, the brake is out of adjustment. Do not use one stroke number for every chamber type.
questions.remember: Pushrod past the limit? Something's wrong.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Brake-hose rubber is worn through to the fabric where it rubs the frame. What is the decision?
options: Fabric showing on a hose means the hose was built with that layer outside
Do not go. A damaged brake hose must be repaired before the trip
Wrap the worn spot with tape and recheck it next week
Worn hoses are safe when they are only on the trailer
questions.explanation: Brake hoses that are cut, rubbed through, or otherwise damaged are defects. Do not tape a hose and start the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Applied brakes hiss at a service chamber. You can hear the air escaping. May you leave the yard?
options: Yes, if the leak stops when you release the pedal and you avoid using the brakes
Chamber leaks matter only when the temperature is below freezing
No. A leak you can hear means do not start the trip
Yes. Chamber leaks are how the brakes cool themselves
questions.explanation: An air leak you can hear, including at a brake chamber, is a reason to stay parked until it is repaired.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: After a normal start the oil-pressure gauge stays at zero. What do you do?
options: Drive gently until the gauge wakes up
Oil pressure is optional when coolant temperature looks normal
A zero reading means the engine is fully lubricated
Shut down. Do not start the trip if oil pressure does not come up
questions.explanation: In the cab, oil pressure has to come up after start. If it stays at zero, shut down and do not begin the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The charging gauge shows discharge and does not recover after the engine is running. What is telling you to stay parked?
options: The charging system is not charging, so do not leave
A discharge reading is the normal sign of a healthy alternator
The air compressor is the only system a discharge gauge describes
Discharge means the batteries are already full and you may go
questions.explanation: The in-cab check includes the charging system. A gauge that stays on discharge means you do not start the trip.
questions.remember: Charging gauge in the normal range.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Tank pressure rises and then stops short of governor cut-out no matter how long the engine runs. What is the call?
options: Drain the tanks so the needle looks closer to the top
Do not go. Air pressure must build to cut-out
Cut-out is optional when the low-air light happens to be off
Any rise on the gauge is enough air to leave
questions.explanation: Air must build to governor cut-out. If it stalls short of cut-out, the system is not ready and you do not roll.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Neither a buzzer nor a warning light comes on when you test the low-air warning. May you go?
options: Yes, if the trailer-supply valve is pushed in
Low-air warnings are tested only at a shop once a year
No. The low-air warning has to work before the trip
Yes. The warning is only a courtesy if you can see the gauge
questions.explanation: The low-air warning is an in-cab item that must work. If the buzzer and light stay silent during the test, do not start the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Set the parking brake, then ease the truck against it. The truck rolls. What did the test show?
options: A parking brake is supposed to creep when you ease against it
The test counts only on a downhill dock
A working service brake means the parking brake can be skipped
The parking brake does not hold and must be repaired before you leave
questions.explanation: The parking brake must hold the vehicle. If the truck rolls when you ease against it, repair the brake before the trip.
questions.remember: Test the parking brake: low gear, gentle pull.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: During a slow roll in the yard the service brake pulls hard to the right. What should you do before the public street?
options: Stop and get the pull corrected
Enter traffic and let the pull wear itself even
A pull means the brakes are new and should be driven hard
Steering against the pull is the repair
questions.explanation: The service brake should stop the truck and should not pull. A hard pull in the yard is fixed before you enter traffic.
questions.remember: Truck pulls when braking? Brake trouble.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: This yard stop at low speed barely slows the truck. What is the decision?
options: Go ahead, because the low-air warning stayed quiet
Do not enter traffic
Use the parking brake as your service brake once you are on the highway
A weak low-speed test is normal until the drums get hot
questions.explanation: If the service brake does not stop the vehicle in the low-speed test, you do not enter traffic. Quiet gauges do not replace a brake that will not stop you.
questions.remember: Weak brakes in the yard? Don't go out.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: With the windows up you smell exhaust in the cab while the engine runs. What is the hazard and the decision?
options: Opening a window makes an exhaust leak legal for the trip
An exhaust smell only means the heater is working
An exhaust leak into the cab means do not start the trip
Cab exhaust is normal on a diesel and can be ignored
questions.explanation: Exhaust leaking into the cab can make you sick or drowsy. Do not start the trip until that leak is repaired.
questions.why: A broken exhaust can let poison fumes into the cab or sleeper.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A frame-rail crack is visible, and the truck is otherwise fueled and loaded. What do you do?
options: A frame crack is cosmetic when only the paint is broken
Frame cracks are allowed anywhere behind the cab
Drive it, because vibration will close the crack
Do not start the trip with a cracked frame
questions.explanation: Frame cracks are a do-not-go defect. Cargo and fuel on board do not make a cracked rail fit for the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Across a frame crossmember a weld has broken open. Is that a go item?
options: No. Broken welds mean do not start the trip
Yes. A broken weld is stronger than the original joint
Yes, if you plan to stay on smooth pavement
Welds are inspected only after a crash has already happened
questions.explanation: Broken welds, like frame cracks, mean you do not start the trip. A smooth road does not make a broken weld safe.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: One cargo strap hangs loose and the freight can shift toward the doors. What do you fix before you close up?
options: Leave one loose strap if the doors will be shut on the freight
The securement. Do not roll with a loose strap that lets the load move
Nothing. Loose straps tighten themselves once you reach road speed
Nothing. Securement is the receiver's job after you arrive
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you roll. A loose strap that lets freight move is corrected before the doors are your only backup.
questions.remember: Cargo secured so it can't shift or fall.

questions.q: The rear door latch is not caught, and the door stands slightly open. May you pull ahead?
options: Yes. Trailer doors latch themselves once the wind catches them
Yes, if a loose strap is leaning against the door
An unlatched door is legal when the shipper says the load is sealed
No. Latch the doors before you move
questions.explanation: Doors must be latched before you move. An open door can swing into traffic or let cargo fall out.

questions.q: Two tarp corners are untied and the cover is flapping. What do you do?
options: Tie the tarp before you go so it cannot tear free or uncover the load
Leave it. A flapping tarp is the required way to ventilate freight
Tie tarps only when rain is certain to fall on the trip
Cut the loose ropes off and haul the tarp unsecured
questions.explanation: Tarps have to be tied. A flapping corner can rip the cover off or let cargo escape. Tie it before you roll.
questions.why: A flapping cover can tear loose and block your view or someone else's.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Hub oil runs down the wheel and onto the brake drum. What two problems does that leak create?
options: Wheel-seal leaks matter only when the tire is also flat
A leaking wheel seal is a defect, and the oil can contaminate the brake
Hub oil on the brake lengthens lining life and should be left
A wet hub means the seal was just packed and is ready for a long trip
questions.explanation: A leaking wheel seal is a defect by itself, and oil on the brake can contaminate the lining. Repair both concerns before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Lining on the drive brake is wet with hub oil, and the seal is clearly leaking. May you leave if you add oil to the hub?
options: Yes. A full hub window makes a leaking seal acceptable
Seal leaks are cosmetic and never reach the brake
No. Repair the leaking seal and the contaminated brake before the trip
Yes. The first stop wipes oil off the lining
questions.explanation: Adding oil does not fix a leaking wheel seal, and oil on the lining ruins the brake. Do not start the trip that way.
questions.remember: Oil on the brake lining? Don't go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Stationary checks are done and the truck has just begun to roll inside the yard. What brake test comes before the street?
options: Skip any moving test if the parking brake already held
Make the first brake test a hard stop from highway speed
Service brakes are tested only at the bottom of a mountain grade
Test the service brake at low speed before you enter traffic
questions.explanation: After you start to move, test the service brake at low speed before you enter traffic. Do not discover a brake problem in the street.
questions.remember: Roll slowly, then test the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why perform that low-speed service-brake test in the yard instead of on the public road?
options: So you find a pull or a weak stop before you enter traffic
The test is only a courtesy for the shipper watching the yard
A brake pull cannot show up at yard speed
The yard test is how you avoid inspecting hoses and chambers
questions.explanation: The low-speed test is where a pull or a failure to stop should show up, before you are in traffic and need the brake for real.
questions.remember: Truck pulls when braking? Brake trouble.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Left-front construction is bias ply and the right front is a radial. Is that an acceptable steer-axle pair?
options: Yes, if both tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread
Mixing matters only when the two tires are touching each other
No. Do not mismatch radial and bias tires on the same axle
Yes. The steer axle is the axle where mixing constructions is recommended
questions.explanation: Radial and bias tires do not belong on the same axle, including the steer axle. Match the construction before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Trailer duals rub each other as the sidewalls touch. What defect is that?
options: Rubbing sidewalls are how duals are supposed to share heat
Trailer duals may touch if the tractor duals do not
A rub mark only shows that the spacing is correct
Duals must not touch each other
questions.explanation: If dual sidewalls touch, the tires are not properly matched or spaced. They must not touch. Correct that before the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Even with legal steer-tire tread, a cut on the front tire shows fabric. Which defect controls?
options: Fabric showing means the tire is done, regardless of the remaining tread depth
Tread at or above 4/32 inch cancels a cut that shows fabric
Fabric showing is allowed on steer tires and banned only on trailers
A cut is legal until the tire is also losing air
questions.explanation: Cuts that show fabric finish a tire on any axle. Meeting the 4/32-inch tread minimum does not save a steer tire with fabric showing.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Two bulges appear, one on a steer tire and one on a trailer tire. How many of those tires are done?
options: Neither bulge counts if the tires still look round from across the yard
Both. A bulge means the tire is done on any axle
Only the steer-tire bulge counts
Only the trailer-tire bulge counts
questions.explanation: A bulge means the tire is done, whether it is a steer tire or a trailer tire. Both tires come off the trip until they are replaced.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Fluid at the power-steering reservoir is full, but the pump belt is loose and squealing. Is the full reservoir enough?
options: A squealing belt means the reservoir is overfilled
Loose belts tighten by themselves once the engine is fully warm
No. A belt that cannot reliably drive the pump has to be corrected before you go
Yes. Fluid level is the only power-steering item on a pre-trip
questions.explanation: A full reservoir does not fix a loose, squealing belt. Belts are repaired before the trip so the pump can actually turn.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Under the cab an air hose is swollen, and you can also hear a leak at the fitting. What is the combined message?
options: A swollen hose is acceptable when the leak is only loud enough to hear
Hearing a leak proves the compressor is strong enough for you to leave
Swelling is the look of a new hose that has not been used yet
Either finding keeps you parked: a swollen hose or a leak you can hear
questions.explanation: A hose that is swollen is a do-not-go item, and so is a leak you can hear. You do not need both defects to stay parked, but here you have both.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Several clearance lamps on the trailer are out. What has to be fixed before you leave?
options: Those required lamps, and any other required lights that do not work
Nothing, if the reflectors are clean
Only the headlights
Dark clearance lamps are legal in daylight on any trailer
questions.explanation: Required lights are part of the walk-around. Clearance lamps that are out get repaired before the trip, along with any other lamp that does not work.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Across the yard you cannot read the far gate because the windshield is filmed and the washer tank is empty. What belongs in this pre-trip?
options: Leave the film in place
Clean the glass and fill the washer
A filmed windshield is legal if both side windows roll down
Washers and wipers are equipment you need only at night
questions.explanation: Windshield and wipers are pre-trip items so you can see. Dirty glass and an empty washer system that leaves you blind are corrected before you roll. Clean the glass and make sure the wipers can keep the view clear before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: One of the three triangles in the rack is shattered. How many usable triangles do you have for the trip?
options: One usable triangle satisfies the emergency-equipment rule
Triangles are unnecessary when a charged extinguisher is on board
Not three. Replace the broken triangle so you have three reflective triangles
Three, because a shattered triangle still counts as a carried device
questions.explanation: You need three reflective triangles that can actually be used. A shattered one does not count. Replace it before you leave.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A full gauge sits on an extinguisher that is not the type required for this vehicle. Does the full gauge save it?
options: Yes. Any charged extinguisher meets every commercial vehicle
Yes. Needle position replaces the requirement that the type match the vehicle
Type matters only on a placarded load, and even then any can is fine
No. The extinguisher must be charged and appropriate to the vehicle
questions.explanation: Emergency equipment includes a charged extinguisher appropriate to the vehicle. A good gauge on the wrong type is still the wrong extinguisher.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Grease is on the fifth wheel, the jaws are locked, and the safety latch is seated, but you still see a gap under the apron. Which finding keeps you parked?
options: The gap. There should be no daylight between the trailer and the fifth wheel
The grease, because a greased fifth wheel will not hold a trailer
The locked jaws, which should stay open for the first mile
The seated latch, which blocks a legal coupling
questions.explanation: Grease, locked jaws, and a seated latch do not cancel a gap. No gap is allowed. Do not move until the trailer sits fully on the fifth wheel.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Lines and the electric cord are secured, but the landing gear is only halfway up. May you take the ramp onto the road?
options: Landing-gear height does not matter once the jaws are locked
No. Landing gear must be fully up before you move
Yes. Halfway up will catch the trailer if the fifth wheel lets go at speed
Yes, if the crank handle has been removed and left at the dock
questions.explanation: Secured lines do not replace landing gear that is fully up. Halfway up will hit the road or the tractor. Raise it completely before the ramp.
questions.why: Landing gear left part way down can catch on tracks or other things.
questions.remember: Landing gear all the way up.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: One broken leaf shows on a spring, while the shocks are dry and the U-bolts are tight. Which item is the defect?
options: The tight U-bolts, which should be left only finger-tight
None of those findings is a suspension defect
The broken spring leaf
The dry shocks
questions.explanation: Cracked or broken springs are defects even when the shocks are dry and the U-bolts are tight. Repair the spring before the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Two chambers tell different stories: one is inside its own stroke limit and the other is past the limit for its size. What is true?
options: If you invent a universal one-inch rule, the longer chamber is close enough to ignore
Only a steer-axle chamber has a stroke limit
Longer pushrod travel always means a stronger brake
The chamber past its own limit is out of adjustment and must be fixed
questions.explanation: Each chamber is judged by the travel limit for that chamber. One good brake does not excuse another brake that travels too far for its type. Do not apply one inch figure to both.
questions.remember: Pushrod past the limit? Something's wrong.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Gauges look normal and the parking brake holds, but the truck pulls during the low-speed service-brake check. Which result controls the decision to enter the street?
options: Do not enter traffic while the service brake pulls
A parking brake that holds cancels a service-brake pull
Normal oil pressure replaces the service-brake test
A pull is acceptable as soon as you leave yard speed
questions.explanation: The service brake must stop the vehicle and must not pull. Hold the truck until that pull is corrected, even if the other gauges look fine.
questions.remember: Truck pulls when braking? Brake trouble.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Welds look solid, but exhaust is leaking into the cab. Which defect still parks the truck?
options: An exhaust smell proves the cab seals are doing their job
The exhaust leak into the cab
Nothing, because the frame is the only structure that matters
Cab exhaust is acceptable whenever the welds are intact
questions.explanation: A solid weld does not clear exhaust in the cab. An exhaust leak into the cab means do not start the trip.
questions.why: A broken exhaust can let poison fumes into the cab or sleeper.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Straps and doors look secure, but one tarp corner is untied and snapping in the wind. What still has to be done?
options: Cut the tarp off so the loose corner cannot flap
Leave tarp ties for the consignee to finish
Tie that tarp corner before you roll
Nothing. Latched doors replace any need for a tarp
questions.explanation: Cargo securement includes tied tarps. Latched doors do not make a flapping corner acceptable. Tie it before you move.
questions.why: A flapping cover can tear loose and block your view or someone else's.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Lug nuts are dry, tight, and free of rust streaks, but a wheel seal weeps oil onto the drum. Tread on that tire is legal. What still fails?
options: Legal tread cancels a wheel-seal leak
Tight lug nuts prove the seal is healthy
Oil on a drum is the normal way a brake stays cool
The leaking wheel seal
questions.explanation: Tight lugs and legal tread do not fix a leaking wheel seal. The leak is a defect, and oil on the drum can ruin the brake lining.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before the truck has moved, oil pressure is up, the system is charging, air is at cut-out, and the low-air warning works. What moving test is still ahead?
options: A low-speed service brake test
No moving test is required once those gauges look normal
The next test is a high-speed stop on the public road
Skip the brakes and test only the horn while you roll
questions.explanation: Good stationary readings do not replace the low-speed service-brake test. Do that test after you start to move and before you enter traffic.
questions.remember: Roll slowly, then test the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Everything else looks fine, but steering play on the 20-inch wheel is far past about two inches at the rim. What still holds you in the yard?
options: Play like that is corrected by driving with a lighter grip
Excessive steering play, more than about 10 degrees, must be repaired before the trip
A clean walk-around of the tires cancels excessive steering play
About two inches of rim movement is the least play a 20-inch wheel must have
questions.explanation: More than about two inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel is more than about 10 degrees of play. That excess is repaired before the trip.
questions.why: Too much steering wheel play can make it hard to steer.
questions.remember: Loose steering wheel? Get it fixed.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Side by side you have a drive tire at 3/32 inch and a steer tire at 3/32 inch. Which tire fails its tread rule?
options: Neither tire fails
Only the drive tire fails
The steer tire
Both tires fail
questions.explanation: Steering-axle tires need at least 4/32 inch, so 3/32 inch fails the steer tire. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch, so the drive tire at 3/32 inch still meets its tread floor.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Regrooved rubber sits on the left front, and a sound radial with legal tread sits on the right front. What do you change?
options: Remove the sound radial
Nothing. Regrooving is the recommended repair for a steer tire
Move the regrooved tire to the other front so the two fronts match
Remove the regrooved tire from the front
questions.explanation: The model manual says not to use regrooved tires on the front wheels. Matching the other front to a regroove would make the axle worse, not legal.

questions.q: Properly checked lug nuts will not budge after you noticed rust streaks on that wheel. What did the streaks require you to do?
options: Check the nuts
Remove the wheel anyway
Ignore streaks, because only chipped paint, never rust, can mean a loose nut
Loosen every nut one turn so the rust can flake off
questions.explanation: Rust streaks from lug nuts can mean they are loose, so you check them. A proper check that finds them tight is the point of looking, not a reason to back the nuts off.
questions.remember: Rust at a lug nut? Check it's tight.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Horn and belts check out, but a power-steering hose is cut. Which defect controls whether you leave?
options: Cut hoses seal themselves once system pressure comes up
The cut hose
A working horn means a fluid hose can wait until the next shop
A good belt takes the place of a cut power-steering hose
questions.explanation: A hose that is cut means do not go. A working horn and a good belt do not carry fluid to the steering gear.
questions.remember: Power steering: fluid full, hoses sound.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: You verify this tractor uses circuit breakers and does not use fuses, and there is no spare-fuse kit. Which statement is right?
options: Circuit breakers must be removed and replaced with fuses before any trip
Breakers remove the need to inspect lights and the fire extinguisher
Spare fuses are the requirement for a vehicle that uses fuses
The truck stays parked until a spare-fuse kit is added anyway
questions.explanation: Confirm spare fuses if the vehicle uses fuses. A breaker-equipped tractor is not failed only for lacking spare fuses. You still check lights and the extinguisher. An automatic defect on this breaker-equipped truck.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Coupling looks complete except the electric cord, which is still unplugged. Jaws are locked, there is no gap, the latch is on, and the fifth wheel is greased. What do you fix?
options: Nothing else. Locked jaws power the trailer lamps
Unplug the air lines so they match the hanging cord
Grease the cord and leave it hanging beside the frame
Connect and secure the electric cord before you move
questions.explanation: Air lines and the electric cord both have to be secure and connected. A good fifth-wheel lock does not turn the trailer lights on.
questions.remember: Cord plugged in, safety catch on.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Three suspension problems share one axle: a leaking shock, a cracked spring, and a loose U-bolt. What is the repair standard?
options: All three are suspension defects
Only the leaking shock has to be repaired
Only the cracked spring has to be repaired
A loose U-bolt is normal beside a cracked spring, so leave all three
questions.explanation: Cracked springs, loose U-bolts, and leaking shocks are all defects. Finding them together does not let you pick just one. Repair the axle before you go.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Cut-out is reached, but the low-air warning never sounds when you test it. Is reaching cut-out enough?
options: A warning that does not sound can be signed off if the gauge needle moves
No. The low-air warning has to work, not only the ability to reach cut-out
Yes. Building to cut-out proves every air warning on the truck
Yes. The warning is supposed to stay silent or the system is faulty
questions.explanation: Air building to cut-out and a working low-air warning are separate in-cab checks. You need both before the trip.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Oil pressure is up, but the charging gauge stays on discharge. May you treat the oil reading as proof the electrical system is fine?
options: Yes. A discharge reading means the batteries are full
Charging is something you check only after the first hour on the road
No. The charging system is a separate check, and this one is not charging
Yes. Oil pressure and the charging system share one gauge
questions.explanation: Oil pressure coming up does not mean the alternator is charging. If the charging gauge stays on discharge, do not start the trip.
questions.remember: Charging gauge in the normal range.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The yard test stops the truck straight, but the parking brake will not hold on a gentle pull-away. Which brake fails the pre-trip?
options: The service brake
Neither brake. Parking brakes are allowed to roll a little
Both brakes, because stopping straight is itself a defect
The parking brake
questions.explanation: A service brake that stops the truck straight does not excuse a parking brake that will not hold. The parking brake must hold before you leave.
questions.remember: Test the parking brake: low gear, gentle pull.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The engine sounds smooth, but you can see both a frame crack and a broken weld. What is the trip decision?
options: Do not start the trip
A smooth-running engine clears structural damage
Broken welds are acceptable if the crack is on a different rail
Frame damage is a cargo problem
questions.explanation: Frame cracks and broken welds mean do not start the trip. How smoothly the engine runs does not repair the frame.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The gate to the street is ahead, the walk-around is done, and the gauges came up normally as soon as you started to roll in the yard. What do you do before that gate?
options: Rely on the gauge check and skip a moving brake test
Set the parking brake while the truck is already rolling toward the gate
Test the service brake at low speed
Accelerate to highway speed and try the brakes in the first gap in traffic
questions.explanation: After you start to move, test the service brake at low speed before you enter traffic. A normal gauge sweep is not that test.
questions.remember: Roll slowly, then test the brakes.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Before the truck moves, when is the first federal cargo inspection required?
options: Only after the first 50 miles
Only at the receiver, once the doors are already open
Only if a trooper is sitting at the scale house
Before you drive
questions.explanation: 49 CFR 392.9 requires a cargo inspection before the vehicle is driven. The check within the first 50 miles is the next inspection, not a substitute for the one you do before you roll. After you have already covered the first 50 miles.
questions.remember: Check the load before you drive.

questions.q: You inspected the load in the yard and have now driven 30 miles. What securement check comes next?
options: Inspect again before 50 miles
Skip every recheck until you have driven 150 miles
Wait until the calendar day changes, then look once
Recheck only if a shipper calls and asks you to
questions.explanation: The within-50-miles inspection is mandatory after you start. It is how you catch a strap or chain that loosens once the load settles. Do not postpone it to the later 3-hour or 150-mile interval. Inspect again before you pass the first 50 miles, even though the yard check was fine.
questions.remember: Check the load early in the trip.

questions.q: After the early-miles cargo check, which interval matches the federal reinspection rule?
options: Only when you stop for fuel, and only if the tarp looks new
Every 3 hours or 150 miles, and at duty changes
Every 100 miles, and never
Once every 8 hours of driving, with no mileage test
questions.explanation: After the pre-trip and the inspection inside the first 50 miles, recheck at every change of duty status and every 3 hours or 150 miles, whichever comes first. A 100-mile habit is not the rule.
questions.remember: Recheck the load as you go.

questions.q: A dispatcher tells you cargo checks can wait until 100 miles. What is wrong with that plan?
options: Mileage never matters, and only a 10-hour break triggers a cargo check
Federal rules drop all cargo checks once the trailer is past the yard
The interval is 3 hours or 150 miles
One hundred miles is shorter than the legal interval
questions.explanation: Do not replace the rule with a 100-mile shortcut. Inspect before you drive, again within 50 miles, then every 3 hours or 150 miles, whichever comes first, and at every change of duty status.
questions.remember: Recheck the load as you go.

questions.q: You switch from driving to on-duty unloading at the dock. What cargo duty goes with that change?
options: Skip inspection because a duty-status change pauses the securement rules
Inspect only the tractor oil and ignore the freight
Open the doors wide first and look after the freight falls
Inspect the cargo and its securement at the change of duty status
questions.explanation: A change of duty status is a required inspection point. Look at the load and the devices that hold it before you continue, and fix anything that has shifted.
questions.remember: Recheck the load as you go.

questions.q: At mile 40 a winch strap that was tight in the yard is hanging slack. What should you do?
options: Stop and tighten or repair that securement before you drive any farther
Leave it until mile 150
Cut the strap off and finish the trip with one less tiedown
Tie the loose end to the door latch and keep rolling
questions.explanation: The inspection inside the first 50 miles exists to catch exactly this. A loose winch is not secure. Stop, retighten or replace it, and do not use the door latch as a tiedown.
questions.remember: Loose strap? Fix it right away.

questions.q: The first 50 miles are done and every strap still looks tight. May you skip checks until the consignee?
options: Yes, whenever the trailer is a van instead of a flatbed
No. Keep checking every 3 hours or 150 miles
Yes. A clean 50-mile check ends cargo inspections for that trip
Yes, if the bill of lading says the shipper already counted the straps
questions.explanation: Passing the early check does not retire the rule. Securement can loosen later from vibration, braking, and grades. Recheck on the 3-hour or 150-mile rhythm and whenever your duty status changes. No. Keep rechecking every 3 hours or 150 miles, whichever comes first, and at each duty-status change.
questions.remember: Recheck the load as you go.

questions.q: Which sequence is the complete cargo-inspection rhythm for a property-carrying trip?
options: Every 100 miles, with the first look allowed to wait until mile 50
Only at midnight
Before, within 50 miles, then every 3 hrs/150 mi
Yard only, then nothing until the receiver breaks the seal for you
questions.explanation: Inspect before you move. Do the next look within the first 50 miles, not instead of the first look. After that, use 3 hours or 150 miles, whichever comes first, and inspect again at every change of duty status.
questions.remember: Check the load early in the trip.

questions.q: Where should the heaviest freight sit in a dry van so the rig handles and the load stays put?
options: As high as the roof bows allow, centered over the rear doors
All on the left wall so the trailer leans a little
Against the doors, with the light cartons used as a cushion up front
Low, near center, blocked from sliding
questions.explanation: Keep heavy cargo low and near the center, usually a bit forward of the trailer center so a headerboard or other blocking can stop it from sliding forward. High stacks raise the center of gravity.
questions.why: Cargo piled high makes you more likely to tip over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why is it a mistake to stack the heaviest pallets on the top layer of a van load?
options: The high center of gravity makes a rollover more likely in a curve or a sudden swerve
Top weight presses the steering axle down and always improves control
Height does not matter if the gross weight is legal
Top-heavy freight shortens stopping distance on dry pavement
questions.explanation: Weight up high makes the combination easier to roll. Put the heavy pieces low, keep the load centered, and block it so it cannot walk forward or sideways.
questions.why: Cargo piled high makes you more likely to tip over.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: The shipper wants the heaviest crates jammed against the rear doors. Why should you refuse that placement?
options: Rear placement is the only way to keep axle weights legal
It can lighten the steer axle and fall out
Rear weight is required so the trailer tandems can be left unbraked
Door-area freight is safer
questions.explanation: Weight too far back lightens the steering axle, so the truck wanders and is hard to steer. Freight stacked on the doors can also fall out the moment those doors swing open.
questions.why: Too little weight on the front axle makes steering unsafe.
questions.remember: Too light up front: hard to steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Too little weight on the steering axle shows up as which handling problem?
options: The service brakes on the trailer stop working
The truck tracks better at highway speed than a balanced load would
The truck wanders and is hard to steer
The steering axle becomes exempt from bridge postings
questions.explanation: The front axle needs enough weight to steer. A light nose wanders and feels vague. Too much weight on that axle is a separate overweight problem. Balance the load. The front tires lack grip.
questions.why: Too little weight on the front axle makes steering unsafe.
questions.remember: Too light up front: hard to steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Your gross weight is under the combination limit, but one axle is over its rating. What is true?
options: Only the gross weight is enforced
An overweight axle is legal if the extra sits slightly left of center
Bridge crews ignore axle weights whenever the registration is current
That axle is an overweight violation even though the gross looks legal
questions.explanation: Know both the gross and each axle. An axle can be illegal by itself. Sliding the trailer tandems or moving freight may be required before you roll.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: How does overloading the combination change braking compared with a legal, balanced load?
options: Stopping distances get longer
Stopping distances get shorter
Only the trailer brakes are affected, and the tractor stops in the same distance
Overload has no braking effect if you shift to a higher gear
questions.explanation: Extra weight takes longer to stop. It can also overload an axle or, if it sits too far back, lighten the steering axle. Do not leave with a load you have not weighed. The brakes and tires are working beyond the load they were set up to handle.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Freight placed too far to the rear of the trailer can do what to the steering axle?
options: Lock the steer tires so they cannot be turned
Lighten it, so the front end wanders and steering grip falls off
Always overload it, no matter how long the trailer is
Remove it from bridge laws
questions.explanation: Weight behind the center can unload the steering axle. Too little front weight makes the truck wander and hard to steer. It can also overload the axles farther back.
questions.why: Too little weight on the front axle makes steering unsafe.
questions.remember: Too light up front: hard to steer.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A nose-heavy load piled against the bulkhead can create which axle problem?
options: It makes an overweight steering axle legal on a posted bridge
It cancels the need to block the freight against forward movement
It can overload the steering axle even when the trailer tandems still look light
It removes all weight from the steering axle
questions.explanation: Too far forward overloads the steering axle. Too far back lightens it. Either mistake is a handling problem, an axle-weight problem, or both.
questions.remember: Too heavy up front: hard steering.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Why do you need the gross weight and each axle weight before you leave a loaded dock?
options: Only the shipper's estimated piece count matters to enforcement
Axle readings are optional if the trailer is sealed
Gross weight is used only for fuel tax
An axle can be illegal even if gross is fine
questions.explanation: Know the gross and the axle weights. Bridges, registrations, and handling all depend on where the weight sits, not only on the total. An axle can be illegal, or the steering axle can be too light, even when the gross number looks acceptable.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Empty pallets on an open trailer can blow off in a crosswind. What does the cargo rule require?
options: Cover or contain them so nothing can leave the vehicle
Stack them above the side rails and rely on gravity
Leave them loose so they can shift into a tighter pile
Hold them with the door latch alone
questions.explanation: Cargo that can blow or fall off must be covered or contained. Gravity and a hopeful stack are not securement.
questions.remember: Nothing leaks, spills, blows or falls.

questions.q: Sand is leaking from a dump body onto the roadway. What is the required fix before you continue?
options: Call the leak legal
Contain or cover the load so it cannot leak, spill, or blow off
Drive faster so the leak spreads out and becomes less noticeable
Ignore it if the leak is only on the right side
questions.explanation: Cargo that can blow or leak must be covered or contained. A trail of sand is unsecured cargo, not a normal operating condition.
questions.remember: Nothing leaks, spills, blows or falls.

questions.q: Are light cartons on an open deck secure if they have not moved while you were parked?
options: Yes, whenever the cartons weigh less than the trailer
Yes, if you promise to stop only on straight roads
No. It must be covered and tied down
Yes. If it sits still in the yard it will sit still at highway speed
questions.explanation: Wind and stops will move freight that parking-lot calm did not. Cover or contain anything that can blow or fall, and use real tiedowns.
questions.remember: Nothing leaks, spills, blows or falls.

questions.q: After you reblock a shifted load, what securement step is still required before you roll?
options: Skip the next 50-mile inspection
Tighten tiedowns so nothing can slide
Leave the binders open so the load can settle on the road
Hook one strap to the door latch and call the job finished
questions.explanation: Blocking without tight tiedowns is incomplete. Tiedowns must be tight before you move, and they go back on the normal inspection schedule after you start. Tighten the tiedowns and confirm the freight cannot slide forward, back, or sideways.
questions.remember: Cargo secured so it can't shift or fall.

questions.q: Why does a half-full tanker surge more than the same tank filled completely?
options: Surge only happens when the tank is completely full
A half-full tank cannot surge if the driver brakes in a straight line
The partial load has open space to move
A full tank has more free surface and therefore surges harder
questions.explanation: A partial liquid load surges more than a full one because the liquid has room to travel. Brake and steer smoothly, and leave extra space. The liquid wave is larger.
questions.why: Liquid moving in a part-full tank pushes the truck.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: What do baffles actually do inside a cargo tank?
options: They cancel all surge, including forward and backward waves
They are only noise insulation and do not affect liquid movement
They let you brake as hard as you would with a dry van
They reduce front-to-back surge, but side-to-side surge remains
questions.explanation: Baffles slow the forward and backward surge. Side-to-side surge can still occur and can cause a rollover, and a partial load still does not behave like boxed freight. Smooth inputs still matter.
questions.why: Baffles slow front-to-back surge; side-to-side surge can still happen.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: How should you brake and steer a tank that is only partly filled?
options: Smoothly, and earlier than you would with a solid load
With a hard stab brake so the wave stacks at the front and then disappears
In neutral, so the liquid cannot climb the tank ends
At the same following distance you use in an empty straight truck
questions.explanation: Liquid keeps moving after the vehicle starts to stop or turn. A partial load is worse than a full one. Smooth braking and smooth steering are the control you have. Surge keeps pushing after you change speed or direction.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A smooth-bore tank has no baffles and is loaded about halfway. Which driving choice fits that cargo?
options: Rely on the missing baffles
Slow earlier and steer gently against surge
Accelerate into turns so centrifugal force pins the liquid flat
Treat it as safer than a full tank
questions.explanation: No baffles plus a partial load is the strongest surge case in ordinary cargo work. Ease off the throttle early and do not make sharp steering or braking moves. Start slowing earlier and make gentle steering inputs so the wave does not shove the vehicle.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which statement about tank surge is accurate for a general cargo driver?
options: Surge is a forward-only event and never affects a lane change
A full tank surges more than any partial load
A partial load surges more, and baffles cut only front-to-back surge
Baffles remove surge completely, so following distance can shrink
questions.explanation: Leave room for the liquid to keep moving after you brake or turn. Baffles help control forward and backward movement only; side-to-side surge can still occur.
questions.why: Baffles slow front-to-back surge; side-to-side surge can still happen.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A 10-foot crate is not blocked or braced against forward movement. What is the minimum tiedown count?
options: One tiedown, because the crate is exactly 10 feet
One tiedown for every 20 feet, so this crate needs none yet
No tiedowns if the crate is heavier than 1,100 pounds
At least two tiedowns
questions.explanation: A 10-foot article that is not blocked against forward movement needs at least two tiedowns. Longer unblocked pieces add one for each extra 10 feet or fraction. Do not secure it with one.

questions.q: A 4-foot crate sits tight against a headerboard that blocks forward movement. What can satisfy the tiedown count?
options: One tiedown can be enough for that short blocked piece if the working load limit is also met
Four tiedowns, because every foot of a blocked piece needs its own strap
Zero tiedowns, because the headerboard replaces every tiedown
One wrap around the door latch and nothing else
questions.explanation: Cargo actually blocked against forward movement by a headerboard, bulkhead, or other cargo needs one tiedown for every 10 feet of length or fraction, so this 4-foot crate can use one. The aggregate working load limit must still be at least half the cargo weight.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: A 12-foot crate is not blocked against forward movement. Which tiedown decision follows the working rule?
options: Hook a single chain to the door latch and call the length covered
At least three: two for the first 10 feet, plus one more
Use one tiedown
Use no tiedowns if the crate is wedged between empty pallets that do not actually brace it
questions.explanation: Cargo that is not blocked forward and is longer than 10 feet needs two tiedowns for the first 10 feet plus one more for each additional 10 feet or fraction. Twelve feet is 10 plus a fraction, so the minimum is three. Do not treat a nearby gap as blocking.

questions.q: An unblocked article is longer than 10 feet. How do you keep the count from becoming a false one-per-ten slogan?
options: Drop a tiedown for every 10 feet once the article weighs more than the trailer
Count only the first 10 feet and ignore the rest of the length
Two for the first 10 feet, plus one per extra 10 feet or fraction
Use one tiedown no matter how long the article is, if a headerboard is somewhere on the trailer
questions.explanation: For cargo not blocked forward and longer than 10 feet, the rule is two tiedowns for the first 10 feet plus one for each additional 10 feet or fraction. A simple one-per-ten count undercounts these pieces.

questions.q: A 20-foot beam is not blocked against forward movement. What is the minimum tiedown count?
options: One tiedown in the middle
Five tiedowns, one for every 4 feet, even if the beam is blocked
At least two tiedowns
At least three tiedowns
questions.explanation: Unblocked cargo longer than 10 feet needs two tiedowns for the first 10 feet plus one for each additional 10 feet or fraction. Twenty feet is 10 plus 10, so the minimum is three. Still meet the working load limit.

questions.q: A 25-foot unblocked piece of pipe is on the deck. What tiedown count does the working rule require at minimum?
options: At least four: two for the first 10 feet, plus two more
One, because pipe is round and length rules do not apply
Three, one for each 10 feet or fraction
Zero if the pipe is nested inside a groove and not otherwise braced forward
questions.explanation: Unblocked cargo needs two tiedowns for the first 10 feet, plus one for each additional 10 feet or fraction. The remaining 15 feet is one full unit plus a fraction, so add two: four in all. A groove that does not block forward movement does not change the count.

questions.q: Other freight is supposed to block a 4-foot carton against forward movement. When does that blocking count?
options: Blocking never changes a tiedown count, even when the carton is tight against a bulkhead
Only when the carton is actually against that freight or another real brace, so one tiedown can then be enough
Whenever the other freight is anywhere in the same trailer
Only if the other freight is behind the carton
questions.explanation: Forward blocking counts when a headerboard, bulkhead, or other cargo actually stops the article from sliding forward. A short piece blocked that way can use one tiedown. Air space in front means it is not blocked.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: The headerboard is solid, but the crates start two feet behind it. Does the headerboard lower the tiedown count?
options: Yes. A gap of two feet is still treated as full contact
Yes, but only if you also hook a strap to the door latch
No. It blocks forward movement only if the cargo is actually against it
Yes. Any headerboard on the trailer halves the tiedown count for every piece
questions.explanation: A headerboard helps forward movement only when the cargo bears on it. If the load is not against it, treat the article as not blocked and use the unblocked tiedown count, including at least two on a 10-foot piece.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: An 8-foot machine is not blocked against forward movement. How many tiedowns are the minimum?
options: One, because it is shorter than 10 feet
Eight, one for each foot of length
None, because machines are restrained by their own weight
At least two
questions.explanation: Shorter than 10 feet does not mean one tiedown when the article is not blocked forward. An unblocked piece longer than 5 feet and up to 10 feet needs at least two. One tiedown is allowed only for a blocked piece, or an unblocked piece of 5 feet or less weighing 1,100 pounds or less.

questions.q: Why is the sentence 'one tiedown is enough for any 10-foot piece' false?
options: A 10-foot piece that is not blocked against forward movement needs at least two tiedowns
Ten-foot pieces are illegal to haul on a flatbed
One tiedown is enough only when the piece is unblocked and exactly 10 feet
The count depends only on the color of the strap
questions.explanation: Do not collapse the rule to one tiedown per piece. Unblocked freight longer than 5 feet needs at least two, and a 10-foot unblocked article is the example that still needs two, not one.

questions.q: How does a 4-foot blocked crate differ from a 10-foot crate that is not blocked forward?
options: Blocking adds tiedowns
The short blocked crate can use one tiedown
Both always need four tiedowns regardless of blocking
The unblocked 10-foot crate can use one, and the blocked crate needs five
questions.explanation: Blocking changes the count. Blocked cargo needs one tiedown per 10 feet or fraction, so the 4-foot crate can use one. A 10-foot piece that is not blocked needs at least two. Meet the working load limit either way.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: A 9-foot crate is tight against the bulkhead, so forward movement is blocked. How many tiedowns does that length need?
options: Nine, one tiedown per foot
Zero, because bulkhead contact replaces tiedowns completely
One, because blocked cargo needs one per 10 feet or fraction
Two, because it is longer than 5 feet
questions.explanation: When an article is blocked against forward movement, it needs at least one tiedown for every 10 feet of length or fraction. Nine feet is one unit, so one tiedown satisfies the count if strength is also met. The more-than-5-feet-needs-two rule applies only to cargo that is not blocked.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: A blocked article is 12 feet long and is tight against a headerboard. What tiedown count applies?
options: One, because blocking freezes the count at a single tiedown for any length
Twelve, because each foot must have its own chain
Three, two for the first 10 feet plus one more
Two, one for each 10 feet or fraction
questions.explanation: Blocked cargo needs one tiedown for every 10 feet of length or fraction. Twelve feet is one full unit plus a fraction, so the minimum is two. Two-plus-one-per-ten is the rule for cargo that is not blocked.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: A 22-foot crate is braced against the bulkhead so it cannot slide forward. What is the minimum tiedown count?
options: Three, one for each 10 feet or fraction
Two, because blocked freight never needs more than a pair of straps
One, because the bulkhead is doing all of the work
Four, two for the first 10 feet plus two more
questions.explanation: Blocked cargo needs one tiedown for every 10 feet of length or fraction. Twenty-two feet is two full units plus a fraction, so the minimum is three.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: What is the aggregate working load limit the tiedowns must provide for an article?
options: A limit printed on the bill of lading, with no relation to cargo weight
At least half the weight of that cargo
At least the full weight of the cargo, doubled again for wet roads
At least one quarter of the cargo weight if the trailer has sides
questions.explanation: Add up the working load limits of the tiedowns. That total must be at least half the weight of the article or group they secure. The count of tiedowns does not replace this strength rule.
questions.remember: Tiedowns hold at least half the weight.

questions.q: Which part sets the working load limit of a single tiedown assembly?
options: Only the winch handle, regardless of a cracked hook
The door latch, if that is where the driver prefers to hook it
The weakest part in the assembly, such as the strap, chain, hook, or anchor
The strongest part
questions.explanation: A tiedown is only as strong as its weakest component. A heavy chain with a light hook is limited by the hook. Anchors count too. Do not rate the assembly by its best piece.
questions.remember: A tiedown is as strong as its weakest part.

questions.q: The chain is rated far above the load, but the grab hook on that chain is a much lower rating. Which rating do you use?
options: The chain's higher rating
An average of the chain and the hook
Zero, so the tiedown cannot be counted, and you may substitute the door latch
The hook's lower rating
questions.explanation: If the hook fails, the chain's rating never gets used. The working load limit of the tiedown is the lowest rated part in the path, including the anchor. The weakest component sets the tiedown's limit.
questions.remember: A tiedown is as strong as its weakest part.

questions.q: You have enough tiedowns to meet the count, but their combined working load limit is under half the cargo weight. Is the load legal to move?
options: No. Total WLL must be at least half the weight
Yes. The count rule replaces the strength rule
Yes, if you twist each strap so it looks tighter
Yes, if the shortfall is only on the rear half of the deck
questions.explanation: Number and strength are both required. Meeting the count with weak straps does not satisfy the rule that the aggregate working load limit be at least half the weight of the cargo.
questions.remember: Tiedowns hold at least half the weight.

questions.q: When must tiedowns be tight, and when must they be looked at again?
options: Tightened once a week, regardless of the trip
Before moving, within 50 miles, then on schedule
Tight only at the receiver
Rechecked every 100 miles, with the first check allowed to wait until mile 50
questions.explanation: A loose tiedown is not doing its job. Tension them before you roll, catch settlement inside 50 miles, and keep using the federal reinspection rhythm. Do not invent a 100-mile interval. Tight before you move, then rechecked before the first 50 miles end, and later on the 3-hour or 150-mile schedule and at duty-status changes.
questions.remember: Check the load early in the trip.

questions.q: You find an open binder on a chain that is supposed to be holding a coil. What does that mean?
options: Leave it open so the chain can stretch without snapping
Wire it open and hook the free end to the door latch
The tiedown is not secure
An open binder is the normal traveling position for chains
questions.explanation: An open binder cannot hold the load. Secure it, then recheck on the cargo schedule. A binder left open is the same class of problem as a loose winch. Close and tension the binder before the truck moves.

questions.q: A strap runs over a sharp steel edge with no protection and is already scuffed. Is that securement acceptable?
options: Yes, if the strap's tag still shows a high working load limit
Yes, whenever the edge is on the cargo rather than on the trailer
Yes, if you add a second strap that also crosses the same bare edge
No. Unprotected edges can cut the strap
questions.explanation: Protect straps from abrasion and cutting. An unprotected sharp edge means that tiedown cannot be trusted. Edge protection does not replace the required number of tiedowns, but missing protection ruins the ones you have. No. A strap over a sharp edge without protection is not secure and can be cut when the load shifts.

questions.q: A winch is still loose when you finish the pre-trip. What is the right next step?
options: Tighten it, or replace the assembly, before you move the truck
Start the trip and let road vibration set the winch
Remove the strap and rely on the headerboard even though the cargo does not touch it
Count the loose winch toward the tiedown number anyway
questions.explanation: Tiedowns must be tight before you move. A loose winch is not a tiedown you can count. The within-50-miles check is for settlement after a tight start, not permission to leave loose.

questions.q: Mile marker 40 is where you notice a strap that was tight at the dock has worked loose. Which response is correct?
options: Tighten it with the door latch as the new anchor
Ignore it because the first cargo check is not due until 50 miles have already been completed without stopping
Stop there and retighten it
Note it in the log and fix it only if it is still loose at mile 150
questions.explanation: You must inspect within the first 50 miles, and a strap that has already loosened at mile 40 is a defect now. Stop and fix it. The first inspection was due before you drove; this is the follow-up, not the first look. Do not wait for a 150-mile mark or a 100-mile habit.
questions.remember: Loose strap? Fix it right away.

questions.q: Block and brace must stop cargo from sliding in which directions?
options: Forward only, because rearward and sideways movement are harmless
Only sideways, because tiedowns already cover the length of the trailer
Whichever direction is downhill when you happen to park
Forward, backward, and sideways
questions.explanation: Cargo has to be prevented from moving forward, back, or to either side. A headerboard covers forward movement only when the freight is actually against it. Bracing and tiedowns still have to cover the other directions.

questions.q: Rear blocking is tight, but nothing is in front of the pallets and they do not touch the headerboard. What movement is still free?
options: Forward, and sideways if unbraced
No movement, because rear blocking locks every direction
Only upward movement, which tiedowns cannot address
Only movement inside the cab
questions.explanation: Blocking must match the direction. A brace behind the load does not stop it from walking forward into the doors or the tractor. Put the freight against a headerboard or use another real forward block, and brace the sides too. Forward movement, and sideways movement if you also have not braced the sides.

questions.q: A sealed trailer still has to be checked in what way?
options: Inspect only the seal number and ignore a dragging strap
Check what you can see without breaking it
Break the seal and unload enough freight to see the nose of the trailer
Do nothing at all
questions.explanation: You do not break a seal just to rummage through the freight. You still inspect everything you can see, including leaks, lights, tires, locks, and any securement device that is visible.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A sealed trailer is leaning hard to one side in the yard. What should you do?
options: Break the seal, climb inside, and rebuild the load yourself on the street
Add a strap to the door latch and go
Do not ignore the lean
Leave immediately, because a seal means the lean is the shipper's secret
questions.explanation: A leaning trailer can mean the cargo has already shifted. A seal limits rummaging; it does not let you haul an obvious unsafe condition. Get the problem fixed before you move. Have the shift corrected before you drive, without treating the seal as a reason to look away.
questions.why: An off-center load that makes the trailer lean makes a rollover more likely.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A strap is dragging on the pavement under a sealed trailer. What is required?
options: Keep going, because you would have to break the seal to touch any strap
Drag it until the next 100-mile mark
Tie the dragging end to the door latch and leave it low
Stop and secure or remove the dragging strap
questions.explanation: You do not break a seal to dig through the load, but a dragging strap is something you can see and it is not secure. Stop and fix it before it snaps or takes out another vehicle. A seal is not permission to ignore it.
questions.remember: Everything that holds the load secured.

questions.q: What is the limit of the idea that you should not break a shipper's seal?
options: You still refuse any hazard you can see
The seal cancels axle-weight limits and bridge postings
The seal means loose cab cargo is acceptable
The seal moves the first cargo inspection out to mile 50
questions.explanation: Sealed freight still gets every check you can make from outside. Do not break the seal to rearrange the load, and do not drive a combination that is visibly unsafe. You do not break it to rummage, but you still refuse a leaning trailer, a leak, or any other hazard you can see.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: A loaded van's cargo has shifted enough that the trailer now pulls to one side. What is the safe choice?
options: Increase speed so the sway averages out
Add a door-latch strap and leave the freight where it slid
Wait until 100 miles have passed before you look
Stop and correct the shift first
questions.explanation: A shift that changes handling means the cargo is not secured. Park and fix the blocking and tiedowns. Do not wait for a made-up 100-mile interval. Stop and correct the shift before you continue, even if that means a delay at the next safe place.
questions.remember: Recheck the load as you go.

questions.q: You are about to accept a flatbed load and you do not know the weight. What should you do before you roll?
options: Get gross and axle weights first
Leave and weigh only if a scale house pulls you in
Estimate by how the fifth wheel feels and skip the scale
Ask the guard to pick a tandem hole at random
questions.explanation: Guessing axle weights is how drivers arrive overweight or with a wandering front end. Weigh the combination and adjust freight or tandem position before the trip. Get the gross weight and the axle weights, then place or slide the load so no axle is illegal and the steer axle is not too light.
questions.remember: Know the weight before you take it.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Cargo that can blow off must also not do which of these things while it is being contained?
options: It may be uncovered if the wind is from behind
It must not leak, spill, or fall onto the road
It may leak a little if the cover is only cosmetic
It may fall off on curves as long as the straight sections stay clean
questions.explanation: Covering is not a decoration. The method you use has to keep the cargo from blowing, leaking, or falling off the vehicle. The cover or container has to actually hold it.
questions.remember: Nothing leaks, spills, blows or falls.

questions.q: A tarp is on the load but several tarp straps are undone and the cover is ballooning. What is wrong?
options: Tarp straps are optional once the tarp is thrown over the freight
The door latch can be the only hold-down for the tarp
The cargo is not contained
A ballooning tarp is acceptable
questions.explanation: A cover that is not fastened is not a cover. Cargo that can blow away has to be contained, and the tiedowns or tarp hardware have to be tight before you move. Secure the cover so it cannot tear loose or let freight escape.

provenance.manual: AAMVA Commercial Driver's License Manual (2025 CDL Testing System)

questions.q: Which loading choice best keeps a heavy crate from sliding forward in a panic stop?
options: Set it just inside the rear doors so the doors stop it
Set it on top of lighter freight with no blocking
Leave a two-foot gap in front of it and call the headerboard a brace anyway
Against a real forward block, tied down
questions.explanation: Forward blocking works only when the cargo is against it. Slightly forward of center is a common placement so the block can do its job without unloading the steering axle or overloading it. Place it against a headerboard or other real forward block, slightly ahead of the trailer center if that still balances the axles, and tie it down.
questions.remember: Blocked in front? Fewer tiedowns needed.

questions.q: Side-to-side, the freight sits entirely on the left half of the trailer. What problem does that create?
options: The trailer leans and rolls more easily
A left-side stack is the preferred way to load for crosswinds
Side placement does not matter if a headerboard is installed
